Original FreeCell homebrew for monochrome and colour WonderSwan, with WonderWitch executable support. src/card.c implements deck shuffling, cascades/free cells/foundations, legal-move checks and win logic; this is substantive native game source.

Original Game Boy incremental/idle game source published by its creator after a competition prototype and commercial expansion. Gameplay uses console-model detection, SRAM progression and two-player link-cable cooperation; substantial game code is in gbcorp.c.

Original Photo! native camera application/ROM that expands Game Boy Camera sensor control, capture, printing, remote control, gallery and flash-storage workflows, with Game Boy/Color and adapter-based Mega Duck/Game Gear variants. Actual exposure/capture-state implementation is present.

Original Pat Morita Team platform-action game source with player physics, combat, energy, bombs, checkpoints, multiple game states and level assets. Current CrossZGB makefile declares native Game Boy, Mega Duck, Game Gear and Master System builds.

Original GB Compo 2021 game about grappling through a city to collect and deliver sushi. Concrete native gameplay includes hook collision/rope rendering and swing interaction; current CrossZGB source builds address Game Boy, Mega Duck, Game Gear and Master System.

Small substantive native Game Boy preemptive round-robin scheduler implementation and demonstration. Timer ISR saves task registers/stack pointer, advances a task-control-block ring and restores the next stack; it is more than a scheduling concept or prose tutorial.

Implemented MCP tooling for Neo Geo Pocket Color development and investigation: hardware-fidelity lint, project scaffolding, asset conversion and bridges to a bundled TLCS-900/H disassembler/emulator. Tool handlers, module loader and subprocess disassembly bridge are concrete code; claimed silicon validation is not independently confirmed.
Native DOS FAT filesystem analysis, directory sorting and defragmentation sources with a Microsoft-style interface.
Native utility enumerating DOS MCB chains, conventional/upper memory, EMS handles and XMS allocations.
Independent native DOS implementation of XCOPY-compatible recursive directory copying, date/archive filtering and overwrite handling.
FreeDOS-Himem-derived XMS manager with alternative HimemX2 allocation strategy and 32-bit extended-memory support.
Ported and maintained C86 compiler, dev86 assembler/linker/archiver/preprocessor, make and dis88 for native ELKS and modern hosts.
Native windowing/graphics implementation exposing Win32 and Nano-X/X11-like APIs, including ELKS/PC-98 drivers.
Compact interpreter for x86 DOS EXE/COM programs with DOS syscall compatibility, text console, debugging and disassembly.
Official maintained PC/GEOS GUI/kernel/application and SDK source release based on Breadbox Ensemble4.13.
Multiplatform continuation of Takeda Toshiya’s System3 for Win32 with native scenario, graphic and music interpreters.
SDL-based native implementation of AliceSoft System3.x, continued from xsystem35, with scenario execution, graphics/audio and debugging.
Preserved/restored Yuzo Koshiro MUCOM88 Z80 MML compiler/driver sources plus modern host music tools using a PC-8801 CPU/OPNA VM.
Reusable KL10/KS10 machine and I/O emulator with console, diagnostic and virtual media utilities; historical OS binaries execute as guests.
Substantive historical Incompatible Timesharing System kernel/userland source with automated emulator-based system reconstruction scripts.
Native Palm OS Conway Life application with editable cellular grid, step/run controls, double-buffered graphics and PRC resources.
Palm m500/m515 hardware emulator with Musashi m68k core, DragonBall peripherals, libretro/Qt frontends, save states and optional Tungsten T3 ARM support.
TypeScript reimplementation of Palm HotSync protocols and cross-platform serial/USB/network synchronization, database transfer and browser/CLI tooling.
TypeScript library and CLI for reading/writing Palm OS PDB/PRC files, core PIM databases and compressed PalmDOC documents.
DECnet Phase IV Ethernet endnode kernel protocol reimplementation plus adapted Linux DECnet user utilities and installation tooling.
Reusable 36-bit Honeywell/Bull DPS-8/M and 6000-series machine simulator for Multics with CPU instructions, memory/IOM and device emulation.
Public third-party archival tree attributed to AIX4.1.3, containing substantial historical IBM POWER kernel, commands and period build environment sources.
Public third-party OSF/1 archival source tree with Mach/BSD kernel, historical userland/X components and period build machinery.
Substantially adapted S.A.M./Bondwell speech synthesis for TRS-80 Model 4 CP/M and LS-DOS, including resident driver mode.
Native Z80 BIOS video/keyboard extension adding ANSI cursor control and text attributes to Montezuma Micro CP/M on TRS-80 Model 4.
TRS-80 LDOS/LS-DOS native driver that accesses virtual hard-disk files through an HxC floppy emulator and FAT32/LBA.
Reverse-engineered LS-DOS /HLP format tools, native HELPGEN disassembly, and Windows help-view/extract/generate implementations.
Annotated reconstruction and enhancements of MISOSYS COMP file/disk comparison command.
Preserved original native Oric graphics and map editor by Jonathan Bristow (Twilighte).
Preserved Jonathan Bristow/Twilighte unfinished Oric game conversion plus storybook and development resources.
Native Oric-1/Atmos Videotex terminal with serial/modem support and optional Python network bridge.
Independent Oric-1/Atmos port of Ozmoo with native screen, keyboard, Microdisc/Sedoric disk I/O and disk-mastering tools.
C/6502 native Oric-1 adaptation of Asteroids arcade game logic and vector shapes.
C tools and format documentation for parsing/decompiling MDX music and PDX samples, compiling MML, and converting/rendering Sharp X68000 MXDRV music.
Native THINK C 5.0 Macintosh game-development scaffolding with Toolbox/event/sound setup, offscreen sprite rendering and a concrete FlappyToaster example.
Native AmigaOS block-driver diagnostics for geometry, SCSI commands, packet support, throughput, latency and data-integrity testing.
C library and command-line tool to inspect, identify, checksum, split/merge and transform Amiga Kickstart ROM images.
Preserved AHCC 6.0 compiler/assembler/linker, editor/shell and Atari libraries, with unpacked original C/assembly source and 68000/68020/ColdFire distributions.
Original authors’ recovered July 1991 Gemini Atari ST desktop and Mupfel shell snapshot, rescued from their surviving SCSI hard disk.
Unity C# reimplementation of the Acorn Archimedes action-puzzle game Cataclysm, with original/demo levels and a new tutorial.
Python/Pygame reimplementation of the Acorn Archimedes ball-and-wheel puzzler Bambuzle, with CSV level definitions and original behavior recreated in new code.
Nim utility for stripping/dumping DIM headers and converting standard Sharp X68000 DIM floppy images to D88.
C asset converter from indexed PNG sprite sheets to X68000 XOBJ/XSP/SP graphics, frame references, palettes and optional XSB bundles.
Maintained original QED Atari GEM editor source, with syntax highlighting, macros, tags and multi-CPU native build variants.

Original Game Boy implementation of Nikoli’s Hitori puzzle rules, with board-size selection, random Latin-square generation, union-find-based puzzle construction, marking and solution checking. It implements game-specific logic rather than a generic game template.

Original native Game Boy chess game with shared C rules/search engine and host test tools. Inspected code implements move generation, legality, alpha-beta/negamax search, quiescence, opening book and a Game Boy display/input UI; it is not a wrapper around an emulated chess CPU.

Original Game Boy C demake inspired by Rocket League and Sideswipe. Its substantial game loop implements car and ball physics, collision response, boost/rotation, computer-opponent inputs, score and win states.

Original Game Boy C arcade homebrew with worm movement, scrolling ring obstacles, collision/death states, scoring, title presentation and battery-backed high-score data. Concrete game-specific implementation and ROM are present.

Native Game Boy ground/air horizontal shooter in C, with banked stages, enemy/projectile handling, terrain scrolling, HUD, bosses and music integration. Actual game loop and boss patterns are implemented.

Original Game Boy vampire-hunting adventure for the German ZFX Action 2024 event. Native C source implements rooms, player movement, enemies, item actions and textual interactions, with 21 room maps and a bundled game ROM.

Original Game Boy jam adventure with player input, environment/door interactions, chests, enemies, multiple house/map assets and a timed game state. The implementation is game-specific C source, not only the supplied tile-design files.

Original Game Boy mining game by Heiko Wolf for ZFX Action XVI, with a dwarf seeking a gem before a mine collapses. Native C implementation contains movement, combat/tool durability, items, room transitions, HUD and ten map assets.

Original native Game Boy C recreation of the Duality arcade minigame in GTA San Andreas. Inspected modules implement game-state updates, moving/shooting objects, collisions, scoring and native rendering; optional printer/multiplayer and SGB support form part of the same work.

Original native Game Boy assembly pirate-exploration game with seeded procedural ocean generation, streamed tile updates, sailing/combat, port economy, shore exploration and two-slot battery saves. Substantial world/combat/save implementations are present; the browser directory emulates the produced ROM and is not the game implementation.

Original Game Boy Color audiovisual demo with multi-scene native C/assembly presentation, DMA-driven tile animation, scanline palette effects, pseudo-3D tower/road and roto-zoom effects. Actual scene code and a 16-bank ROM are present, beyond a static screenshot/example collection.

From-scratch native C reimplementation of RetroSouls’ ZX Spectrum GLUF for SMS, Game Gear and Game Boy Color, built on CrossZGB. Inspected coroutine-driven player/level state implements charging, floor circuits, lifts, enemies, level progression and access codes; original level assets are converted by project-specific tools.

Native Game Boy Dizzy-style engine implemented in C around The Mushrooms Pie, a DizzyAGE example game. Concrete source handles scrolling room transitions, collision/animation, inventory/items, dialog/energy and room-specific bat/darkness/firefly interactions; it is a game-specific engine with content rather than an untouched template.

Preserved original Affinix Software Game Boy Color RPG source, developed chiefly in 1999–2001. Substantial C/assembly game, battle/overworld engines, maps/events/audio, design documents, historical builds and custom asset/build toolchain are retained as one coherent historical source archive; this is not a binary-derived reconstruction.
Substantial native Workplace Shell extension providing SOM classes, XCenter widgets, object/desktop extensions and system configuration.
John Allen original file manager, text/hex viewer and editor source, released for preservation with OS/2, DOS and Win32 platform adaptations.
From-scratch OS2LDR replacement with LE/LX kernel loading, disk/partition tools, filesystem support and modular pre-boot runtime.
Preserved IBM Workplace Shell for WIN-OS/2 and Windows3.1, replacing Program Manager with an object/folder-oriented desktop and setup package.
Historical Turbo Pascal lexer/LALR parser generator source with DOS, DPMI, Win16/Win32, OS/2 and Free Pascal build variants.
Native MOVE-compatible DOS file/directory move utility including cross-drive recursive copy-and-delete and same-volume renaming.
Native DOS screenful text pager with BIOS screen-dimension handling, tab expansion, interactive key input and localization.
DOS ASSIGN-compatible drive remapping implemented with C loader and resident assembly intercepting INT21 and absolute disk INT25/26.
Scenario bytecode decompiler/compiler and DAT archive utility for AliceSoft System1–3, with translation/debugging support and explicit original MSX2 Gakuen Senki handling.
AliceSoft System3.x scenario compiler/decompiler with ALD/ALK archive and PMS/QNT/VSP image utilities.
Reusable Motorola EXORciser 6800/6809 and SWTPC 6800 simulator with interactive monitor, disassembler and MDOS/EDOS/IMD disk utilities.
Synchronous Verilog MIT CADR Lisp machine implementation, FPGA board project files, simulation verification environment and microcode assembler/disassembler.
Go port of the author’s SIMH-based IBM 360/370 emulator, with CPU/channel/device implementations, assembler/disassembler and memory/register command monitor.
Previous NeXT computer emulator fork with concrete browser-worker/Emscripten entry point, GUI/display/audio/filesystem integration and WebAssembly build configuration.
Browser transistor-level circuit simulator and interactive chip-layout browser, with 6502 revD and Motorola 6800 node/transistor data and debugging/trace interfaces.
Reusable C++14 Yamaha FM/SSG/PCM sound-chip emulation cores plus VGM rendering example, supporting historical arcade, computer, console and synthesizer audio development.
Independent Sun-2 workstation emulator with MMU, SCSI, framebuffer/keyboard and experimental 3C400 network-device implementations.
Continuation of TME with modular Sun2/Sun3/SPARC/UltraSPARC machine models, CPU/MMU execution engines and modern display/network/host integration.
Reusable ARM handheld emulator with multiple Palm OS 5/Windows Mobile device models, SoC/MMU/peripheral emulation, virtual SD card and GDB remote debugging.
Experimental Palm IIIx/m100/IIIc emulator with ESP32-S3 target, native C hardware bridge, Windows VB.NET desktop harness and Palm ROM database/PRC extraction tooling.
Native TRS-80 utilities synchronising TRSDOS/LS-DOS date and time with supported emulator host-clock ports.
French AZERTY keyboard BIOS patch and installer for Montezuma Micro CP/M on TRS-80 Model 4/4p.
Internationalised KI/DVR native keyboard driver for TRS-80 Model III/4 running LDOS 5.3.
Native C/6502 real-time 3D projection and rasterisation library with interactive text, lores, hires and colour demonstrations.
Native Orix/Telestrat development utility inspecting ACIA serial status and testing serial transmission, console and joystick input.
Experimental native Orix/Telestrat PCM-file streaming to the parallel/printer port for a Digiblast-style audio interface.
Substantial native Oric Stormlord conversion source with later Telemon/Orix integration and package recipes.
Preserved Twilighte Oric adventure development tree with game engine, scene modules, disk routines, editors and music resources.
Substantially enhanced BBC/Electron Boulder Dash engine with external cave loading, new elements, cave/sprite editors and conversion utilities.
Detailed 6502 Shamus disassembly with semantic routine labels, combat/maze/timing analysis and ACME reassembly recipe.
Original author’s recovered mid-1980s TRS-80 Model I cassette BASIC extension source with extended graphics, music, strings and program editing.
C command-line conversion of classic Macintosh Glider 4.0 binary house files into Glider Vintage JSON, including linked multi-file houses.
Native Amiga console interposer translating Amiga console operations and xterm/telnet input while supporting remote shells and console applications.
Standalone Amiga replacement ROM image hosting MED memory inspection/editing, low-level chipset initialization and CPU control for hardware debugging.
Author’s native Amiga 3000/3000T memory diagnostics mapping address/data/cell failures to physical ZIP RAM chips, including memory absent from the OS free list.
Original BFFS AmigaOS filesystem source release with read/write BSD UFS/FFS support and native filesystem-checking, formatting, dump/restore and inspection utilities.
Maintained Tera Desktop source, an alternative GEM desktop for Atari TOS/MiNT systems with directory windows, file operations, application launching and integrated viewing.
Continuation of the free ST-Guide hypertext replacement with native TOS and modern-host viewers, HCP hypertext compiler and HYP/REF inspection/conversion tools.
Maintained COPS XCONTROL-compatible manager for Atari CPX control-panel modules, with independent windows, module loading and callback/resource adaptation.
Dedicated GNU-binutils supplement for TOS/MiNT executable and archive manipulation, including flags, stack-size editing, symbol tools and old-archive conversion.
Native GEM terminal and process/PTY integration for FreeMiNT, combining TosWin lineages with VT100/VT52/ANSI-style terminal handling.
Native Atari development library implementing GEM AES/VDI bindings, extension calls, compatibility glue, headers and extensive function-reference documentation.

Native four-channel Game Boy music application with oscillator controls, chord sequencing and Arduinoboy MIDI input. Substantial source implements sound-register manipulation, note/frequency UI, serial MIDI events and a chord-step sequencer; easy/ is a frozen earlier version of the same project.

Native bouncing-ball/paddle demonstration built to exercise a real cooperative/preemptive context-switching library, mutexes and ring-buffer communication. Each ball is a separate task, with architecture-specific SM83 and Z80 register-save/restore code; it is development research rather than a claimed full Arkanoid reconstruction.

Native Game Boy 2.5D/isometric room engine and interactive demonstration with 9×9×4-cell scenes, room/world linked-list maps, collision reconstruction, masked rendering, rotation, shadows and enemy movement. Includes project-specific scene/map and GBTD converters rather than just a published ROM.

Original native character-entry application that produces rotated/inverted text banners on the Game Boy Printer. UI, glyph-to-print-tile handling, progress display and serial printer packet/status commands are present; a reused printer library is attributed in source.

Open-source native Game Boy interface ROM for the Orange FM custom radio cartridge, implementing frequency/preset/volume/settings UI, radio/RDS/status synchronization and a cartridge-MCU command protocol. Interrupt-driven sleeping minimizes console interference with radio reception.

Game Boy/GBDK adaptation of the msx_qrcode/Nayuki QR-code lineage with ROM-banked encoder, payload checking, bank restoration and runtime graphical rendering demonstration. The modified encoder and platform wrapper are present; this is a reusable native library port rather than an embedded guest-CPU wrapper.

Native on-device memory hex viewer/editor for Game Boy and Mega Duck, with navigable address display, independently selected write address/value, VRAM-safe reads, bank-register writes and dark-mode interface. Concrete memory-access and UI code make this a useful debugging utility.

Native Game Boy/Game Boy Color authenticator implementing HMAC-SHA1/RFC6238-style TOTP, base32 account entry, MBC3 RTC access and battery-SRAM storage, plus GB-specific UI/audio/SGB border. Pure-C crypto and concrete hardware glue are present, independently of its sibling GBA port.

Experimental native Game Boy musical application inspired by granular synthesis, with editable grain-selection cells, loop mode, grain size/speed/period controls and timer-driven CH3 waveform output. Actual control logic, native audio register manipulation and grain data are present.

Native Game Boy CH3 audio application that evaluates sixteen selectable bytebeat-style integer formulas, with function/settings/visualization screens, pitch/tempo controls, wave-RAM playback and scanline display effects. Formula execution is compiled C, not emulation of a historical program CPU.

Native C/GBDK SNES mouse and gamepad link-port drivers with both blocking and interrupt-driven polling, packet interpretation and drawing/input-test ROM. Includes physical wiring/inverter documentation and hardware compatibility matrix; SNES is the peripheral protocol, not an emulated software target.

Original CGB-only Mobile Adapter GB diagnostic client with separate native GBDK/C and RGBDS/SM83 implementations of packet framing, checksum/session/ACK handling, adapter config readout and network tests. It exercises actual serial protocol behavior rather than repackaging a Pokémon ROM or wrapping a guest CPU.

Native Game Boy 4×4×4 tic-tac-toe with 76-line board evaluation, computer move/fork scoring, three difficulty levels and rotatable sliced-board UI. Author traces own implementation from ZX81 Sinclair BASIC circa 1982 through QL/BBC BASIC and a 2004 C version, then a GBDK UI; predecessor binaries are not analyzed here.

Original replacement native Game Boy Camera ROM exposing sensor exposure/dithering/gain controls, capture modes, histogram analysis, gallery saving/deletion and printing. Direct sensor/register and image-SRAM source is present; designed for HDR’s flashable camera PCB.
Creative Labs SBFMDRV CMF sound driver recovery: multiple annotated x86 disassemblies by NewRisingSun and Valley Bell, plus Valley Bell C ports and original-output comparison fixtures.
Preserved Samuel Audet 1997 DOS utility that probes Sound Blaster access and rewrites Win-OS/2 SYSTEM.INI driver lines to avoid modal errors when the sound card is unavailable.
John McSorley 1995 PC Magazine Win16 system utility that allocates conventional-memory blocks and shrinks them to influence low-memory allocation, with companion Visual Basic memory viewer.
Historical OS/2 WPS Toolkit library and samples for extended attributes, process/system/PM controls, WPS settings, configuration files, regular expressions and memory-mapped files.
Chris Wohlgemuth multimedia WPS classes with audio/image/video metadata and playback integration, media folders, JPEG IO procedure, converters and SOM class definitions.
Andrei Los OS/2 Alt+Tab replacement and taskbar with Presentation Manager popup, shared-memory keyboard hooks, XCenter widget and DOS full-screen switch helper.
FreeDOS keyboard management implementation with BIOS interrupt hooks, multiplex API, programmable actions and KL/KC layout loading. No guest CPU interpreter.
Jason Hood SHSUCD suite derived from John McCoy SHSUCD: MSCDEX-compatible redirector, ISO-backed CD/DVD drivers, optical-image creation and El Torito boot-image extraction.
Imre Leber DOS CHKDSK reimplementation with FAT12/16 image and disk checks, cross-link/lost-cluster repair, directory and long-name checking, surface scan and XMS sector cache.
ND-100/CX full-system emulator with memory-management, storage/network peripherals, BPUN loading, disassembly and DAP debugging, maintained as a substantial nd100em continuation.
ND-500 emulator with instruction implementations and generated decoding tables, disassembler, DOM/program loaders, interactive debugger and DAP adapter.
LMI Lambda system emulator executing original microcode and binaries, including Lambda processor, Intel 8088 SDU, NuBus, SMD disks, tape and console.
C implementation of the Medley Interlisp bytecode virtual machine, garbage collection and host display/filesystem/network interfaces, preserving and extending the historical Venue runtime.
Preserved and modernized Xerox/Venue Medley Interlisp programming environment with historic Lisp sources, compiled files, fonts, libraries, desktop and sysout loadup pipeline.
DEC PDP-6 emulator transcribing machine schematics, virtual front panels, peripherals, a newer C simulator and assembler/loader/DECtape utilities.
Low-level Whirlwind, TX-0, PDP-1 and PDP-5 emulators with physical/SDL panel interfaces, peripheral tools and PDP-1 remote-debug service.
Qt6/64-bit continuation of Palm OS Emulator 3.5 with DragonBall hardware emulation, random-input testing, debugger/profiler, TCP automation and MCP proxy.
DEC PDP-11/70 system emulator with MMU, disk/tape/terminal/network devices, debugger with expression-based breakpoints, desktop and microcontroller front ends.
Xerox Dandelion/Star 8010/1108 full-system emulator with microcoded central processor, Intel 8085 IOP, disks, display, Ethernet and source/disassembly debugger.
Modern .NET Xerox Alto I/II XM emulator with microcode engine, Diablo/Trident disks, Ethernet, display/input, print raster hardware and integrated debugger.
Java reimplementation of Xerox Network Services including Courier/RPC, clearinghouse/authentication, boot, filing, printing, mail, external communication and virtual Ethernet hub.
Semantically commented and reassemblable disassembly unifying the Dragon 32 and both Dragon 64 BASIC ROM variants.
BeebAsm-format annotated Atom disk operating-system source, WD1770 adaptation and disk-management utilities.
Source restoration/disassembly and optional enhancement of Dragon Beta OS-9 boot ROM, kernel, drivers and commands.
Annotated Z80 disassembly/reassembly of NAS-DOS 1.4 for Nascom disk systems.
Original Atari 8-bit BASIC compiler/interpreter and integrated editor with a modern-host cross-compiler and Atari 5200 output.
Annotated MADS-format TurboBasic XL 1.5 disassembly with bug fixes and automatic low-memory relocation tooling.
MADS-converted BW-DOS sources with substantive resident DOS, command-processor and utility optimizations.
Annotated ROMDOS boot-sector reconstruction and new single-sector boot experiments with reproducible disk/ROM packaging scripts.
Native Atari XL/XE port of reconstructed BBC BASIC 3.10 with MOS translation layer, graphics, sound and file-I/O adaptations.
Software SID waveform/envelope emulation for Atari 8-bit, adapting C64 tune replay routines to POKEY output.
Substantial original Atari 8-bit rule-based puzzle game, portable C logic and Windows level editor source.
Cross-assembler framework using C preprocessing and inline C++ metaprogramming with retro-machine templates and opcode macros.
Reusable native shared library and developer SDK for Amiga character-set discovery, Unicode conversion, codepage tables and Base64 handling, with maintained AmigaOS3/4, MorphOS and AROS variants.
Substantial native Amiga port of OpenSSL with version-selecting master library, per-application state and threading integration, command-line application and developer SDK.
Opened, reformatted and translated source of Richard Körber’s formerly closed Amiga hardware/system identification library, accompanying ARexx library, diagnostics and expansion-board database.
Host toolkit for formatting, checking, extracting and repacking X68000 SxSI/Human68k disk images with partition metadata, extended names, Shift-JIS and preserved file attributes.

Hugo Fiennes’s recovered RISC OS serial block-driver and Atomwide/Serial Port hardware-module sources, including Internal/PC wiring, Dummy and SP_Dual variants, original binaries and provenance metadata.
Recovered Hugo Fiennes / The Serial Port RISC OS SCSI firmware family with Alpha, QD, VTN, Turbo and EcoSCSI drivers, ROM builders, filing-system/filer modules and formatter/tape application sources.
Gavin Wraith’s native RISC OS Lua port with SWI calls, typed memory blocks, file-type/directory helpers and LPeg support integrated with Lua 5.4.3 sources.
Preserved Acorn ROM-image construction utility that arranges kernel/HAL/modules from a splitfile, patches image size, pads fixed positions and emits checksums/CRCs and signatures.
Windows desktop tool for detokenizing Acorn BBC BASIC V files and applying context-based variable/procedure renaming and syntax highlighting.
Structured .NET library for authoring AmigaGuide hypertext databases, nodes, links, formatting and navigation metadata for native Amiga documentation.

Substantial source adaptation of 0x7f's Black Castle: player weapons, monsters, bosses, level data and platform-specific sound/scrolling implementations. The inspected port has explicit SM83, Z80 and mos6502 targets rather than an embedded guest CPU interpreter.

Native presentation viewer plus a host-side JSON-to-header compiler. PNG backgrounds, per-text placement/colours, typewriter animation, slide navigation and cartridge-RAM resume are implemented rather than only described.

A compact but complete-looking native graphics experiment: the user enters a binary sequence with A/B, edits it, then the program repeats the pattern around an expanding square spiral using GBDK drawing primitives. The repository contains approximately 180 lines of project-specific C and pattern.gb.

Native diagnostic ROM with per-button counters, invalid D-pad detection, model detection, link-cable exchange, screen alignment/gradient tests, sound feedback and theme persistence. Selected C implements the diagnostic state and flash-save routines.

Native channel-3 audio demonstration implementing timer-interrupt sawtooth generation and variable-rate playback of an embedded sample. The inspected source writes wave RAM and sound registers and exposes pitch/mode controls.

Native VGM file browser/player streams uncompressed register-command music from cartridge SD storage. Separate Game Boy wave/sound, Game Gear stereo PSG and Master System PSG/OPLL implementations are present; inspected implementations decode VGM command bytes directly rather than executing a guest CPU.

GBDK input integration and a drawing demonstration for an Inside Gadgets USB adapter with modified CH559 firmware. Source implements serial interrupt transfers, a receive ring buffer, three-byte packet decoding, cursor motion and mouse-controlled drawing/scroll/clear.

A substantial native four-shade drawing application with 18×15 canvases, up to sixteen in-memory canvases, cursor/menu input and visual colour indicators. README describes Kindle e-ink palette optimisation; the output remains a Game Boy ROM, not a native Kindle port.

Native benchmark cartridge measures eighteen checksum/noncryptographic/light-cryptographic algorithms against a generated 1024-byte buffer. Inspected C implements dispatch, paginated/sortable results and frame-counter timing, plus concrete xxHash32 and classical hash implementations.

Native waveform oscillator with pitch/octave selection, preset waveforms, waveform visualisation and sound-register/timer control. Inspected implementation copies selected packed samples into channel-3 wave RAM and updates the display from waveform contents.

Native experimental drone generator evolves a 32-nibble shift-register waveform, packs it into channel-3 wave RAM in a timer interrupt, and uses waveform data for scanline distortion. Period controls, waveform reseeding and playback state are implemented.

Substantial ZGBJam 2019 game adapted for Game Boy, Game Gear and Master System. Inspected source implements helicopter acceleration, landing/death states, hook deployment, collisions and three-level progression; assets and menu/win states are present.

Substantial BitBitJam 2017 game adapted for Game Boy, Mega Duck and Game Gear. Player aiming/flying/dancing states, launch motion, damage, moving platforms, enemies and banked multi-level maps are represented in source.

Native Cell Machine remake explicitly crediting Sam Hogan's original. Substantial C implements cell placement/rotation, push/generator/update rules, step/run simulation, scrolling maps, menus and cartridge-RAM save/load state.
Independent PC-98 disk-format analysis and Python conversion suite: synthesizes FDI geometry headers, strips FDI/HDI headers, checks heuristic image validity and creates blank media.
Aaron Lawrence and Ronald Brill OS/2 help viewer and replacement HelpMgr.dll, with substantive IPF file parsing, full-text search and native Presentation Manager integration.
Preserved native OS/2 Presentation Manager utility by Arthur van Beek and Steven Levine that parses executable import tables and diagnoses DLL search-path and load failures.
IBM sample-derived PMSpy source archive with native window selection, message filtering and shared hook DLL implementation for observing posted and sent OS/2 PM messages.
IBM SD386 5.00 final source archive: native source/assembly debugging, symbol/type inspection, multithread/process control and ESP remote-debug transport support.
Martin Lafaix resource manager/decompiler suite preserving REXX resource-container editing and .RES-to-.RC reconstruction plus C/Pascal packed-resource extraction helpers for OS/2 binaries.
Eberhard Mattes emxomf preserved converter implementation, including GNU a.out relocation/symbol handling and STABS-to-IBM HLL3 debug-information translation.
Eric Auer native DOS APM/ACPI control utility and resident idle handler, implementing POWER-compatible modes, cache flushing, disk/video power controls and reboot/shutdown paths.
Daniel Kegel NANSI preserved and extended DOS console-driver source implementing ANSI escape-state parsing, cursor/video handling and keyboard reassignment with FreeDOS-era maintenance.
Eric Auer native DOS replacement GRAPHICS utility implementing resident CGA/EGA/VGA/MCGA screen capture and PostScript, Epson ESC/P and HP PCL printer output.
Official Hercules continuation implementing System/370, ESA/390 and z/Architecture processors, devices, hardware console, tracing and historical disk/tape utilities.
Control Data 6000/70/170/180 system simulator with 60-bit CPU and peripheral processors, disk/tape/network devices, dual Cyber 170/180 state operation and historical-system installation automation.
BESM-6 48-bit instruction and extracode emulator with Dubna monitor job processing, embedded system tapes, assembler, simulated drums/disks, text encodings and plotter-output generation.
Ada rewrite of Data General MV/Eclipse emulation, sharing processor and memory code between physical MV hardware simulation and AOS/VS Ring-7 user-program emulation.
JavaScript Burroughs B5500 stack/descriptor processor and multiprocessor central-control emulator with peripheral devices, browser console and software/source recovery artifacts.
JavaScript implementation of the decimal Burroughs 220 processor, arithmetic and control panels with Cardatron, tape and terminal peripheral models, accompanied by BALGOL recovery work.
JavaScript IBM 1620 Model 2 decimal processor, memory-cycle state machine, operator panel and card/paper-tape/disk/printer/plotter operating environment with historical software recovery.
Coherent kit of processor, bus, serial, storage and display models for RC2014/RCbus, Retrobrew and other retrocomputers, focused on software development and Fuzix testing.
Continuation of discontinued ES40 emulator with DecChip 21264CB EV68 CPU/PALcode, Tsunami chipset, storage/network/display devices and optional x86-64 JIT.
Preserved GXemul 0.6 tree with C/C++ instruction translation, full-system DECstation/SGI and other workstation machine models, peripheral/network emulation and debugger infrastructure.

Integrated X68000 cross-development environment built around m68k GCC/binutils, Human68k/IOCS runtime support and ELF-to-X executable plus X68k-object-to-ELF converters. Also supplies startup/linker/spec files, Newlib integration, socket and pthread compatibility libraries and remote-debug wrappers.

Native Human68k loopback block-device driver and losetup command that mount XDF/DIM/D88 floppy or HDF/HDS/MOS storage images as local drives. Implements resident driver installation plus a documented patch to Human68k disk-I/O cache linked-list handling to permit nested filesystem access.

Work-in-progress Atari STE enhancement project for Lotus Turbo Challenge 2, with address-specific original routine stubs, replacement road/background/car rendering, blitter-assisted sprite paths and runtime caching. Build emits patch blocks keyed to original game addresses rather than a standalone replacement game.

Reverse-engineered reimplementation of Brøderbund’s 1990 Amiga Wings of Fury for Atari STE/Mega STE. A substantial C++ game implements original flight model, enemies, weapons, all 15 maps, front end, saved games and drawing on AGT, with Amiga-format decoders and conversion scripts plus 68k disassembly/decompilation research.

Community continuation of Juan Antonio Gómez Gálvez’s reusable MSX/MSX2/MSX2+ emulator for Amiga, built from original v3.1 source and parts of v3.2/v3.5. Large native 68020 assembly implementation includes Z80 execution, VDP timing/sprites, cartridge mappers, FM sound, menus and save support.

Original Dreamcast first-person shooter and custom DCE3D engine by Josh PH3NOM Pearson. The published source includes a native PowerVR rendering pipeline, player/enemy combat, collision, scene triggers, custom MD2 loading and FMV support. This is the released incomplete native game project, not a commercial-game reconstruction.

XL2 Sonic Z-Treme is a native Sega Saturn Sonic fangame using an older Z-Treme Engine, with game/entity logic, player physics, camera/rendering, CD loading, animation and sound source. It is an independently programmed fangame inspired by Sonic X-Treme, not a recovered Sonic X-Treme source tree.

High-level C development library and Windows-oriented toolchain for Neo Geo CD, layered over Neo Dev Kit and DATlib. Its own implementation manages sprites, palettes, joypads, collisions, CDDA/ADPCM and project workflows, rather than merely collecting links or wrapping one game.

Enhanced C++ recreation of the Homestar Runner Flash game Trogdor. README explicitly says the author opened the original in a Flash decompiler and manually ported its ActionScript and assets to C++, recreating Flash animation/scaling behavior. Includes real gameplay classes, collision/animation logic and multiple console builds, not an emulator wrapper.

Original C++ SDL1.2/SDL2 Sudoku game with on-demand puzzle generation, pre-generated harder puzzles, controller/touch/mouse input, saves and scalable graphics. Includes extensive native console build support and its own game-logic implementation; no reverse-engineering origin is claimed.

Independent C# WonderSwan/Color emulator with its own V30MZ core, hardware devices and desktop interfaces. A Windows Forms player and Dear ImGui/OpenGL debugger/disassembler share the core; this is reusable console emulation and inspection tooling, not a game-specific runtime.

Cycle-stepped Atari Lynx emulator library in Rust, exposing Lynx CPU/bus, cartridge/EEPROM, Mikey display/audio/UART and Suzy sprite/math hardware. Its reusable core serves several separately packaged frontends, rather than embedding emulation for one game.

Long-running reusable PC Engine/TurboGrafx-16 emulator for Nintendo DS-family hardware, with its own native emulation loop, HuC6280 integration, VDC/VCE/PSG state, CD-ROM and Arcade Card handling. Distinct target-specific emulator in FluBBa library family.

Jolly Good API educational emulator for ColecoVision/Super Game Module, CreatiVision and My Vision, with documented hardware models, memory mapping, state serialization, controller devices and TMS9918/PSG integration. This libretro-hosted source also includes an actual reusable core and JG API build.

Native WonderSwan hardware-behavior and emulator validation test ROM collection, covering CPU quirks, timing, DMA, display, EEPROM, interrupts, sound and RTC, with interactive timing/memory/I/O inspection utilities. Substantial C/assembly tests and own ROM build graph rather than a list of tests elsewhere.

Original GameCube/Wii homebrew hovercraft racing project inspired by Diddy Kong Racing. Source includes component-based scenes, controller input, hovercraft behavior, camera/math, graphics/resources and rendering systems. It is an independently written native racer prototype, not a port or Diddy Kong Racing reconstruction.

Reusable native Nintendo DS emulator for WonderSwan, Color/Crystal and Benesse PocketChallenge V2, with V30MZ execution, hardware scanline integration, cartridge/EEPROM save states and ROM loading. Its WonderWitch/BootFriend transfer tools also support handheld development workflows.

The 1994 Safari Software space-combat game reconstructed from its shipped binary into a modular C engine. Flight/combat implementation cites original byte offsets; DOS graphics, cockpit, missions, keyboard, music and sound drivers are present. It targets semantic equivalence rather than byte-identical recompilation.

A reusable analysis, disassembly, x86-to-C lifting and runtime toolkit extracted from multiple PC recompilation projects. Includes MZ/NE/LE/PE and NeXTSTEP Mach-O readers; x86-16/32/64 lifters and differential tests; DOS, Win16, Win32-on-POSIX and native32 runtime components. It is infrastructure rather than a game-specific interpreter wrapper.

A separate osFree subproject reimplementing the 16-bit Windows 3.0 environment on DOS/VDM, with kernel, USER, loader, drivers and system components. Source incorporates and adapts Wine, TWIN, ReactOS and HX-DOS code. KRNL286 selector allocation and its Watcom/JWasm build are present, not merely a compatibility proposal.

Independent osFree Family API implementation for binary dual-mode applications that run without recompilation on DOS and OS/2. Contains KAL, VIO/KBD/MOU, memory/file/NLS, static and dynamic API libraries, and a Wine-derived NE DOS loader.

Continuation of Rene Straub's 1995–1996 Tetris-style OS/2 Presentation Manager game. The maintained 1.50 tree retains the historical playfield engine and adds multilingual UI/help, configurable input, sound and modern Open Watcom builds; legacy source/material is separated.

Original source of Media Pocket's 1999 Brick Blaster and WinEOS 4.00 Alpha, restored to match the released game by comparing disassemblies. Includes translation-length/coordinate corrections, updated makefiles and narrowly documented compatibility patches for Windows.

Original open-source release and continued maintenance of the 1997 first-person role-playing game. The large C engine preserves DOS renderer/game/network modules alongside SDL-based native ports and a newly integrated Emscripten target.

A substantive Commander Keen 4 EGA source modification derived from K1n9_Duk3's reconstructed Keen 4–6 sources. Changes the engine timing/render pipeline to 70-fps operation, adds smooth one-pixel panning options and CRT Terminator synchronization support, while retaining the reconstructed C/assembly game tree.

Native homebrew DOS game-engine framework with VGA Mode 13h double buffering, compiled x86 sprite blitting, Korean/Latin bitmap fonts, PIT timing, keyboard IRQs, OPL2 VGM playback and Sound Blaster PCM mixing. Includes an actual game/smoke-test harness and TypeScript asset tools.

Historical archive by an original author augmented with concrete Space Panicco technical analysis and a working browser VMAP level editor. The editor imports/exports the original stage format, paints stage cells and validates playable actor/enemy placement. Promoted for implemented tooling and format analysis, not as recovered game source.

A native Turbo Pascal DOS action game made for the 2026 CGA Game Jam. Its nine Pascal modules implement timed gameplay, player/enemy behavior, HUD, sprites, scoring, background and menu, using the CGA BGI driver.

A reusable Python-standard-library memory scan/edit/freeze tool for DOSBox Staging's HTTP memory API. A local Python server serves its JavaScript UI, scans memory and maintains cheat tables; it targets arbitrary DOS software rather than wrapping one game.

A clean-room NES reimplementation of Commander Keen Galaxy episodes 4–6 with a PC-side pipeline extracting the original DOS executable tables, graphics, maps and audio into NES assets. Native C/6502 game code targets MMC5, with rescaled 60-Hz player physics, actor logic, HUD, audio and banked graphics.

Java implementation of the Xerox Mesa machine architecture in two machine profiles: Draco emulates the 6085 Daybreak/Dove and Duchess reconstructs the Guam environment used by GVWin. Implements Mesa CPU, virtual memory, traps, disk/floppy formats, display/input, networking and execution debugging.

C23 Apollo Domain family emulator with Motorola 68020/68030/68040 machine profiles, storage controllers and a reconstructed proprietary Apollo token ring. Implements ring framing/MAC/PHY and firmware-visible devices; includes differential/oracle tooling and a substantial test suite.

Rust/C++ emulator of original SGI IRIS Indigo IP12, centered on the MIPS R3000A with instruction decoding, MMU/cache/coprocessors, PIC1/HPC1/INT2 devices, SCSI, graphics, network and a Qt debugger UI.

Reusable high-level execution environment for Tapwave Zodiac native ARM applications. Uses Unicorn for ARM and 68k launch code while reconstructing the 612-entry TwGlue/Palm OS interface, graphics, input, sound, VFS and application callbacks. This is an application-class emulator, not a wrapper for one game.

Native Palm OS utility that shifts the system calendar epoch/window, converts stored dates with backup, reinstalls after reset and patches date conversion/formatting/select-day APIs on 68k Palm OS 3.5–4.x and ARM Palm OS 5. Source contains separate 68k installer and native ARM patch implementation.

C# partial reconstruction of Ridge32 workstations with custom 32-bit CPU/instruction decoder, virtual/physical memory, traps, disk controllers, display and a debugger/disassembler. Actual CPU integer/floating instruction dispatch and Priam device sources exist.

C# reconstruction of Xerox PARC PUP/Interim File Server protocols: BreathOfLife network boot, EFTP, FTP, CopyDisk disk imaging, time/name service, routing and mail. Serves Alto emulators or real Alto machines using UDP/raw Ethernet and optional BeagleBone interface.

Recovered Compatible Time-Sharing System source tree cleaned against historical listings. Contains FAP/MAD operating-system, filesystem/loader, commands, libraries and tools plus tape/disk staging and SIMH boot instructions, rather than documentation-only preservation.

C emulator reconstructing Centurion CPU-6 and known peripherals from Eldorado EE200 material, diagnostics and reverse-engineering discoveries. Includes CPU/MMU/DMA/interrupt state, scheduler, disks, mux, disassembler and CBIN loader.

Java mainframe programming environment implementing HLASM-compatible macro assembly, linkage editing, zCOBOL compilation and a runtime emulator with QSAM/VSAM/CICS services. Substantial assembler, processor and service implementations, macro libraries and regression tests exist.
C/SIMH-based reusable simulator of Soviet M-20 45-bit mainframe with machine arithmetic, memory, card reader/punch, drum, tape and printer devices, Russian/English frontends and media/autocode tools.

Java Swing integrated development and simulation environment for IBM 1401. Combines source editing, Autocoder invocation, SIMH process control, execution/breakpoints, memory/console/printout views and timer/UI support; original frontend source is maintained separately from bundled external engines.

Python implementation of IBM 1620 Model 1 decimal CPU with 20,000-digit default memory, flag bits, instruction execution, card-file and typewriter I/O, CMEM loading and built-in debugger. Supports varied historic programs and compiler/assembler workflows rather than a game-specific wrapper.

Reconstruction of Konami's 1986 RC-741 MSX software synthesizer, including the annotated 32 KB Z80 listing, DAC output timing, tone engine and tape-data formats. This is a non-game application disassembly with supporting Python research tools.
Annotated recovery of HAL Laboratory's 1984 16 KB MSX golf cartridge. Includes address-anchored names/notes, executable Z80 listing and Python reconstruction of course maps, scripts and compression.
Annotated Z80 recovery of Casio's 1985 32 KB MSX golf cartridge, with address-stable analysis notes and course/3D rendering tools derived from the ROM.

Recovery of T&E Soft's 1983 Normal Edition golf cartridge as a 246-line tokenized MSX BASIC program, with complete line commentary, course-data decoding and a retokenizer. It contains no game Z80 machine code.
Full sixteen-bank Z80 disassembly of Konami's 1988 RC-759 Parodius MSX cartridge. Includes bank-aware tracing, labeled code/data and ROM-derived graphics, text and audio reconstruction.
Annotated recovery of multiple Kaypro II/IV boot ROMs, CP/M BIOS revisions, CONFIG utilities and character generators, with original images, assembly listings and binary-comparison scripts.
Disassembly of Romantic Robot RODOS 2.19 for Amstrad CPC, developed into relocatable, bug-fixed RODOS 2.22. Includes annotated ROM source, debug commands, test disks and release/build machinery.

SkoolKit reconstruction of Psion's 1982 ZX Spectrum Space Raiders, including annotated game listing, control/reference files, snapshot input and recipes for documentation, assembly and runnable TAP output.
Annotated Z80 disassembly of the first MSX Topo Soft cassette-loading logo animation, with decoded graphics attributes/self-modifying code and cassette wrapper source.
Commodore 64 Dino Eggs recovery with extensively labeled 6510 assembly, hardware constants, original PRG/disk images and separate disk-protection/error-check build options.

Recovery of the CP/M ISX.COM ISIS-II compatibility environment, plus modified BDOS and Z80182 P112 BIOS needed to run Intel development tools. Includes disassembly, system-image build scripts, utilities and floppy-image data.
Reusable Rust crate for 6502 binary disassembly with undocumented opcodes, addressing modes, cycle counts, register-use and status-flag metadata. Source includes complete opcode model and tests.
Swift library and macOS command-line tool for MOS 6502 assembly analysis, including label/comment-aware disassembly, opcode definitions, Woz Monitor fixtures and an unfinished assembler parser.

A native X680x0 sprite-management system by Yosshin, used in Cho Ren Sha 68K and other games. Its raster-time sprite doubler supports up to 512 displayed sprites, dynamic PCG assignment over 32768 patterns and triple buffering. This is the reusable assembly library, not a Cho Ren Sha port or CPU wrapper.

A native X680x0 text-plane renderer by Yosshin for 8x8 and 16x16 sixteen-color fonts, including sprite-PCG-to-font conversion and palette/scroll operations. The published assembly implementation and C examples preserve a library originating in 1994.

A Human68k remote-debugging server derived from bet4it/gdbserver, adapted to m68k programs built with elf2x68k. It runs the X-format target on X680x0 and serves GDB over serial, with exception/register/process control and pthread-aware thread support. Native debugger software rather than an emulator.

A m68k re-expression of xorvoid SectorC: a 512-byte C-subset compiler that runs on X68000 and emits native m68k instructions. It contains token parsing, expression and control-flow compilation, branch fixups and direct instruction emission, plus examples and a test harness.

An author-maintained collection of X68000 games sharing a C/68000-assembly hardware and asset framework: BINGO de PRO-68k, Ball und Panzer Golf/BattleKata, Over Kata racing, Suikata ball-merging and X68ZKeeper match-three. Kept as one collection record to avoid inflating shared-engine directory paths into separate projects.

A native X68000 FM music-tracker/editor implementation. Its C sources implement phrase editing, pattern rendering, channel commands, playback timing and OPM-register updates; it is a tracker application rather than a desktop MDX decoder or emulator.

A Human68k SMB filesystem driver, mount tool and interactive client using libsmb2. It translates Human68k filesystem request packets into remote share operations, manages directory/file handles and converts Shift-JIS/UTF-8 names, making network shares available as native drives.

A native Human68k remote-drive driver paired with a Windows/macOS serial service. It exposes the connected host filesystem over RS-232C/UART with request packets, cached reads/writes and directory operations, emulating the practical host-drive facilities available in X68000 emulators.

A native X680x0 utility that loads XDF floppy images outside the configured usable memory and patches boot-time ROM access to boot directly from those RAM-resident images. Includes original C image/SRAM control and 68000 ROM-patching code, not an emulator wrapper.

A Human68k network driver for a W5500-based Ethernet adapter connected through the X680x0 joystick port. It provides a Keisoku Giken inetd-compatible socket/control interface and DHCP support through original driver and bit-banged hardware access implementation.

A lightweight SQLite3 port to Human68k, combining upstream amalgamation with a custom stdio-backed VFS, OS-bridge stubs, compact SQL shell and disk-backed UTF-8/Shift-JIS conversion. Supplies native static-library and MicroPython wrapper integration as well as the command-line application.

Dave Appleby and John Tytgat resource converter for Acorn RISC OS. It reads and writes Toolbox Resource RESF v1.00/v1.01 and Wimp Template binary files through editable text, with class/gadget/icon reconstruction and relocation handling. Includes native desktop front end and portable command-line build.

Chris Bazley native RISC OS Toolbox application that extracts the Window Manager ROM/RAM sprite pools or window-tool sprites into valid Sprite files. Replaces Dave Thomas original Grab with a fresh implementation and fixes sparse/invalid sprite-area layouts when saving.

A native classic 68000 Macintosh Conway Game of Life application written in modern C++ and built using Retro68. Includes cell-field state updates, compact bit matrices, QuickDraw-oriented grid renderers, window/event handling and buttons.

Multi-system emulator with C++ console/hardware implementations and a C# desktop/debugger interface. The selected SourMesen repository is the archived roughly-2.1.1 mid-2025 codebase; its pinned README redirects ongoing development to MesenCE. One Mesen lineage record is proposed, not a separate count for the successor.

Independent Rust multi-console emulator organized into reusable CPU, console backend, renderer, GUI, debugger and web crates. Implements Sega 8/16-bit systems and expansions plus Nintendo consoles and PC Engine; not a game-specific wrapper.

JavaScript Sega Master System/Game Gear emulator evolved from a JavaGear port into an optimizing dynamic recompiler. Includes explicit bytecode parsing, control-flow analysis, AST generation and optimization and generates executable JavaScript functions for arbitrary loaded ROMs.

Modernized standalone Charles MacDonald SMS Plus lineage, intended as a small reference Sega Master System/Game Gear emulator for homebrew and emulator developers. Contains actual CPU, memory, VDP, sound and shell source.

C-language Android Master System/Game Gear emulator by Phil Potter with Java Android UI and native SDL-based emulation. The published cleaned-up open-source project includes its own substantial Z80 instruction implementation rather than only calling an external console core.

Independent C Sega Game Gear emulator with built-in Z80 assembler and disassembler, written as a learning and hardware-development reference project. Includes tests for CPU, graphics, assembly/disassembly and integration.

Portable Zig multi-system Sega emulator integrating native hardware scheduling, video/audio, memory and reusable external CPU cores. Supports Genesis, Sega CD, Master System, Game Gear and SG-1000 with desktop, web and libretro frontends.
Rust Virtual Boy emulator with reusable core, middleware and a command-line frontend/debugger. Implements V810 CPU, display and sound devices and supports arbitrary commercial or homebrew ROM inputs.

Virtual Boy emulator native to Nintendo 3DS, continuing r3Ddragon/Reality Boy/Red Dragon with a V810 dynamic recompiler, busywait detection and hardware-accelerated stereo rendering. Selected as the active representative of that lineage.

Independent Rust Virtual Boy emulator designed for Apple Vision Pro, with Swift Apple-platform integration and an additional Rust desktop frontend. Core explicitly models V810 state, bus activity, timing and interrupts.

Portable Atari Lynx emulator from Keith Wilkins Handy through SDLEMU, with a modern SDL2 renderer, GUI, controller input, settings and ComLynx networking. One representative of the Handy core/SDL lineage is proposed.

Oswan WonderSwan/Color emulator port for OpenDingux and Windows, containing NEC V30MZ CPU, video, APU, input and cartridge/file implementations with a handheld UI. Selected representative of the Oswan lineage, rather than counting each downstream port.
Native C++23 re-creation of The 7th Guest engine with GRV scripting, VDX decoding, puzzle logic and separate preservation disassemblies for DOS, Win32, Classic Mac and CD-i players.
Recovered C game core and C++ ix audio library for the 1996 Kilrathi Saga Win32 Wing Commander II, with modern SDL2 port and comparison tooling.
Function-by-function C11 transliteration of the DOS/EGA racer engine, recovered game tables and wave/music virtual machines, with native SDL2 and WebAssembly outputs.
Maintained kLIBC-0.6 lineage fork implementing Unix-compatible C runtime facilities on OS/2, with its own DLL/version identity and backward ABI/API compatibility.
Preserved Odin32 compatibility-layer source, here in a branch aimed at SWT/OS2 and Eclipse with Win32 API libraries, loader/runtime integration and test applications.
LFN-aware Norton Commander-style TUI file manager with built-in Zip/UnZip, editor, panel and file operation source for 16-bit DOS and modern Windows.
Rust multi-system emulator for PC-98/9821, PC-88/88VA, PC-6001, MSX, FM Towns/FM7, Sharp X68000/X1 and IBM PC/AT.
Native OS/2 Presentation Manager audio player with plugin playback/decoding infrastructure, playlists, audio controls and historical source distribution/build documentation.
Preserved native OS/2/eComStation FAT32 installable filesystem driver and UFAT32 support DLL source, attributed to Henk Kelder and netlabs.
Aaron Lawrence native Pascal/OS2 graphical text editor with find/replace, printing, autosave and language resources, preserved as original source.
OS/2 continuation of the eFTE/FTE folding editor with text buffers, syntax highlighting, configuration and native console/PM integration.
Jim Wilcoxson's independent C emulation of Prime 50-Series minicomputers, with disk/MAGSAV boot, R-mode save-image loading, peripheral support, tracing and PRIMOS operation.
Jan Jaeger's separately authored Prime 50-Series implementation, with CPU instruction groups, disk/tape, AMLC networking, configuration and debugger support.
Preserved Daniel Seagraves hardware-level Texas Instruments Explorer 1 emulator, including Raven microcoded CPU, NuBus, memory, NUPI storage, SIB display/input and SDL frontend.
Robert Martin's Lua/Codea implementation of a 4K-word, 12-bit PDP-8 with interactive front panel, ASR-33 teletype, paper-tape reader/punch, debugger-like controls and historical tape programs.
JavaScript PDP-11/40 system emulator with MMU, registers, clock, terminal, RK05 disk model, disassembler and debug UI; loads and exports disk-image buffers and is documented running Unix V6.

Compact, independent browser PDP-11 emulator implementing kernel/user registers and memory mapping, traps, interrupts, console and RK05 disk I/O, with a disassembler and runnable Unix-oriented HTML frontend.
Paul Nankervis's JavaScript 36-bit DECsystem-10 KI10 emulator, with floating-point, device I/O, front-panel controls, diagnostics and RP03 disk configuration for TOPS-10 v6.03A.

Substantial C++ Win32 emulator/debugger for the Soviet Elektronika MS-0511 UKNC dual-processor educational machine, with CPU/PPU, memory controllers, video, disks, tapes, sound, disassembly and console debugging.

C++20 implementation of the B1710 microinstruction processor and B1700 bit-addressable architecture, paired with microcode debugger/disassembler, MIL and S-language assemblers and a historical tape reader.
Browser-based reconstruction of the Burroughs B500 decimal/BCD computer, with processor operations, console panel, asynchronous worker execution, card/printer/tape I/O and a disk module.

Source-preservation and browser integration project for Research Unix V4 through V7, combining recovered historical C/PDP-11 source and media with an educational TypeScript frontend, source overlays and a Paul Nankervis PDP-11 bridge.
Jeremy Hall's Go implementation of the 16-bit Data General Nova CPU, interrupt/device framework, console, clock, loaders and disassembler, with instruction/logic tests and example command tools.

Interactive native CPC star-field demo by Diego Freniche, with separate entity lifecycle, star generation, directional physics and rendering systems; includes keyboard direction and hyperspace effects.
Reusable ZX Spectrum 48K workbench containing its own machine-cycle Z80 core/disassembler, Spectrum memory and ULA/tape/audio model, source-level debugger, macro assembler and desktop/CLI frontends.

Host-side tape/snapshot conversion and playback tool paired with a native Z80 turbo-loader for real Spectrum 48K/128K machines. Handles TAP/TZX/snapshots, pulse generation, WAV output, compression and optional Qt UI.

Reusable batch and Z80 loader pipeline that extracts game blocks, rearranges/crops SCREEN$ data, compresses with ZX0, and packages replacement compressed TAP/TZX or disk loaders. Per-game configurations and multilevel disk loaders are included.

Native Z80 assembly sequel for CPC 464 by Daniel Saura Martínez and Enrique Vidal Cayuela. Contains modular game/menu/entity managers, collision and physics systems, power-ups, sprites, level maps and Arkos music assets.
Original 2019 native CPC game by Enrique Vidal Cayuela and Daniel Saura Martínez, with Z80 player/entity/enemy logic, keyboard/game state loop, sprite animation and two dozen Tiled maps.

Native CPC 464 game created for an Automatic Reasoning course and CPCRetroDev 2016 by Cristina Rivera, Miguel Sancho and Fernando Verdejo, with map-based movement, enemies, knives, scoring and custom pathfinding.
Native BBC Micro four-player Riichi Mahjong implementation in one substantial BeebAsm source, with Mode 7 tile display, human controls, computer opponents, scoring and practice hints.

Stephen Scott’s remaster of his 1993 BBC Micro arcade game, retaining BBC BASIC source while upgrading from MODE 5 to MODE 2, graphics/sound, bugs and late-level difficulty. Includes a BeebAsm disk-packaging script.

Self-contained JavaScript browser assembler/editor with symbolic two-pass NMOS 6502 assembly, undocumented opcodes, multiple sources and ORG regions, listing/symbol output and bootable BBC DFS SSD generation.

Long-running native 6502 Scorched Earth-style multiplayer artillery game by Tomasz Pecko and Pawel Kalinowski, with deformable terrain, weapon shop, computer opponents, POKEY audio and Atari 5200 support plus a work-in-progress C64 port.

Recovered 1990–1992 SICK graphics/music demo, preserving a byte-exact RISC OS source tree and readable BBC BASIC V with inline ARM2 assembler. This is source restoration of the released v2.02 demo, recovered from PackDir SCSI-drive backups, not a new emulation wrapper.

Recovered final 1993 working tree of SICK !Tertis v2.05, including original application, assets, source/build scripts and readable detokenised sources. A distinct game from the authors’ Bananaland demo.

Three standalone modern Python tools recover BBC BASIC V text, PackDir archives, and ADFS floppy images from Acorn RISC OS media. Implementation handles inline ARM assembler tokens, line-number references, LZW, metadata and load/execute address preservation.

Preservation collection of System Interrupt demos I–V with actual recovered BBC BASIC/inline ARM implementation for Demo V v1.01, dated 5 February 1989. Only Demo V qualifies as source recovery; I–IV are contextual released binaries.

Author-released source recovery of Hugo Fiennes’s Archimedes bulletin-board software, last used around 1994. Substantive server, file/mailbase, transfer protocols, editors and ARM modules survive with historical Acorn build scripts.

Reverse-engineered specification, Python parser/applier and encoder for K. Higashide’s 1992 BdifSet .bfd binary patch format. Recovered from disassembly of Human68k 68000 binaries, with bidirectional delta operations and CRC handling implemented.

X68000 floppy formatter lineage: original personal utility preserved in fdformat and redesigned FDFORMAT2 implements parallel per-drive state machines, physical formatting, BPB/FAT/root-directory/minimal-IPL logical formatting and sector sliding. Represented as one project lineage.

Python decryption and patching implementation for early Macintosh PACE-protected software, explaining on-the-fly self-modifying decryption, bad-block floppy checks and debugger/timing checks. Multiple per-title scripts recover inspectable 68000 program bytes and alter protection checks.

Compact native Macintosh boot disk driver implemented in C with m68k assembly entry/header shim. Implements Apple partition scanning, registering/mounting HFS volumes, SCSI READ(10)/chunked WRITE(10), DriveStatus and drive icon in a position-independent raw driver.

Clean-room C++20/raylib reconstruction of Lander behavior using Mark Moxon’s annotated Archimedes ARM analysis as specification. Implements terrain, ship dynamics, mouse polar control, rendering and collision rather than executing an embedded original CPU.

Native classic Macintosh FreeCell homebrew with full C game rules, deterministic Microsoft-compatible numbered deals, undo and Toolbox window/menu/event handling. Original source implementation, not claimed decompilation.

Classic Macintosh native pendulum simulator with C numerical integration, configurable angle/velocity/resistance/length/gravity, Toolbox event handling, preferences dialogs and drawing. Original homebrew application, not source reconstruction.

Regional Super Bomberman reconstruction with a remade source/asset build, decoded graphics, levels, DBoot songs and samples, plus bugfix/debug configurations. This is the original SNES game, not an emulator wrapper.
Work-in-progress annotated reconstruction of Japanese v1.0, including banked CPU code, reset/WRAM logic, symbols and a substantial independently decoded SPC sound engine.

Game-specific SNES disassembly in Yoshifanatic1’s ROM framework, with its own bank/routine macros, native memory maps, SPC audio engine and original-ROM asset extraction/reassembly workflow. CPU reset/main/NMI routines and explicit compressed SPC engine are present; only USA supported despite generic multi-region menu entries.

Game-specific SNES disassembly in Yoshifanatic1’s ROM framework, with its own bank/routine macros, native memory maps, SPC audio engine and original-ROM asset extraction/reassembly workflow. Read native CPU register initialization, bank macros and SPC source. Only USA ROM map exists; extraction explicitly rejects PAL despite assembly menu scaffolding.

Game-specific SNES disassembly in Yoshifanatic1’s ROM framework, with its own bank/routine macros, native memory maps, SPC audio engine and original-ROM asset extraction/reassembly workflow. Read native reset, lives/level-state initialization and bank reconstruction. USA is the documented supported release.

Game-specific SNES disassembly in Yoshifanatic1’s ROM framework, with its own bank/routine macros, native memory maps, SPC audio engine and original-ROM asset extraction/reassembly workflow. Large bank/routine source, text tables and decoded SPC engine are present. Only USA map/extraction supported; JP/EU/French/German assembly menu options are framework scaffolding, not evidence of completed support.

Partial multi-version disassembly of the creature-collecting RPG, with extensive reconstructed system, battle, script and graphics components. English translation lives on a separate patch branch; this record reviews the default source branch.
Partial two-version reconstruction of Network Adventure Bugsite with reconstructed bytecode VM, game filesystem, window manager, text and banking components, plus Python format/assembly utilities.
Bank-by-bank RGBDS disassembly of the original accelerometer-based GBC title, with native reset/interrupt vectors, header, all 64 assembly banks and checksum manifests.
Annotated partial disassembly of the compact, mapperless Game Boy puzzle game; regional assembly generates US and Japanese ROMs and supports study of the level-49 kill screen.

Deliberately partial source reconstruction sufficient for translation, including text engine, HUD, status screen and save routines. German translation with variable-width font lives on de branch and is not the reviewed default branch.
Standalone shared tooling extracted from Pokémon disassemblies, with RGBDS map parsing/free-space analysis, source/symbol utilities and 1bpp/2bpp-to-PNG asset conversion.

Matching decompilation of original PlayStation SDK libraries, with substantive reconstructed sound sequencing, SPU and compression functions, version-conditional implementations and object/library comparison infrastructure.

Readable C reconstruction of original Legend of Mana main executable and 17 overlays for US and Japan. Pinned README claims full byte-identical links and recompressed overlay binaries for both releases, while original SDK library assembly is retained.

Ryan C. Gordon’s independent OS/2 compatibility implementation loads OS/2 NE/LX executables and maps their APIs to Linux libraries. Pinned lx_loader.c validates modules and native/doscalls.c implements OS/2 calls; this is substantive reusable compatibility software.

Joel Ek’s unofficial patch project for Blizzard’s WarCraft: Orcs & Humans. Actual JavaScript patch definitions contain version-specific x86 addresses and assembly bytes; the C DOS patcher checks, applies and restores binary slices.

Preserved RSXNTDJ 1.5.1 source distribution, including Win32 runtime/startup code, GCC wrapper, libraries, RSXIDE and examples. gccw32.c configures RSXNTDJ includes/libraries and invokes GCC; rsxide.c implements project and target handling.

M. Kajihara’s Professional Music Driver source release, preserved in a mirror. Includes PMD sound drivers, MC music compiler, PMP player and IBM-PC variants. Actual PMD.ASM playback initialization and OPTASM/OPTLINK build batches were inspected.

Reusable Python tools for Windows 3.1 binary research: derive NE segment maps from DOSBox memory, convert CPU coverage into IDA/Lighthouse addresses, and reconstruct OPTLOADER-compressed executables. optloader.py contains an explicit modeled loader and decompression logic.
Japheth’s source collection of DOSAlloc, DosMonW, GDIStat, Notify, SetMode and Share. Inspected implementation reads USER/GDI heap status and hooks DOS calls, with C++ UI and 16-bit assembly sources.
Josh Patterson’s native retro-developed Windows 3.11 HTTP server. C++ Winsock implementation binds/listens from XML configuration, with a custom segmented-memory manager and static-file server UI.

Onitama/onion software’s original NEC PC-9801 archive contains historical games, BASIC sources, C utilities, Advanced SOUP compiler and assembly graphics routines. Inspected Crazy World BASIC gameplay, ASC C compiler entry/parser setup and .8086 graphics-bank assembly.

Ronny Wester’s circa-1994 Cyberdogs source release, preserved in LibreGamesArchive. dogs.pas contains the application and mission flow; game.pas implements movement, collisions, enemies and bullets, with source units for input, graphics and sound.
Restored and adapted Qualitas PIF editor for osFree Janus. Original 1992/1993 C source implements standard/advanced PIF property UI and binary PIF loading/saving.
Qualitas MAXEdit configuration-file editor source adapted as Janus System Editor. Actual historical C source implements MDI document windows, configuration paths and INI/PRO editing.

Self-contained native Windows 3.x Notepad adaptation derived from Wine Notepad. C source implements file operations, editor state and Win16 API integration; README explicitly describes removal of Win32-specific dependencies.
Wine Clock adapted to native Windows 3.x for Janus. Actual C drawing code creates analog hands/ticks and digital/time display; repository includes its own resources and makefile.

Aaron Ardiri and Michael Ethetton's Liberty 1.3.1 source archive preserves a reusable original Game Boy emulator written for Palm handhelds, including 68k CPU/video/sound code and a ROM-to-PDB converter.
Hilary Cheng and David Schmenk's Apple II/IIe emulator for Palm PDAs combines a substantial hand-written 68k 6502 interpreter, memory-mapped Apple I/O, video and disk-image conversion tools.
Bodo Wenzel's formerly PalmBoy Game Boy emulator source is preserved with a 68k execution core, video/memory implementation, VFS, saved states and multilingual Palm resources.

The implemented portion of Patrick Barron's planned UNIVAC 1100 emulator is a usable C image-inspection toolkit. uimage2strings unpacks paired 36-bit words from disk-pack images and decodes 9-bit ASCII or 6-bit FIELDATA for external analysis.
A reusable TypeScript PDP-1 interpreter with 18-bit memory/registers, instruction groups, console switches, paper-tape loading and vector display, presented through an Angular front panel.

Paul Kimpel's detailed General Precision LGP-21 implementation reconstructs the processor, rotating fixed-head disk memory, arithmetic mechanisms, control panel, Flexowriter and Tally paper-tape devices from machine manuals.

Kenneth Gober's C# SEL 810 suite includes a substantial processor/memory/console model, TCP peripheral links, tape server, BASIC tape construction, loader-aware tape dumper and control-flow-assisted disassembler.

Historical TRIPOS BCPL operating-system and tool sources shared with permission from Tim King, covering the shell and utilities plus Nova, PDP-11, LSI4 and Motorola 68000 assembly/compiler support. This is the historical lineage underlying early AmigaDOS, not an AmigaDOS replacement.

Peter Onon's Elliott 803 emulator models 39-bit arithmetic and processor operations alongside an unusually physical operator experience: charger, contactor, hours-run counter, sound and console wiring.

Andrew Herbert's maintained extension of Lee Wittenberg's EDSAC emulator implements machine orders/arithmetic and tape-style I/O, adding tracing, binary store upload and execution limits for the EDSAC Replica Project.

Josh Dersch's independently written Python implementation of a standard 4K-word PDP-8 includes instruction dispatch, memory, console Teletype and paper-tape loading; it is broader than a single program wrapper.

Maintained native 6502 assembler for SpartaDOS X and BW-DOS, restoring Marek Goderski's historical Fast Assembler and adding parser, arithmetic, diagnostics and memory-management fixes. Reviewed FAMAIN's multi-pass assembly driver and FAPARSE implementation establish substantive tooling.

Original native Atari sliding-tile puzzle from ABBUC 2021: combines colored tiles, with deterministic progression rather than a random generator. Inspected INCMAIN initializes GTIA colors, input and game transitions; the source set includes Atari computer and 5200 entry points.

Historical Atari Kermit terminal and reliable-transfer implementation maintained in ca65-compatible source. Its large implementation documents Apple-to-C64-to-Atari ancestry, Atari CIO/850 I/O conversion and decades of transfer and terminal fixes, rather than only shipping binaries.

Native Atari port of Juan J. Martinez's MSX single-screen platformer, written in WNF and 6502 assembly. Inspected night-knight.wnf implements hardware setup, game state, enemy dispatch, lives and PAL/NTSC timing, with 80 level data files and sprite/runtime modules.

Substantial native Atari timber-chopping arcade game, also identified as Timberman in source and assets. The 96 KB assembly implementation includes player state, branch/playfield display lists, PAL/NTSC timing, difficulty and RMT music integration.

Native Amstrad CPC shooter implemented in C with CPCtelera. Inspected game.c contains player/bullet/entity state, health display, six connected maps, enemies, bases and screen redraw logic; source assets, entity and animation modules are present.

Original C64 maze arcade game by Stefan Wessels, featuring generated mazes, guards, boost/shoot mechanics and survival/escape modes. Reviewed game.c implements game state and loop; maze/player/monster/platform source modules provide substantive native implementation.

Native C64 arcade flying/shooting game written in XC=BASIC by Csaba Fekete with graphics by Daniel Fekete. Reviewed main BASIC source implements raster interrupts, SID effects, joystick movement, scrolling, wave transitions and collision/action modules.

Native C64 brick-smashing puzzle/action game in C by Johan Berntsson. Reviewed main.c implements native screen/game mechanics and brick scoring; the 2020 revision added multi-brick bonuses, cursor controls and instructions, followed by a cc65-format update.

Binary-patching and replacement-loader project for C64 Wasteland, moving disk I/O to IDE64 and separating saves, fixing PAL/NTSC timing and turbo-speed behavior. Reviewed wasteland_fix.asm patches fixed-address game routines, requesters and interrupt vectors, and incorporates loader/fileops modules.

Client/server space-game proof of concept with a native C64 assembly client and Java server. Reviewed vortex.s initializes DHCP/UDP, login, interrupts, sprites and music; server Universe.java creates the shared map, entities, planetoids and destructible scenery.

Native classic-Mac network terminal with Telnet IAC negotiation, VT100/VT220/xterm rendering, Finger, multiple sessions and settings. Independent application from the author's Geomys Gopher client; variants remain one project.

Modern C implementation of a Macintosh MDS-style 68000 assembler, linker, resource compiler and MacBinary writer. Handles A5 globals, instruction encoding, branch sizing and classic project/resource dialects.

Dependency-free C disk-image tool implementing classic Macintosh MFS/HFS allocation, catalogs/B-trees, Finder folder metadata, resource forks and MacBinary import/export. It edits actual disk structures rather than wrapping an emulator.

Restoration and Retro68 adaptation of Erny Tontlinger's 1992 serial-terminal source distribution, preserving C interpreter, serial I/O, capture/scrolling, MacBinary and X/Y/ZModem/QuickB transfers with THINK C/MPW artifacts.

Coherent four-utility suite for Star Fighter 3000 game data: SFToSpr graphics conversion, FednetCmp compression, SFSkyEdit skies and SFColours palette mapping. Contains native GUI code, data backends and tests, kept as one suite.

Command-line parser and geometry converter for compressed/raw Chocks Away and Extra Missions model/index files into Wavefront OBJ/MTL. Source includes primitive decoding, material/color mapping and normals generation.

Portable 32/64-bit MDX playback library derived from GORRY's MXDRVg C conversion of disassembled X68000 MXDRV.X and X68Sound chip emulation. Adds isolated contexts, register/key-on APIs and sample WAV/player frontends.

Preserved/normalized source of Zenji Nishikawa's Z-MUSIC 2.08 driver/compiler/player plus rebuilt MZL 2.08e sources and later patched variants. Repository documents matching 2.08e from base sources and unified sources intended to reproduce original executables.
Modernization of Mitsuky's WebXpression native Human68k browser, adding UTF-8 to Shift-JIS conversion and TLS support while retaining HTML parsing, images/cache/history and 68k display routines.
