AMOS BASIC audio editor/loop processor with IFF/AIFF/WAV/MP3/OctaMED handling, multichannel arrangements and realtime effects. Actual current ASCII source, historical AMOS versions, custom 68k music extension and Windows VST bridge are included.

Original small-memory Amiga Image ViewEr 1.7 source with C UI/screen setup and 68000 assembly GIF/IFF decoding, scaling, Floyd-Steinberg dithering and display routines. GPL re-release preserves substantive 1994 native application.

Native ARM assembly Revision 2024 64KB demo with sequence/music synchronization, particle systems, palette/graphics code and packed loader. Complete effects implementation and asset build scripts establish more than a binary release.

Native ARM assembly stereoscopic/anaglyph production with dual-eye dot tunnel, 3D scene projection, scroller, music and sequence assets. Deadline 2023 production distinct from later Push despite shared build/framework code.

Original C64 rail shooter in 6502 assembly plus source-derived portable C simulation, SDL frontend and substantive native Archimedes port. Archimedes-specific rendering, input, sound/synthesis and ARM assembly support share a coherent game core.

A native Neo Geo Pocket Color homebrew reinterpretation of Atari's Asteroids. Its own C entity pool implements rotating ship sprites, thrust, asteroid splitting, aimed UFO fire, collisions, waves and flash high scores; it is neither an arcade CPU wrapper nor a recovered Atari binary.

Native C adaptation of Konami's 1982 arcade maze shooter for Neo Geo Pocket Color. Separate game, map, screen and entity modules implement keys, treasure, teleport zones, doors and enemy spawn/chase/patrol behavior, rather than emulating the arcade board.

A native Neo Geo Pocket Color Frogger adaptation with implemented scrolling traffic, logs, diving turtles, homes, timer, fly bonus and pond progression. Source variants support arcade portrait and Coleco-style VFD presentations within one project lineage.

Original Neo Geo Pocket Color homebrew inspired by Pengo. C modules implement authored grids, sliding ice blocks, crush rules, hatching and pursuing Sno-Bees, wall stuns, lives and level timing. README explicitly says no original Pengo code, artwork, audio or data is used.

Native C Neo Geo Pocket Color adaptation of Q*bert with pyramid tile states, Coily pursuit, falling balls, rescue discs, rotated D-pad movement and high-score entry. It packages its own NGPC ROM rather than running an arcade emulator.

A clean-room-labelled Neo Geo Pocket Color homage to 1982 Blue Print. Native C modules implement searching houses, carrying machine parts, chasing bombs, a timed rope scene, blueprint completion and monster defeat; authored maze data is compiled into the game.

A substantial Eclipse Theia/Electron IDE dedicated to VUEngine and Nintendo Virtual Boy development. Custom TypeScript/React extension implements project-aware code generation, hardware-specific editors and build integration, including a layer/frame pixel editor with tile grids. Distinct development tool from the already tracked VUEngine runtime.

Native Motorola 6809 Vectrex assembly game with title, logo, gameplay and game-over states. Gameplay updates a paddle, accelerated ball, enemies, missed-enemy markers, particles, score and screen timing, with Vectrex BIOS vector drawing.

Linux C host utility implementing Sega Saturn USB DataLink packet/checksum and FTDI transport logic. It can dump the BIOS, read/write Saturn memory and upload/execute homebrew, enabling native console development and inspection without the original Windows-only software.

Reusable Sega Saturn emulator for Nintendo Wii derived from Yabause Wii and selected Yaba Sanshiro improvements. Substantial fork includes Hollywood GPU rendering and its own SH-2-to-PowerPC dynamic recompiler, with dual SH-2 machine state, rather than being a game-specific emulation wrapper.

Native Sega Saturn C 3D platformer/demo built on Jo Engine and SGL. A substantial main.c implements player movement/collision, enemies, powerups, title and level selection, camera modes, object viewing and an interactive map builder, with Saturn texture/map assets and Jo entry point.

Cross-platform Go command-line tool for constructing Sega Saturn homebrew CUE sheets from an ISO and numbered audio track files. Actual implementation locates tracks, identifies WAVE/BINARY formats, sorts by track number, formats pregaps and writes the cue file.

Standalone C++ disassembler for 16-bit DOS MZ and COM images. It uses Capstone for instruction decoding and implements its own binary loading and experimental recursive traversal and cross-reference discovery.

Reusable PC emulator and reverse-engineering environment that records real-mode DOS execution, builds control-flow graphs and emits C# override projects. This is the maintained C# continuation of the original Java Spice86.

C# disassembler and analyst for 16-bit NE binaries, originally designed for MajorBBS and Worldgroup modules but also supporting general Win16 EXE/DLL files. Enhanced analysis resolves imports, relocation references, strings and compiler idioms.
C++ libopcodes-based executable disassembler derived from swdisasm. It parses DOS MZ/LE/LX linear executable structures and emits AT&T/GAS-style assembly intended to support analysis and reassembly.

Alone in the Dark-family research tools: LIFE/TRACK script disassemblers, PAK extraction/repacking and background export, live DOSBox memory/variable views, and recorded-session playback for inspection.
Small but substantive C++ disassembler for 16-bit DOS MZ programs, following branches from initial CS:IP to separate reachable instructions from data and allowing function annotations.
Wine-derived compatibility layer that runs Windows 1.x–3.x executables on 64-bit Windows using CPU emulation, Win16-to-Win32 API conversion, DOS services and handle translation.

Open-source release of Topten Software Windows 3.0 emulator. Sharp86 CPU emulation loads Win16 applications while implemented APIs are mapped to modern Windows calls; includes debugging and NE module/heap management.

Independent SDL engine for Ultima VI, Martian Dreams and The Savage Empire, using original data with reconstructed game logic, conversation interpretation and Lua game scripts. This repository is the standalone engine before its integration into ScummVM.

SDL2 C reimplementation of Cosmo’s Cosmic Adventure with actors, collision, effects, level/container loading, audio and UI. Address-style variables and decoded actor dispatch remain in recovered engine logic.
Native SDL engine recreated from the original Titus the Fox/Moktar games, with ported movement/game behavior, level/sprite decoding, OPL playback and configurable data layout.

Attempt to translate Interplay Dragon Wars’ 16-bit real-mode assembly engine to portable C. Includes annotated original-engine disassembly and reconstructed resource, script, UI, party and rendering subsystems.
C and NASM reconstruction of the 1987 DOS BARD.EXE, with reconstructed root and overlay modules and a reproducibility-focused Microsoft C 4.0/LINK 3.51 build/compare pipeline.

C and x86 assembly reconstruction of Might and Magic III: Isles of Terra including resident code, VROOMM overlays, data and script/gameplay modules. Build tooling reconstructs and compares the original packed executable.

A reusable Rust implementation of the InfoAge UNIVAC 1219 machine and its programming tools. The shared crate implements 18-bit register/memory execution, instructions, arithmetic, I/O and tape handling, with CLI assembler/emulator/disassembler frontends and a browser UI. It is a substantive implementation inspired by Duane Craps’s earlier tools, rather than a packaged museum image.

A native UNIVAC 1219 assembly implementation of a 32-bit RISC-V interpreter, with OCaml decoding/code-generation/fuzzing tools and a C build environment. This lets modern C programs compile to RISC-V instructions and execute through an interpreter on the historical 18-bit machine. Its opcode dispatch and arithmetic/memory/branch handlers are present as UNIVAC assembly sources.

The actual K&R C Lilith emulator Andreas Borchert developed in 1983 to bootstrap ETH Modula-2 onto a Perkin-Elmer 3220 running Unix VII. The repository preserves the execution engine, loader, storage, Unix service bridge and tracing code. This is historical development software preservation, with known period-compiler dependencies, rather than a new browser emulator.

Preserved ETH Zürich C18 Modula-2 multipass compiler sources, derived from the 1981 compiler and adapted at Ulm in 1983 for a Lilith emulator under Unix VII. The repository contains actual compiler passes, symbols, code-generation modules, build recipes and steady-state C18 binaries, so it is a source-preservation/toolchain record separate from the emulator that runs it.

A reconstruction of the 1988 Norsk Data ND-120 3202D CPU board from original design documents, first represented in Logisim and now maintained as Verilog. Includes CPU/decode gate arrays, PAL translations, microcode, MMU and bus devices, simulation harnesses and FPGA board integrations. This is a hardware/firmware reconstruction distinct from the catalogued nd100x and nd500x software emulators.

A C# TMS9900 instruction-level development simulator with a Forth-like interactive monitor, assembler, memory access, single stepping and status/workspace-register state. Source implements the architecture’s RAM-backed register workspace, context switching, flags and instruction dispatch, with tests and usable assembly examples; it deliberately models the CPU rather than recreating a complete TI 990 system.

A source-grounded new reconstruction of NASA MSC’s lost VIEW visualization program from its surviving reports, plots and film output. Fixed-form period-style Fortran implements trajectory, projection, spacecraft and celestial line drawing; a modern shell compiles it for live browser presentation. The project explicitly labels conjectures, modern substitutions and restomod additions rather than claiming recovered original source or an exact UNIVAC executable.

IBM’s Python implementation of 3270 terminal interaction, including a TN3270 data-stream engine, zti terminal UI and ati automation compatibility layer. The code implements terminal orders, screen state, EBCDIC handling, session management and protocol negotiation, providing reusable access to historical mainframe interfaces rather than merely launching another emulator.

A static JavaScript implementation of IBM 3270 and 5250 terminal protocols for mainframe and AS/400/IBM i access. Browser modules implement datastream parsing, fields, screen state, TN3270E/TN5250E negotiation and ENPTUI behavior; connection uses an external TCP-to-WebSocket bridge. Substantive parsers and protocol tests distinguish it from a skin around an existing emulator.

Preserved and maintained PilRC source for compiling Palm resource scripts into application resource data, including bitmap/font processing and optional preview UI. The implementation includes the real resource parser/serializer, language/type tables, bitmap encoders and font tools, with Palm examples. This is the long-running original Palm tool lineage, not another Palm SDK mirror.

The historical pilot-link C libraries and command-line conduits for communicating with Palm handhelds from Unix-like systems. Implements Palm DLP and lower-level link/socket protocols plus record packers, synchronizers and install/backup/debug tools. This is an independent original protocol/tooling lineage, not the already catalogued modern JavaScript palm-sync or palm-pdb projects.

Original 2016 platform/action game source by Juan J. Martinez for the ZX Spectrum 48K, with room data, enemies, collectibles, keyboard/joystick selection and a bespoke loader. This is the native game, not an emulator wrapper.

Simon Springett’s 1984 ZX Spectrum BASIC shepherding game preserved as readable source with tape/audio artifacts and a source-to-tape utility. Shepherd, sheep chain and pursuing wolf are simulated by the game itself.
Text adventure independently implemented in portable C and then hand-ported to Z80 for CP/M and the 48K Spectrum. A turn-limited lighthouse crisis supports inventory/object puzzles and two solutions.
Mouse-aimed native Spectrum Next arcade defense game. Players eliminate approaching Jeffs using delayed explosions, charge management and numerous bonuses while advancing through areas.

Native single-control-key Spectrum game with levels, collectibles, doors, teleporters, slowdown effects and a countdown. Full game source includes source-level trace/debug support and designer utilities.
Original Spectrum action/puzzle game built around integer-optimized flocking/Boids behavior. The player manipulates levels to clear a swarm under a time limit.
Native ecological hunting/puzzle game in which grass spreads, grazers eat/reproduce/starve and a hunter intervenes in an evolving world. One source tree supports Spectrum, C64, MSX and Master System.
Native slalom/obstacle arcade game for the Spectrum, also ported to Amstrad CPC 464. Shared C code switches hardware/rendering and keyboard backends between the machines.
Alfonso Saavedra’s Metroid-inspired Spectrum fan game using La Churrera. The player explores a spaceship and carries fourteen eggs one at a time to an incubator before reaching the control room.
Original compact Spectrum timing game: activate a moving chopper at log markers, earn round scores and progress through logs while maintaining a high score.
Wordle-style five-letter word puzzle implemented for the ZX80, ZX81 and Spectrum/Timex family. Six guesses receive positional/letter feedback and feed a running score.
Native Amstrad CPC platform/action game by Samuel Bolanowski and Atharuddin Syed, built with CPCtelera and a duck/bubble-themed character and enemy set.

Native Worms-like turn-based artillery game for CPC 464/6128 with destructible procedural terrain, teams, hotseat/CPU opponents, multiple weapons and persistent score storage. Includes attract-demo programs.

Raylib-based Windows/Linux/Web restoration port of Richard Phipps’s 2008 Chaos Groove, itself a remake of Julian Gollop’s Spectrum Chaos: Battle of the Wizards. Preserves native board/spell gameplay rather than wrapping a Spectrum CPU emulator.

Reservoir Gods' original Atari ST vegetable-juggling game source, identified by the HOTPOT.PRJ header as Double Juggle Vegatabobble: This Is Vegetable Juggling (2002). The repository currently contains the Hotpot implementation rather than a separate new game per directory.

Original MIDI rhythm game for Atari ST: one or two players guide dragons to collect notes while the ST sound chip plays selected MIDI tracks. Actual gameplay, MIDI parsing and native GEM graphics are present.
Monochrome endless runner written from scratch for Atari ST, with jump, kick and slide mechanics, custom raster/PSG routines, interrupt vectors and keyboard/mouse drivers.
Native Atari GEM adaptation of John Elliott’s C/GEM 2048, retaining his sliding-block board logic and GEM front end while adding an m68k Atari build and NatFeats support.
Native Atari ST arcade game by Daniel Bahrami and Scott Charles, with moving platforms, ball physics/collision, music, custom interrupt/input handling and double-buffered rendering.
Original Atari ST typing/rescue game whose model tracks swimmer movement, word rows, score and decorative state; includes native raster, PSG, interrupts and input code plus module tests.
Ataxx-style RISC OS desktop board game in RiscLua, including full board/rules classes and native Toolbox wrapper integration. Source and a bundled standalone runtime application are present.
Gavin Cawley’s Centipede-like game, begun on an Archimedes A410/1 in the late 1980s and revisited from backup. Includes earlier character-based gameplay and newer desktop/sprite implementation.
Native C/OSLib recreation of Lode Runner for RISC OS, with destructible terrain, climbing/digging, enemy navigation, sprite rendering, WIMP integration, configurable scaling and saved level progress.
Stephen Fryatt’s desktop Peg Solitaire game, with original untokenised BBC BASIC WIMP event handling, drag/board interaction, resource files and a reproducible-source packaging layout.

Playable Space Invaders-style shooting sample for X68000/X68000Z, intentionally simple for learning native game programming. Scene, enemy/player/bullet state, sprites, input and sound are actual C/assembly implementation.

Bare-metal X68000 wireframe battle-racing game with local one/two-player modes, three tracks, drift/boost/slipstream mechanics, fixed-step simulation and double-buffered display. Boots from XDF without Human68k runtime.
Original Ludum Dare 40 Amiga game built around Amiga C Engine, including gameplay state, map/square simulation, HUD/scores and native blitter-based graphics.

Preserved Soliton Klondike/Freecell source by Kai Nickel, Dirk Stoecker and contributors, with MUI card-game widgets, profiles/statistics, datatype/cardset loading and native Amiga-family build recipes.

Original arcade platformer with upward scrolling, timed stages, enemy bounces, dash/boost movement, unlockable skins, high scores and MML music. game.c implements concrete player/entity collision, spawning, level progress and native Game Boy video/audio control.

Fan-made native Game Boy demake of Evoland. Source implements tile-map movement, player sword animation, chest activation and progressive controls/game features. This is a work-in-progress original implementation rather than an original-binary interpreter.

Native Game Boy Advance Pump It Up-style rhythm simulator consuming StepMania SSC charts. Judge.cpp implements timing windows, hold judging and score feedback; SongScene orchestrates native sprites, audio, chart play and multiplayer/hardware effects. It does not emulate an arcade CPU.

Unfinished original Game Boy Color exploration/platform game developed in 2011–2012. next.c handles camera and banked world tile streaming; player.c implements acceleration, jumping, swimming and underwater movement against chunk-based maps.

Native Numberlink-style Game Boy/Game Boy Color puzzle game. Concrete C board representation, tile drawing and connection logic are backed by assembly save, effects, level manager and sound subsystems, with generated puzzle packs.

Native Game Boy Color flood-fill puzzle game with a randomized 14×14 board, limited moves, palette selection, win/loss scenes, transitions and sound. Source uses CGB tile attributes and palette registers rather than emulated predecessor code.

Original native Game Boy top-down pirate action game with anchor melee, cannon shooting, enemies, collisions, level state, pause/menu transitions and hUGE/CBT-FX audio integration. main.c and hero.c contain concrete hardware-facing game logic.

Native Game Boy Color falling-piece pet-building puzzle game with multiple game types, special pieces, hinting, variable difficulty, music, statistics and two-player link-cable play. gameplay.c implements drop progression, linked-player game-over handling and input/state updates.

Native Mega Drive music-cartridge software, with track browser, ordered/shuffle playback, on-screen visualizations and custom cartridge LED-array support. Main C program uses native VDP/joypad routines; XGM driver manages the Z80 sound processor.

Original native 68000 Sega Genesis speedrunning adventure demo with randomized elevator/floor connectivity and scripted conversations/events. Main X68 source builds native vectors/header/init and game systems; ActionScript routines implement scene-exit resolution and event handling.

Native NES homebrew recreation of Undertale’s Lesser Dog battle. Assembly main source initializes PPU/APU/RAM and includes custom graphics, text, input, coroutine/generator and battle/menu modules. It creates a real NES ROM rather than wrapping the PC game in a CPU interpreter.

Original computer-themed NES RPG made for Game Off 2021. C main controls desktop/window-style UI and game state; dungeon source creates sector layouts, tracks completion and loads entities, supported by MMC3 mapper and native assembly runtime.

Native GBA Lua game framework built from parts of the author’s BlindJump C++ engine. Concrete BPCoreEngine.cpp embeds Lua APIs and allocator; gba_platform.cpp accesses GBA hardware. Lua manifest/build script packages resources/scripts behind a native engine ROM to enable small games.

Reusable C++ toolkit for analyzing 8086 DOS MZ executables and comparing instruction-level reconstructions even when routine and data layout changes. Includes header, map, signature, pointer and duplicate-code tools plus an instruction decoder and analysis library.

Java/Swing interactive disassembler, binary format analyzer and hex editor. Includes concrete DOS COM loading/disassembly and MZ header/relocation readers alongside PE, ELF, Mach-O and media-format analyzers.

Original Qualitas 386SWAT protected-mode debugger source archive with extensive assembly, instruction decoding, source-symbol tools, VCPI/DPMI integration and Windows VxD components. Supports debugging native protected-mode and virtual-8086 clients.

Source release and continuation of Deb16f, Deb32f and Deb16fw, a family of native DOS DPMI and 16-bit Windows debuggers originating in 1992. Provides protected/real-mode breakpoint handling and symbol/file support.

Reusable Python tools connecting GDB/pygdb to DOSBox guest registers and memory, processing instruction traces, decoding selected DOS system calls and substituting multi-instruction patterns with readable pseudo-operations.

Small Python implementation for locating early Microsoft CodeView NB00 data appended to DOS MZ executables and reading module/public-symbol subsections. Intended for symbols produced by Microsoft LINK 3.x through 5.03.

Preserved OS2Linux source library implementing OS/2 C APIs on Linux, allowing applications with available source to be recompiled and linked natively. Contains file, process, memory, module, semaphore, pipe and resource API modules.
Preserved Ivan Skytte Jørgensen OS2API library mapping OS/2 DOSCALL APIs onto Win32. Recompiled OS/2 program source links against OS2API.LIB to execute natively under Windows NT.
Original 1995 assembly unpacker for programs that started as DOS COM images and were packed into EXE form. Uses Intel 386 debug registers and real-mode execution to recover the unpacked image.

Reconstruction of Heinz Hombergs DOS-Expander 4.0 file manager and program menu, with Borland Pascal/assembly sources plus a modern-terminal Rust behavioral port. Rebuild scripts compare recovered modules against original binaries.

C/assembly reconstruction of Chris Van Genderen pcZIP V1.00.000B/D parallel-port Iomega ZIP/Jaz driver and manager binaries. Includes byte-identical assembly baseline, C command dispatch and differential hardware-protocol oracle.

Historical source-release reconstruction/archive of DOS Fractint versions up to 19.6, preserving the Stone Soup Group fractal generator, optimized assembly arithmetic, graphics drivers and help compiler. This is source restoration rather than binary decompilation.
Ian Hammond’s reconstruction of the XXDP+ HMDLD0 monitor by reverse assembling the XXDP23 binary. A complete monolithic annotated monitor source is preserved alongside binary reference and listings.
Preserves David Mills’s Fuzzball operating-system/network suite, including MACRO-11 implementation modules, RT-11 command files, libraries and distribution disk images.

Historical ELF system files recovered from SAIL, with PDP-11 operating-system/network source, linker code, manuals and PDP-10 host-side tools. The archive explicitly records conversion of SAIL 36-bit words into ASCII octets.
Original MACRO-11 Micro Operating System source provided by J. Noel Chiappa, including processor/storage management, asynchronous I/O, network modules and Terminal Interface Unit configuration.
Preserved Mini ITS executive and device/network software for assorted PDP-11 front ends, terminal concentrators and bridges, with selectable machine configurations and PALX assembly instructions.

Tony Nicholson’s RSTS/E maintenance repository contains actual BASIC-PLUS FIT date-word fixes, build commands, DECnet/E ONLPAT patches and related PDP-11 utility sources. Scope is maintenance patches, not a complete reconstructed RSTS kernel.

Original legacy HAMMONDsoftware RUST/SJ and RUST/RTX operating-system source/binary collection, with MACRO-11 monitor, boot, EMT and device routines plus utilities and Windows-side support. It is unrelated to the modern Rust programming language.
Actual Xinu version-7-derived kernel/tree being ported to Motorola 68000, with 68k startup and context switching, scheduler/network C sources and freestanding m68k toolchain recipes.
Preserved 1990s Pilot VT100 application source and later Palm OS 4 SDK compatibility patch, implementing serial terminal I/O, escape parser, screen handling and configurable keys.

Mats Nordstrom’s early-1980s FORTRAN Interlisp interpreter, preserved in original form and translated with f2c into a subsequently hand-maintained portable C interpreter, with Lisp libraries, image-building scripts, manuals and regression tests.

Substantial preserved TENEX monitor/source archive with multiple historical revisions, MACRO-10 memory/scheduler/file modules, EXEC and utility sources, assembler/linker command files, manuals and hardware documentation.
Reusable C# IBM 1130 CPU/system emulator and assembler with instruction classes, memory/interrupt handling, card devices, partial disk support, tests and optional Web API/frontend.
Independent TypeScript Centurion minicomputer emulator with substantial CPU6 opcode/addressing-mode implementation, RAM/ROM/diagnostic/multiplexer cards and debugging support.
Fresh-search slice: exact `TI-99/4A disassembly reconstruction` and broader `ti99 disassembly` returned no repositories in the connected GitHub search.

Fresh-search slice: exact `SG-1000 disassembly reassembly` returned no repositories; broader `sg1000 homebrew` resolved to a previously reviewed hardware clone, three direct forks and a third-party ROM collection.

Fresh-search slice: exact `Apple Lisa development toolkit homebrew` returned no repositories; broader `apple lisa development` promoted the new lisa-c cross-development environment and its linked LisaPaint application.
lisa-c — Apple Lisa Office System C cross-development, object/disk tooling and native runtime support.
LisaPaint — original native Lisa Office System painting application built with lisa-c.

Routine-by-routine reverse-engineering-derived conversion of all six C64 California Games events to a 32K BBC Micro Model B. Native 6502 game rules are adapted directly, with rebuilt BBC graphics, disk overlays and sound; not a game-specific emulation wrapper.

Reusable native C64 emulator for Sharp SM5A Game & Watch ROMs, supporting Ball, Vermin, Fire and Helmet through a shared CPU interpreter and per-title display adapters. Distinct from native C64 gameplay remakes.

Author-released abandoned college-project side-scrolling game demonstrator, with a controllable running/jumping character, scrolling graphics buffers, IRQs, object/action logic, level and sprite resources.

Native CPC didactic RPG/platform engine demonstration with tile map, limited camera window, collision, coins, doors/keys, enemies and combat scenes. Complete text BASIC listing is the substantive implementation.
Native K&R C dungeon game for Amstrad PCW CP/M Plus with alternative generic CP/M VT100 build, eleven dungeon levels, combat/inventory logic and native map encoder, decoder and editor tools.

Complete author-released smooth-scrolling C64 racing game and earlier prototype from the Lemon64 Fun and Games with Assembly tutorial; converted from native Turbo Assembler development to ACME/C64Studio source.
Author-released single-screen platform survival game created for Scene World issue 32's Let's Make a C64 Game tutorial, including native graphics/music and KickAssembler source.
Expanded 16-level parachutist landing/high-score game developed natively on C64 after a 2KB competition entry, then transferred into cross-assembly source including disk high-score support.

Full 16-level C64 arcade maze game for Scene World issue 29 with crystals, pursuing spiders, temporary invulnerability, lives, high scores and ending sequence; distinct from abbreviated tutorial version.

Complete C64 River Barrage project adapting Martin Piper's reusable scrolling/SEUCK engine, with new title/high-score frontend, shield, animations, score panel, audio choices and picture-loader intro.
Reusable C/Z80 engine for native ZX Spectrum 48K and 128K adventures, with SP1/JSP sprite backends, hero/enemy/bullet collision, generated game data, banking, maps and flow rules.
Native Atari 8-bit minefield/action game implementation by Peter J. Meyer combining C game logic, 6502 interrupt/graphics/audio routines and cartridge/XEX layouts.

Gary James’s native Blitz Basic maze game, preserved and adjusted by earok. This is editable Amiga game implementation, including map, player/enemy/pill updates and IFF assets, rather than a WHDLoad slave or emulation wrapper.

Mike Cooper’s Amiga Format competition platform game, supplied with permission and detokenized to readable Blitz Basic by the preservation repository. It has multiple playable characters, world logic and original graphics/sounds.

Recovered isometric action shooter by Peter & Kalle K, originally entered in the Amiga Format Blitz Basic competition and recovered from an Acid Software hard drive. earok’s preservation adds fixes to oxygen timing, corrupt levels and end-of-game looping.

earok’s open Scorpion Engine Christmas puzzle-platformer source, with Santa, Rudolph and pushable presents. The repository contains executable visual-script command graphs, actors, maps and platform data, rather than screenshots or an engine-only demo stub.

Scorpion Engine adaptation of the DOS multiplayer rabbit arena game. Contains original-style gameplay scripts for bunny motion, collisions, spring/water/ice behavior, gore, spawning and scoring, plus full maps and assets.

Merlyn Kline’s native ClearView hypertext reader/compiler preserved with a 32-bit-clean RISC OS build path. Supports wrapped multi-font text and inline Sprites, Draw files and Ace Films; source includes reading, compilation, search, bookmarks and printing.

George Nakos’s Atari ST media-handling plugin and SamariTan CLI, supporting ST/MSA/DIM floppy images and AHDI/ICD-style hard disk images. Contains image decoding, FAT filesystem integration and create/extract/update operations on modern hosts.

Atari cartridge-image creation tool by ggnkua. Parses TOS PRG inputs, writes cartridge application headers, performs relocation, and embeds a native 68000 loader that copies programs from ROM to RAM before running them.

George Nakos and Douglas Little’s linker-stage conversion utility turns m68k ELF into native Atari TOS PRG, including relocations and optional symbol tables. It is useful to cross-development workflows and preserves a dedicated Atari executable-format implementation.

Eduardo Ojeda’s original 2002 two-player Classic Mac arena game and its 2026 native SDL3 restoration. Original C code and art are retained; a replacement SAT/QuickDraw compatibility layer allows the physics, ball, ships, missiles and power-ups to run on modern macOS and Windows.

Tom Pickering’s C++ recreation of Fantasia’s 1997 RISC OS puzzle game using original assets with permission. Implements 100 levels over five worlds, with wizard/blob switching, ladders, falling/pushable/breakable blocks and collectables.

Stephan Kleinert’s original BBC BASIC RISC OS desktop implementation of the Robots/Daleks survival game. Retains tokenized editable BASIC source in !RunImage, desktop templates, sprites, scores, lives and teleport mechanics.

Kochise’s archived native Atari Falcon030 Mandelbrot/Julia explorer. Full 68030/FPU assembler implementation controls the Falcon video mode, screen memory and blitter before computing fractal iterations.

Native vector action game with player/enemy movement, projectiles, frenzy and scoring. MKnight.asm contains the cartridge entry, title/credits states, game state, player/enemy updates and vector/speech data; it is substantial cartridge source rather than a ROM-only archive.

Native 6809 recreation of the 1971 discrete-logic arcade game. Gameplay, artwork, timing and sound were measured from the companion FPGA recreation and schematics. game.asm implements missile lives, game flow, scores, collisions, explosions and hyperspace rather than emulating an original CPU.

Interactive Vectrex handwriting recognizer: joystick or experimental light-pen stroke input, 12×12 integer rasterization and a 144–64–10 neural network running on the console CPU. vecnist.asm implements drawing, scaling, first-layer accumulation, second-layer multiplication and score displays; weights and training/test twins are supplied.

Native C89 scrolling shooter consolidating Star Rise, Bydo Incursion, Star Fall and Final Strike into one cartridge. main.c has chapter loading, ship selection, force pod, charged beam, waves, bosses and chapter-unlock flow; graphics swap by chapter to fit tile memory.

Native NGPC fan reimagining of SNK’s Last Resort with two ships, five stages, orbital option-pod control, charged wave cannon, multiple pod weapons and monochrome mode. main.c has stage terrain installation, pod movement/fire and independent game progression.

Native puzzle-fighter proof of concept with falling gem pairs, rotations, gravity, crashes, rectangular power gems, chain damage, CPU garbage attacks, story/endless modes and unlocks. src/game.c contains actual grid/phase resolution and difficulty tables; field.c renders through NGPC tile hardware.

Button-driven native C reimplementation of Zork I with verb/noun selection and scrolling text. engine.c directly implements room/object accessibility, light sources, inventory, puzzles, score, troll/thief interactions and victory state; this is not a Z-machine CPU-wrapper port.

C++/Qt tracker, piano-roll, instrument/SFX and project tool for native NGPC sound export. polling_driver.cpp supplies real Z80 polling-driver bytes and command host logic; project includes clean-room Z80/T6W28 preview cores and C/ASM output.

Material NGPC-targeting fork of GB Studio 4.3.2 with V3 Python compiler, native C generation, audio conversion and emulator-backed play/debug. v3Build.ts snapshots project/resources and invokes V3 export/build-ROM; compiler.py validates reachable IR and creates specialized build plans.

Original turn-based homebrew battle/RPG for the PC-FX. main.c implements player HP/MP/stats, two-player and survival flow, battle choices and sound, while game.c handles native PC-FX controller/rendering interfaces through liberis.

Explicit native C/Z80 rewrite of NES Final Fantasy rules using Disch’s disassembly as specification and user-ROM extracted assets, not 6502 translation/emulation. Battle overlays, fixed-bank services, maps and quest state run through 512KB MegaCart banking with SGM RAM.

Reusable Supervision emulator with 6502 interpreter, memory and I/O maps, interrupts, scanline GPU and sound implementations. common/gpu.c renders actual packed Supervision pixels and palette state; not a title-specific emulation wrapper.

Independent reusable Gamate emulator with CPU opcode/cycle engine, LCD, bank/protection/memory and UI implementations. CPU.cpp contains concrete execution and cycle tables; Emulation.cpp handles BIOS/ZIP/ROM loading and machine state.

Jasper de Keijzer’s 1996 five-in-a-row game, preserved as original ICC sources and a 2026 OpenWatcom Presentation Manager continuation. The 19×19 game implements position updates, computer move search and win detection; this is its own native game lineage.

Herbert Bushong’s 1996–1997 OS/2 Lights Out puzzle continued as a plain-C 32-bit Presentation Manager rewrite of its preserved Borland OWL source. The 6×8 board has two-state and three-state modes, scoring and persistent settings.

Jan M. Danielsson’s 1997 two-player worm combat game restored for OpenWatcom with native DIVE graphics, MMPM/2 audio and configurable keyboard/joystick input. Its substantial game-thread code implements worms, missiles, apple powerups and round results.

Dmitry Ivanov’s native OS/2 enclosure game, continued from the 2002 open-source release and modernized to OpenWatcom. The player builds walls to contain moving balls; implementation includes runner/hunter motion, ball collisions and territory replacement.

Dirk Vandenheuvel’s 1995 Asteroids-style Presentation Manager shooter, released as GPL source in 2002 and continued with an OpenWatcom build. Native C implements vector objects, shots, enemies, asteroid geometry and powerups, with keyboard, mouse and GAME$ joystick controls.

Michael G. Slack’s 1997–1998 Sibyl OS/2 adaptation of Alex Lane’s 1990 minefield-walking puzzle, translated to C/OpenWatcom in 2026. The game implements mine placement, travel/marking and a new bounded safe-cell deduction solver.

Michael G. Slack’s 2001 Sibyl blackjack game translated to native C/OpenWatcom for OS/2. The rules implementation covers multi-deck shuffling, dealer/player scoring, splitting, doubling and insurance, with original Pascal retained.

Peter Wansch’s 1994 native Reversi game continued in OpenWatcom with preserved ICC sources. Its independent engine implements legal-move detection, disc flipping, positional evaluation and recursive multi-level computer search.

Andreas Kieser’s 1996–1999 VisPro/REXX Yahtzee-style dice game rebuilt in C for native OS/2 Presentation Manager. It supports one to five players and implements category scoring, held dice, bonus calculations and score lists.

James L. Dean’s 1988 native maze game, carried through a 2023 GCC/ArcaOS port and a 2026 OpenWatcom restoration. It generates window-sized mazes, tracks path/backtracking and computes a visible solution.

Michael Bruestle’s 1997 native OS/2 Minesweeper game, maintained as a separate lineage from the already tracked Mine Sweeper/2 project. Its own PM field widget implements mine creation, neighbor counts, reveal/mark interactions and statistics.

Turgut Kalfaoglu’s 1992 OS/2 typing-practice game restored to OpenWatcom. The native PM program presents falling words and accepts typed input before they reach the bottom, retaining original source alongside the current port.

Dr. R. Grothmann’s native OS/2 arithmetic puzzle continued in OpenWatcom C++. Players combine six supplied numbers with arithmetic operations to reach a target; the implementation also searches for a solution.

Mateusz Viste’s low-requirement DOSMid music player extended by Tronix with Creative Music System/Game Blaster output and simple percussion. Real-mode C includes MIDI/MUS decoding, timing, hardware outputs and a substantial CMS voice/register implementation; this is a substantive native application branch.

Reusable browser player and test platform for floppy-era PC-98 freeware/doujin software. Integrates NP2kai hardware emulation with independently implemented DOS executable loading, INT 21h services, EXEC/TSR/MCB/XMS support, archive/FAT extraction and a browser UI. It accepts multiple user-supplied programs and is not a game-specific CPU wrapper.
Alan Snyder’s original portable C compiler archive, including machine-independent compiler phases, target descriptions, assembly runtime, ITS/WAITS/TOPS-20 variants and technical reports.
Preserves K. Chen and Ken Harrenstien/SRI’s PDP-10 C compiler, with parser, typed syntax trees, optimizers, register allocator and PDP-10 code generation.
Original MIT Muddle interpreter/compiler archives in PDP-10 MIDAS assembly, with 1970s SUMEX copies, TOPS-20 interpreter/compiler, manuals and later machine-independent MDL material.
Rutgers TOPS-20 Common Lisp distribution with Uppsala modifications, native bootstrap/LAP code, compiler and reader/library implementation, Flavors and Portable CommonLoops branches.
Historical Rutgers Pascal compiler sources recovered from University of Utah, including Pascal compiler implementation, MACRO-10 runtime/debugger/I/O modules, command files and detailed manuals.
BBN’s native TENEX BCPL implementation, including BCPL parser/translator/code-generator sources, MACRO runtime support, compiler-generation command files and historical manuals.
Original DEC FORTRAN IV compiler and LIB40 runtime sources, including FX compiler passes, native arithmetic/I/O libraries, assembly/link control files and manuals.

Preserves Harvard’s extensible interactive PPL implementation from SAIL/TENEX, including assembly interpreter/parser/runtime modules, build/link command files, manuals and an additional archived Unix distribution.

Recovered Stevens Institute SITBOL compiler/runtime modules, extracted from historical University of Arizona archive material, covering lexer, syntax, interpreter, strings, arrays, I/O and garbage collection.
Substantial Tymshare PDP-10 monitor archives with scheduler, swapping/memory, filesystem, devices and many machine/site configuration variants, plus build control files and operational documentation.
Foonly-specific TENEX-derived monitor source with changed scheduler, storage/forks/device code, MFEXEC command executive and F2/F3 microcode collections.
ETH M2M-derived multi-pass Modula-2 compiler retargeted for Motorola 68020 Nixdorf Targon/31 and Sun-3/SunOS, with native runtime libraries, compiler driver and debugging/profiling utilities.
Original native PDP-10 Interlisp environment archive with MACRO-10 Lisp kernel, Interlisp compiler/editor/assembler/loadup sources, historical SUMEX/Linköping/PARC distributions and manuals.
Original experimental Mostly Useless eXperimental eXecutive for DEC PDP-11, with C/assembly kernel, process creation and task loading, trap/MMU/clock handling, drivers, shell and sample tasks.

Native Z80 implementation of the pyramid-hopping arcade concept for Amstrad Plus, with ASIC sprites, synthesized sound and separate cassette, disk and CPR cartridge packaging. Substantial native game implementation rather than emulation.

Original 64K Amstrad CPC match-three game with special-candy combinations, diagonal gravity, obstacles, ingredient objectives, 60 levels and AY voice samples. Native Z80 source is the primary project; optional desktop emulator wrappers are secondary packaging.

Native CPC 6128 puzzle game in which a stick figure changes gravity in eight directions and walks around corners; rooms, hazards, doors and crates provide puzzle progression. Includes a separate optional .NET/browser room editor, without substituting emulation for the native game.

Native CPC 6128 fleet-strategy game featuring a shrinking refugee convoy, 3D ship rendering, squadrons, combat and cockpit/minigame sequences. Banked Z80 source and disk streaming are genuine target-specific implementations.
Large Z80 homebrew shooter based on Goldorak/Grendizer, targeting the CPC Plus ASIC and GX4000 cartridge system. Source covers movement, enemy waves, weapons, bosses, HUD, shop and ending sequences.

Source for the CPCRetroDev 2019 story-driven action/adventure game LUDIC, with contemporary CPC and Enterprise builds. Shared C gameplay and target wrappers implement native output for both Z80 computers.

Original Amstrad CPC single-player shoot-em-up produced by Gameroid students for CPCRetroDev 2018. Native Z80 source includes player/enemy/bullet/control/render modules, compressed tilemaps and interrupt-driven music.

Original Pipe Mania-inspired electronic-circuit puzzle for CPC 6128, written in ugBASIC and cross-compiled to native Z80. Grid routing, piece placement, distance and win checking are implemented in the included BASIC source.

Original two/four-player BBC Model B territory-control game whose ownership state is encoded in 35 CMYK dither patterns. Native 6502 game has tanks, paint splats, ink reservoirs, AI opponents, keyboard remapping and 32 level layouts.

Substantial 6502 conversion of the author’s ecological BBC game, originally released in mixed BASIC/assembler in 2022. The new engine owns per-frame diver/fish/shark/jellyfish collision, oxygen, sound and score while BASIC retains setup, scenery and level flow.

Original author’s preservation and direct JavaScript port of FLY, published in The Micro User in July 1985. Includes detokenized/tokenized cassette source, a faithful classic browser presentation and an extended 3D game sharing line-number-annotated rules.

Work-in-progress native C64 adaptation of Kevin Edwards’s released BBC Galaforce source. A substantial C64 implementation replaces hardware setup, bitmap rendering, keyboard input and sound while retaining real alien types, waves and flight-pattern data from the original.

Native TRS-80 Model 4/4P recreation of Fallout’s terminal-hacking password puzzle, implemented in LS-DOS/TRSDOS BASIC with selectable difficulty and intelligence options. Complete readable listing plus interpreted, compiled and bootable disk forms are included.

Raymond Hill’s author-published 1992 Atari ST arcade game source, with single-player asteroid-style combat and a modem-linked two-player mode. The repository preserves original C plus extensive 68000 drawing, collision, input and modem routines, project definitions and a distributed PRG.

Jérôme Mahieux’s Atari ST board/puzzle game and level editor, originally dating to 1995 and released with complete STOS listings, assets and a Python floppy/source-template generator. This is the game implementation and editor, not just a launcher.

Jeff and Steve Fulton’s 1990 Atari ST poker-dice game archive includes the original tokenized STOS BASIC GAME.BAS, compiled PRG, graphics, sound/data and detailed original instructions. Read-only structural analysis identifies the Lionpoulos STOS header and a complete ordered tokenized BASIC program, not merely a binary with incidental strings.

Author archive of the historical GEM-PC adaptation of an oil-company economic strategy game originally written for Atari ST GEM in the 1980s. The substantial C source tree preserves economics, drilling, transportation, newspaper events, GEM UI and IBM DOS compatibility routines; comments include 1986 development dates. This record covers the recovered PC implementation, not an established native Atari ST build.

Author-released 1990–1993 Amiga tools: Hunk executable/object inspector, Hunkhack self-decompressing-file manipulator, UnStuff Macintosh SIT extractor, DXF-to-SDF Sega CD model converter and line-ending converter. C implementations preserve real parsing and conversion logic.

Per Olofsson’s joystick-operated native Amiga game menu, with OCS/AGA layouts, directory navigation, responsive asynchronous IFF screenshots, slideshows, per-game scripts and configuration. Full Amiga E sources are provided for launcher, menu and helper.

Grzegorz Kraszewski’s system-friendly native Amiga implementation of the line-untangling graph puzzle, containing window/menu interaction through Amiga Intuition, coordinate transforms, graph generation/solving tests and level loading.

Robin Southern’s native AmigaOS 3.x C game framework supplies event, time, memory, window, input and planar/chunky framebuffer implementations, including a 68000-family chunky-to-planar assembly component. This is a reusable native framework, not an emulator wrapper.

Keli Hlodversson’s Conway’s Game of Life implementation performs cellular-automaton work using the Atari ST BLiTTER, wrapped in a GEM application. Source includes BLiTTER register definitions, counting tables, update routines and window/display code.

Python/Pygame reimplementation of the Atari ST edition of Super Sprint, aiming to reproduce original gameplay while adding custom cars/tracks/music and improving waits and controls. The source implements vehicle dynamics, collisions, track logic, AI opponents, menus and asset managers.

Alan Richardson’s early-1990s Atari ST tank/vector-game prototype, released by its author with C and 68000 assembly for vector graphics, line drawing and joystick handling, plus historical object and PRG files.

Sandor Drieënhuizen’s reusable Atari ST 68000 assembly subsystem exposes keyboard scan/ASCII tables, last scan code and two joystick states to GFA BASIC via an inline binary and documented fixed jump table. Full assembly and GFA demo are included.

Native Amiga 500 space-shooter homebrew in 68000 assembly, with direct custom-chip video/DMA/sound, double buffers, player/enemy/laser logic, lives, score and title/game-over screens. Includes source modules and raw graphics/audio assets.

Cross-platform installation/build integration for the EPSON/TASKING S1C88 compiler, including Pokémon Mini headers, locator configuration, startup assembly and an executable hello-world source example. This is an SDK integration project, not a reconstruction of the proprietary compiler.
Python control-flow-aware Pokémon Mini binary disassembler with explicit opcode tables, BIOS mode, symbol input, user entrypoints and execution-path output.
Python decoder/converter for Pokémon Mini Minlib song streams, reconstructing note duration, pitch and duty-cycle information and emitting WAV or MIDI.
Tkinter desktop graphics-conversion tool that previews bitmap tiles and generates Pokémon Mini tile and masked sprite byte data.
Header-based S1C88 support library with hardware registers, inline assembly pixel plotting, character/font rendering, key polling and scrollable tile-map routines.
Original 2 KiB Channel F road-and-river crossing game written from scratch in Fairchild F8 assembly; includes palette tests, branch-range checks and emulator snapshot-analysis tools.

Rust/WebAssembly Channel F emulator application with browser canvas video, audio, controller/front-panel handling and URL-based BIOS/cartridge loading, using the same author’s separately sourced chips::fairchild_f8 board core.
Portable libretro Channel F emulator created by David Richardson, with a complete F8 instruction implementation, memory/port/video/audio/controller models and optional BIOS high-level routines.
RP2040 firmware turning the WonderSwan EXT port into USB serial and digital stereo audio devices; dual-core TinyUSB service plus UART, PIO and DMA hardware handling.

Long-running Delphi/Lazarus emulator suite with native Pascal CPU and device implementations and reusable arcade, computer and console drivers, including relatively uncommon Casio PV-1000 and Super Cassette Vision.

Independent TypeScript DAP frontend for cc65 Lynx programs, driving Gearlynx through TCP debug-monitor and framebuffer protocols; source/symbol parsing, breakpoints, stepping, overlay selection and memory visualization.

Author-published recovery of Grzegorz Drozd’s 1998–1999 Polish DOS game; the main Pascal implementation includes character physics, combat and environmental effects, with graphics, sound, mouse and XMS units.
Original 2022 survival roguelike sharing dungeon, item, monster and player implementation across CP/M, 16-bit DOS and modern Pascal targets; this is an original game, unrelated to Alone in the Dark.
Preservation of the 1994–1997 multiplayer, isometric, turn-based DOS tactics game by Niko Nevatie and Kari Luojus, including the game, editors and original Turbo Pascal/i386 assembler source.

Original lightweight DOS game launcher created in 2022, with metadata filtering, play-time tracking and a PathMinder-inspired text UI. Pascal implementation launches games using a separately credited ExecWithSwap module.
Original two-player MS-DOS action game by Gered King for the June 2021 GDR 4x4x4 challenge, with a Pascal state machine, match simulation, map editor, assets and GDlib mode-13h routines.

Ongoing Pascal version of Andrew Danson’s DOS platform game, started around 1999 and retaining levels from his earlier QBasic version. Includes engine, XT and standard builds, level editor, graphics modes and sound drivers.

Original Czech graphical/text adventure for PC XT, DOS, CGA and mouse, created for and winning the 2019 DOS game competition. The Pascal implementation includes parser/command regions, inventory, room logic and graphics objects.
Preserved Pascal source of Depicus’s Windows 3.1 Wake-on-LAN utility, with VCL application/forms and a component implementing socket-based magic-packet transmission.

Author-published source accompanying Patrick Prémartin’s January 1999 PointDBF article: a Delphi VCL login/password-change component and demonstration applications, with event hooks for application-defined password handling.
Assembly reimplementation of the IBM PS/2 Model 30-286 font-selector experience for ordinary VGA DOS machines, with live preview, font loading and a persistent INT 10h/INT 2Fh TSR.
Author-published 1991–1993 DOS resident utility source for visual disk-activity indication and selective drive read/write restrictions, implemented by hooking BIOS INT 13h.
Small original real-mode DOS COM utility suite implementing shutdown, standby and suspend through the APM 1.0–1.2 BIOS interface, with basic error reporting.
Original low-level keyboard scan-code diagnostic for DOS, with IRQ1 handling and an alternative standalone boot-sector mode; build tooling can package it into FreeDOS floppy/CD images.

Original graphical DOS game menu in QuickBASIC, enumerating game subfolders, displaying thumbnails and launching PLAY.BAT, plus helper tools storing long game names inside reserved bitmap palette entries.
Preserved original 1.0 source of Joe King’s 2000 Delta Code BASIC action game, with one/two-player combat, laser guns, maps, sprites and a Toadman 1-to-2 map conversion program.

Source copied from an operating MR12.7 Multics instance and reconstructed from simulated backup tapes with mxload; preserves and extends the Bull HN/MIT source release, including substantial PL/I and ALM system implementations.
Collection of BCause, a single-pass B-to-x86-64 compiler, and bbesm, a B-written compiler for BESM-6 under Dubna; also preserves the PDP-7 B compiler that bbesm explicitly derives from.
PCC revival tree containing a substantial Elbrous-B machine backend and runtime startup sources; local.c/local2.c retain MIPT 1988 Serge Vakulenko headers and actual stack-machine code generation.

Independent by-the-Bluebook C++ implementation of the 16-bit Smalltalk-80 VM, object memory, BitBlt and SDL host integration; restores use of Xerox release-2 images and source browsing via a POSIX filesystem layer.

Independent Java-8 translation of the Bluebook VM with normal and Stretch object memory, Alto disk emulation, and Tajo/XDE filesystem emulation; supports original V2, DV6 and converted Analyst images.
Hardware-specific port of Dan Banay’s Smalltalk-80 VM to Circle, replacing desktop SDL/OS facilities with Raspberry Pi kernel, framebuffer, USB input and SD/FAT storage integration.
Reviewed the snapshot-saving refactor, interpreter-linked object memory, GC root handling and host file operations.
Author’s 2002–2003 hobby compiler recovered from old disk archives and updated; full C frontend maps ALGOL-60 scope, arrays, call-by-name and procedures into C with a driver and runtime.
OCaml compiler and C runtime implementing the June-1972 ALGOL W language description and intended to compile OS/360 ALGOL W programs with little or no modification.
Revives Dijkstra’s 1960 Electrologica X1 ALGOL compiler through preserved Pascal transcription and p2c-derived C, bundled with an X1-like simulator, procedure library, decoding tools and tests.
Portable RSRE/DRA ALGOL-68RS frontend extracted from ELLA and continued from Sian Mountbatten’s Linux port, with ALGOL68 sources, generated C, runtime preludes and self-hosting build path.

Port of the historical Oberon System to an Oberon-to-LuaJIT compiler/runtime and Qt backend, preserving substantial text/viewer/editor/application modules and replacing original inner system services.

Restores OP2 from Native Oberon 2.3.7 Alpha, converts native file format to UTF-8, refactors machine dependence, and adds standalone C99 compiler builds plus ARMv7 and RV32 code generators and bootlinkers.

Full Bell Labs/Vita Nuova Inferno system source including native and hosted kernels, Dis VM, Limbo compiler, libraries, device services and applications, maintained as a portable distributed operating environment.

Commented Z80 reconstruction of TRS-80 Model I/III Level II BASIC ROMs, with enhanced variants and EACA System-80 support. The author explicitly identifies the material as a derivative disassembly rather than original Microsoft/Tandy source.
Preservation release of Ed Fries’ Romox Atari 8-bit game, with original source disk and Kay Savetz’s exported text files. Kept as one source-release family.

Reusable C cross-assembler implementing Mac/65-compatible syntax, macros, Atari directives, binary/image output and emulator-state injection. Selected maintained Peter Hinz fork as the single ATasm lineage record.

Expanded maintained Python collection for TRS-80 Color Computer software development. Its substantial DECB-to-BASIC09 translator is beyond the small image-conversion ancestor; retained as one CoCo Tools family record.

C/assembly development framework with MSX hardware backend, SDL host backend, Konami-5 mapper linker and font/MIDI conversion utilities. It lets the same application sources be tested on Linux then compiled to MSX cartridges.
Native MSX-DOS browser/downloader for the file-hunter.com archive, with search/type/generation filters, MSX2 text interface and UNAPI TCP/IP transfer code.
Commented native BASIC Wordle-like game for Tandy Model 100 and related Kyocera/NEC/Olivetti machines, with compressed yearly dictionaries and platform-specific terminal/date handling.

Native MSX pseudo-3D rail shooter with separate MSX1, MSX2, Turbo R/V9958, V9990 and experimental V9968/Geo3D configurations. One family record prevents counting each hardware experiment as a new game.

Configurable C/Z80 game-development runtime covering MSX graphics, input, audio, storage and memory banking, plus build and asset tools. Many sample games/demos are examples within one reusable library project.

Portable C game library with target-specific graphics/input/sound and a coordinated game collection including Cross Chase, Shoot, Bomber, Snake and Horde. Canonical upstream supersedes the stale miguelqvd/CROSS-CHASE fork discovered first.

An independently written ARM implementation of the Amiga Batman game with converted graphics, scrolling tile maps, compiled sprites, player movement/collision tests and projectile updates. This is a partial game port, not the already tracked MarkyTurtle Amiga source reconstruction.
A native C++ side-by-side text-file difference viewer with an Amiga GUI, Myers-derived diff engine, selection/search/navigation and background worker code.

Darren Coles’s substantial Amiga E rewrite of the historical AmiExpress BBS, authorised to use the name by the former rights holder. Includes the node/controller, setup/user tools, file-transfer protocols, mail, FTP and HTTP services.

Rudolph Riedel’s maintained source and historical release archives for Greg Cunningham’s DiskMaster2 file manager, including the later C and AmigaOS4 adaptation, command processing, windows, preferences and ARexx support.
Daniel Stenberg and Kjell Ericson’s historical Amiga editor sources, continued by Vidar Hokstad, with editing/undo, text folding, scriptable FPL integration, ARexx and syntax-sensitive display.
Historical open-source Intuition menu enhancer with popup-menu drawing, remapping, preference editor, menu hooks and screen/bitmap management.

Niklas Lindholm’s Swedish KOM-model Amiga BBS, originally developed 1990–1996, later maintained by Tomas Kärki, and revived from NiKom 1.60 sources in 2015. Contains node/server code, conferences, file areas, Fido support and utility libraries.
Hynek Schlawack and Sebastian Bauer’s open-source MUI mail client with POP3, IMAP, SMTP, MIME handling, configuration, address book and Amiga-family platform backends.

Long-running Amiga-family MIME mail user agent, begun by Marcel Beck in 1995 and continued by the YAM team, with MUI GUI, POP3/SMTP transport, folders, identities, filters, encryption integration and ARexx.

Oxyron’s Amiga OCS demo source plus reusable trackmo framework: floppy track loader, Doynamite-derived 68k depacker, P61 player, memory manager, effect launcher and many individual demo parts, with host asset tools.
Chris Bazley’s native RISC OS relocatable module implements joystick SWIs using keypad input, with switched, analogue and damped modes, chiefly to test game joystick support without hardware.
Three native Amiga commands read floppy tracks into ADF images, write ADF images to real drives and copy disks with verification, backed by shared track-device I/O code.
Native ReAction GUI for xadmaster, xfdmaster and Deark with tabbed archive browsing/extraction, LhA/Zip modification, optional virus scanning, disk images and ARexx integration.
MUI frontend for organising and launching Amiga WHDLoad games and demos, with repository scanning, metadata/properties, game images and several native CPU/OS builds.
Amiga E commodity that monitors window drags and snaps/resizes windows at screen edges and corners, including screen-change notifications, configurable zones and Shift bypass.

Original WIP LynxJam 2021 game with a ghost, explorer, holes, maze gates, level maps, title and results screens. game.c contains native sprite structures, explorer states and level/game processing rather than a ROM wrapper.

Native Space Invaders-style WIP with moving enemy formations, player shots, linked-list bombs, collision flags, bunkers and joystick-controlled player. This is an authored C adaptation, not an Intel 8080 reconstruction.

Native Game & Watch-style Lynx game with two game modes, segmented number sprites, score, rabbit position, cocotte timer, lives and action-speed state. ingame.c is substantive implementation and generated assembly is also retained.

Commented educational native Lynx game with animated boy/tree sprites, jump arcs, collision and falling state, score/lives, intro and sound. A distinct game-level implementation on a reusable template.

Full native tile-matching RPG/puzzle game released in 2014. Assembly contains horizontal/vertical matching, board solvability checks, combat, animation, sound and link multiplayer, with art and auxiliary checksum tool.

Native Game Boy game prototype inspired by the football section of Tiny Toons Adventures: Buster Busts Loose. Includes fixed-point object acceleration, active-object bitfields, animation, sprites, joypad and smooth parallax/background implementation.

Real-time native GBC lighting shader demo. Assembly computes simplified dot products with log-space cosine/power lookup tables, run-length encoded normal data and packed Game Boy tile output; Python prepares normal-map sequences.
Reviewed a new MAME Lua tap that logs MIPS-to-IOMCU commands, MCU answers, status/events and EEPROM traffic from the project's RE notes.

Native controller test application that counts presses of a selected button over ten seconds. Actual C state machine reads BIOS current/previous input, detects rising edges, tracks VBlank time and displays totals.

Native 3D skimboarding game WIP: wave movement, board and character meshes, trick rotations, fall/landing checks, input and scoring. Repository contains several historical variants of the same game; selected .03 code is substantive Jo Engine implementation.

Charles Petzold’s September 1990 Microsoft Systems Journal checkers game, preserved with its original sources and a 2026 Open Watcom 32-bit PM continuation. The implementation includes board/judge windows, legal-move generation, recursive jump enumeration and a threaded computer strategy.

Todd B. Crowe’s native OS/2 vector-style Asteroids clone, updated for Open Watcom and ArcaOS. This is the OS/2 game’s source continuation, distinct from the Atari arcade disassembly and unrelated Asteroids homebrews already catalogued. The implementation has game modes, two-player scoring, motion/drawing helpers and configurable keyboard/mouse/joystick input.

Restoration and 32-bit OS/2 PM continuation of Microsoft’s 1988 OS/2 Toolkit JIGSAW sample. It slices a BMP into 36 draggable pieces and preserves GPI retained-segment transforms, piece/island manipulation, zooming and asynchronous drawing. The original 16-bit source is retained in legacy; this is unrelated to the similarly named Jigsaw electronic-puzzle game already indexed.

Frank Sven Nestel’s 1995–2001 PM arithmetic-puzzle game and associated generator/evaluator/solver sources, updated in 2026 for Open Watcom. Actual source implements several legal equation families, randomized puzzle generation, evaluation and a threaded Presentation Manager interface.

Charles Petzold’s magazine-published 1989 OS/2 15-puzzle code, continued as a 32-bit PM application. Source handles row/column tile slides, blank tracking, scramble/reset, solved-state detection and the elapsed timer, with 2026 localization and settings additions.

David Boudah/Bou Software Systems’ 1996 IBM Open Class Boggle game, with original C++ preserved under legacy and a 2026 plain-C PM rewrite. Board source implements Fisher-Yates dice shuffling and Qu handling; dictionary and UI modules validate words and run the timed game without the original IBM C++ class libraries.

Enumerate Inc.’s 1996–1999 polygon-stopping game, preserving its original V GUI/X11/Windows95 C++ sources and a 2026 OS/2 SDL2 front end. Polygon and walk classes maintain vertices and motion; the new main loop handles input, menus, timed bonuses, lives and drawing.

Rene Auberger’s 1999 native OS/2 Mastermind game, with its legacy C source and a 2026 Open Watcom continuation that consolidates the language/resource DLL design into one executable. Source renders guess rows, drag/drop pins, exact/color-only feedback, timers and high scores.

Mike of Vienna’s 1998 OS/2 bird-shooting game, preserved with original C and an Open Watcom/ArcaOS continuation. The PM message procedure moves bird sprites, performs mouse hit tests, counts kills, supports the all-birds action and manages pause/focus/timer state.

E. L. Zapanta’s IBM-era 1992–1994 native 32-bit OS/2 bingo game, preserved with original C and a 2026 Open Watcom build. Source contains randomized card/number creation, multiple bingo-pattern checks, score tracking, printing, virtual hall players and MMPM/2 sound support.

Stangl Roman’s 1992 ball-rolling OS/2 PM game, including its 2017 anniversary-era source and a 2026 Open Watcom continuation. The draw thread manages the playfield, weighted random symbols, deflectors, holes, movement and points while the UI accepts mouse input and maintains settings.

Kent Lundberg’s 1993–2002 native OS/2 Presentation Manager version of robots, continued for ArcaOS. GAME.C implements robot pursuit, collisions forming heaps, legal moves, teleport, sonic screwdriver, scoring and level progression; separate source covers PM UI and high scores.

Michael G. Slack’s OS/2 Sibyl/Object Pascal cribbage game source archive, with an engine tracing back through a DOS Turbo Pascal port to David Addison’s Amiga A-basic game. The recovered OS/2 engine scores hands and play, recommends discards and chooses computer cards; visual forms, configuration and resources are included.

New native PC-98 MS-DOS adventure engine by PokuG/Yarufu. It interprets Shift-JIS story scripts with branching, choices, flags and save/load, drives PC-98 planar graphics and GRCG output, and optionally uses PMD BGM and DOS mouse input. This is native homebrew, distinct from recovered ADV98V commercial-engine research.

Independent preservation repository containing transcriptions and tape-derived source for Burroughs B5500 software, including University of Washington APL, Wirth EULER, Heriot-Watt Pascal, SNOBOL, Lisp, system patches and CUBE user-library tapes. Substantial recovered implementations and per-program provenance distinguish this from an emulator-only record.

Howard Bussey preserves the SDS-940 BASIC implementation he extended at NOAA around 1970 with formatted output, multiple file I/O and strings. Source returned through the Hawaii BCC-500 lineage contains the compiler, runtime and scratch-page sections rather than a modern BASIC clone.

Recovered original CMS assembler source, macro definitions and assembly listings from old CP/67-format tapes. Recovery used VM/370 and z/VM conversion before ASCII extraction. The repository name mentions CP/67; inspected payload is specifically CMS, with source headers dated 1973 as well as older material, not a verified complete CP kernel.

Pascal Bourguignon reconstructs the 1961 IBM 7090 LISP 1.5 punched-card source from Bonnie’s Birthday Assembly listing, preserving card layout and known typographical quirks while generating some tables and inferring five obscured cards. Includes original listing PDF, reconstructed assembly, generator Lisp, assembler patches and run recipe.

Independent C reimplementation of LISP 1.5 as described in its manual, with eval and evalquote REPLs, reader, evaluator, cons-cell memory management and library examples. This is neither a mirror nor the IBM 7090 card transcription.

C++/Qt tool decodes the Tioga rich-text file format used for most Xerox Cedar/Mesa archived sources, displays documentation and syntax-highlighted source, and supplies a Cedar lexer plus experimental parser. Derived partly from archived Andrew/Emacs decoder plugins to make the 1993 Solaris Cedar tree inspectable.

Reimplements the asterisk-squasher coroutine example from Melvin Conway’s 1963 compiler paper in modern x86/x86-64 assembly, with Linux, macOS and Windows versions, both subroutine and coroutine styles and smoke-test fixtures. Focused historical programming-technique reconstruction rather than a full compiler.

Elixir implementation of an SDS-940 assembler with opcode map, lexical and expression parsing, symbol resolution, pseudo-operations, relocatable address handling and assembly listing output. README is boilerplate, but substantive assembler implementation and tests establish its purpose.

Elixir SDS-940 user-mode simulator with CPU execution, memory mapping, process/machine state and host-side SYSPOP implementation. Phoenix umbrella provides surrounding application infrastructure. Scope is running many user programs rather than reconstructing a complete original TSS kernel.

Neil Higgins’s reusable Python LGP-30 simulator models instructions, drum memory, Flexowriter input/output, paper-tape and Intel HEX loading, with interactive debugging controls and recovered program examples. Its stated goal is a hackable simulator suited to future MicroPython use rather than cycle accuracy.

Neil Higgins’s two-pass LGP-30 cross-assembler provides structural validation, symbols and expressions, directives, formatted listings and Intel HEX binary output. Modernized syntax intentionally differs from the historical native assemblers.

Companion Python tool converts sparse Intel HEX LGP-30 binaries into v-formatted LGP-30 paper-tape text, preserving start address in Stop and Transfer records. Implementation groups segments into chunks, writes tape headers and encodes the machine’s nonstandard hexadecimal alphabet.

Reusable C11 LGP-30 core with drum rotational timing, all instruction implementations, Flexowriter/simplified I/O interfaces, integrated assembler and memory-image format, plus batch CLI and interactive debugger. Independent implementation has tests and detailed manual-linked instruction semantics.

Compact independent Go assembler for LGP-30 source with labels, opcode/order table, literal packing, multiple number notations, two-pass symbol replacement and native-word emission. Unit tests exercise literals and parsing; implemented tool distinct from the author’s browser-emulator code.

Native turn-based wolf-pack survival strategy game for the Commodore C64, Plus/4 and Commander CX16. C gameplay implements prey spawning and movement, wolf selection, energy costs, catching prey, scoring and ten levels, with separate machine I/O implementations.

Native 6502 graphical adventure engine and playable technology demo for Acorn Electron/BBC Micro Model B, inspired by the style of Sierra AGI. Includes a custom script bytecode VM, synonym-aware text parser, tiled backgrounds, sprites and compressed tape loading; this is an original engine, not a recovered AGI interpreter.

Large native MSX multiplayer snake game with up to eight players, battle/training game states, forty levels, score codes, sound and joystick-adapter support. Implemented in C using MSXgl, with substantial game code and data rather than an engine-only sample.

Substantial native MSX adventure/action game source with a banked overworld, title sequence, scrolling tile renderer, sprites, collision system, inventory/weapons, NPCs and enemy entities. C implementation coordinates segmented modules and interrupt-driven display updates.

MSX2 graphical/text adventure adapted in C from a Spanish-book BASIC listing called Neutronia. Includes English and French versions, graphics, parser vocabulary, location/action state, sound and MSX-DOS disk distributions.

Historical original MSX Asteroids-like game by Eric Boon and Manuel Bilderbeek, preserved as C source with CVS-era revision headers. Contains ship/asteroid/UFO objects, bullets, explosions, collision detection, scoring, shield-energy and level/bonus handling.

Native MSX turbo R raycasting demo game by Wouter Vermaelen and Artrag, also released as ANGRYBOT.COM. Implements fixed-point 64-column ray casting, textured/flat drawing, sprite rendering, movement clipping, dungeon loading and NPC behavior in C with performance-critical Z80 assembly.

Native Amstrad CPC 464 runner by The CiAO Project, written in Z80 assembly with CPCTelera. Separate managers/systems implement scrolling grassfield, levels, player/enemy entities, AI control, physics, collisions, sound, menus, death and victory/restart flow.

Native CPCRetroDev 2019 Amstrad CPC platform game, titled Super Tongueboy in README and Super Tongue Dino in source/configuration. Assembly entity system includes level/obstacle managers, invisibility, player input, enemy behavior, physics, collisions, rendering, deaths and in-game menus.

Native Amstrad CPC 464 roguelike/dungeon-action shooter in Z80 assembly using CPCTelera. Game loop generates levels and rooms, updates player/enemies/attacks, checks bullet, stairs, doors, object and actor collisions, and handles room changes, HUD and game-over state.

Original CPC RetroDev 2016 Amstrad action game source dump with player platform movement, enemy behaviors, collisions, level data, graphics, sound and interrupt routines. Includes a coherent main assembly unit with included subsystems and level/enemy initialization.

Native Amstrad CPC two-player arena-action game from SubXplosion’s 2016 academic project. Large C implementation handles characters Jimmy/Obdulia, controls, movement/collisions, ammunition, shots, keys/doors, arena blocks, rounds, score, menus and music.

Native Amstrad CPC zoo-themed action/collection game in C. The source menu calls it Zoo Clean (and retains Scape text), while repository is zoo-care. Gameplay includes directional movement, bait/attack controls, guard/enemy state behavior, collectibles, cage-opening objectives, lives and level changes.

Original work-in-progress Sierra-style point-and-click adventure for Amiga. Native C includes room loading, text handling, images, custom screen/UI abstraction and a separate vocabulary/room-data compiler. Distinct title from commercial Murder! and from the author's Parrot project.

Original solid-polygon space-trading/combat prototype inspired by Frontier: Elite II. Contains substantial original universe generation, terrain renderer, physics, ports, contracts, combat, save state and ECS/AGA/RTG Amiga backends, rather than an emulated original game.

Preserved original 1993 Amiga game source by Paul Grebenc, uploaded by its author. Full C game loop includes thrust, collision, landing pads, scoring, BOB graphics, keyboard/audio and memory services. This is an independent Amiga implementation, not the indexed C64 Jupiter Lander disassembly.

Compact native custom-screen Amiga game launcher experiment by MrZammler. C source implements manifest/game-list display, gameport joystick navigation and Execute-based launch, with a classic VBCC build. Distinct lightweight interface from full iGame.

From-scratch C++20 recreation of John Calhoun's Macintosh Glider 4 with original house-file compatibility and a separate house editor. Implements its own physics/game state, object behavior, binary house reader/writer, SDL renderer and audio. Independent of Aerofoil, which ports Glider PRO.

Original RISC OS Star Trek-themed spaceship/shooter learning project. Tokenised BASIC application files are accompanied by readable plain-text .bas equivalents with ship movement, shields, phasers, enemies, projectiles, sprites and audio.

Native AmigaOS package manager with CLI, GadTools and MUI interfaces. Portable C core implements signed catalog verification, dependency resolution, recipes and receipts; Amiga layer implements HTTP/AmiSSL downloads and DOS-library install/remove operations. Independent package-manager component extracted from Amiga Imager.

ANSI C AmigaOS game-development library implementing screens, Copper synchronization, IFF loading, icons and graphics.library-compatible BOB/VSprites with custom accelerated blitter/mask operations. Substantial reusable graphics subsystem rather than the author's skeletal Blaster game.

Native Commodore 64 implementation based on Amiga Nuclear Reaction. C/6502 assembly provides atom-placement chain reactions, two-player turns, winner detection, AI search, PETSCII rendering, SID sound and hardware input. Substantial independent game implementation.

Pascal/Foxy native Mega Drive assembly port of ERE's Atari ST poker game. README explicitly credits Foxy's reverse engineering; source implements card/deal evaluation, betting turns, opponent decisions and Sega display/input/audio routines.

Educational native Atari ST C/assembly Flappy Bird recreation with complete staged implementations. Latest stage includes game state/collision, monochrome raster routines, menu, score, PSG effects/music, IKBD input, vectors and VBL timing. Distinct from deferred BBC/Electron binary-only Flappy Bird release.

Tomasz Słanina’s 2007 native WonderSwan Color Snake game, published with its complete 80186-compatible assembly, level data and a C COM-to-cartridge converter. This is original homebrew rather than recovered commercial source.

Original Vectrex homebrew by Brian Jones. A single-cell organism orbits nuclei, jumps between them and tethers the board while avoiding biological hazards; the repository exposes the native game implementation rather than wrapping an old ROM.

Oscar Toledo’s original Zombie Near action game source release, preserving dated development snapshots and native platform versions. The ColecoVision game contains its own Z80 game loop, enemy AI, maps and SN76489 music rather than emulating an existing game.

Native NGPC scrolling-shooter demo built on NGPC Template 2026. Unlike a bare starter template, it contains a substantial distinct shooter implementation, scripted stages, multiple enemy patterns, bosses, graphics and audio.
