A standalone source template extracted from the original OVER REV Neo Geo Pocket Color racer. Promote only the reusable engine/sample in the checked-in ZIP: the full game is distributed as binaries and explicitly has not had its complete source published.

WonderSwan Bad Apple demo with a native banked command-stream/tile video player and interrupt-driven PCM/IMA-ADPCM audio, plus a Java video quantizer. It is native media-player homebrew, not a recovered game executable.

Independent native replacement for the FreyaBIOS/FreyaOS WonderWitch abstraction layer. It aims to make existing freely available WonderWitch software run with third-party WonderSwan cartridges and emulators, with BIOS services, interrupt plumbing and OS/filesystem code.

Oscar Toledo’s CP1610-native replacement BASIC interpreter for the Intellivision Entertainment Computer System. It implements a full-screen editor, tokenized statements, floating-point expressions, graphics, sound and tape I/O.

BASIC-to-CP1610-assembly cross-compiler with its own parser, intermediate-code representation, register tracking, peephole optimizer and native runtime prologue/epilogue. Provides a substantial original retro language toolchain rather than only editor support.
Haskell MIDI importer and converter that maps instruments, quantizes time and allocates available voices, producing IntyBASIC MUSIC statements or a standalone preview program for Intellivision/ECS.

Pre-alpha collection of reusable 6809 routines/macros for Vectrex vector drawing, timers, scoring, text, raw audio and DS2431 EEPROM. It adapts existing routines and some BIOS calls into macros to trade ROM space for cycles.

PC Engine ASM/C SDK with native hardware libraries for sprites, video, scrolling, input, interrupts, audio, storage and mathematics, plus desktop graphics/tilemap/VGM tools and runnable source examples.

Extended pcmenc audio conversion toolkit based on Arturo Ragozini/Daniel Vik’s MSX encoder, adding SN76489 targets, packing methods, banking and cycle-budgeted Z80 replay routines. Actual encoder and native players are present.

Unofficial retranslation/re-localisation of the original Japanese Master System Phantasy Star. The source includes annotated Z80 disassembly, text/graphics reimplementation, grammar-aware multilingual scripts and gameplay/bug-fix patches, not merely released IPS/BPS binaries.

Reusable C89 emulation library for Fairchild F8-family systems, including Channel F. Models the CPU instruction/ROMC machinery and memory, display, beeper, controllers and auxiliary devices; shared by multiple distinct platform frontends.

Native PC-98 DOS agent plus Windows Python CLI and MCP server for bounded hardware/DOS inspection and file/directory transfer over RS-232C. Substantial command parser, DOS memory/device inspection and streaming transfer code; not a shell or game wrapper.

Windows .NET input window and native FreeDOS(98) resident program transmit committed Japanese input into PC-98 BIOS keyboard queues. Contains serial protocol, TSR hooks, IRQ buffering and a device-driver alternative.
Reusable NEC PC-9801/PC-9821 emulator implementing V30/x86 instruction execution, machine bus, disk controllers, GDC/GRCG, YM2608 and compatible BIOS/DOS interception in C#. Not tied to one game.

Host-side wxPython application with actual D88/FDI/HDI/HDM/raw/NHD parsing, FAT12/FAT16 filesystem access, PC-98 IPL/MBR partition detection, hex viewing and controlled writeback. Reusable preservation and inspection tooling.

Rust/wxDragon GUI for detecting and analysing PKLite-packed DOS executables, with a Rust-port bitstream/Huffman/LZ decoder and experimental MZ output reconstruction. Substantial implementation exists, but executable restoration is incomplete.
Complete native DOS tank-combat Pascal program with keyboard/mouse movement, projectiles, collision logic, scores and BGI graphics; original source and data/binary packaging remain available.

Shaun Brandt/Holy Meatgoat Software collection of native DOS projects including Damanoid, Move-it Man, LOCGAED CGA sprite editor and a historical Allegro Tetris. Retained as one repository-level collection, not inflated into one row per directory.
Native Turbo Pascal 7 multimedia/game engine with VGA renderer, widget UI, TMX/PCX/BMP loading, resource manager, XMS, AdLib HSC music, Sound Blaster audio and example XiClone game.

Native Pascal/x86 assembly VGA toolkit covering buffered blitting, BMP images, fonts, keyboard/mouse/joystick, Sound Blaster WAV playback, PC speaker, timer and package I/O, with sample chess, snake and Tetris games.

Author-released Sadist 2 (2000), sequel to Sadist, with original Polish Turbo Pascal code, 2026 English translation, tools and installer scripts. Graphics, XMS storage, mouse and sound units accompany the main game.
Original 2020 game-jam pseudo-3D space shoot-em-up using vanilla DOS DIV Games Studio 2 and mode-7-style presentation. PRG game source and custom Watcom C++ DLL modules are included.

TypeScript browser reimplementation of Ben Freeman’s 1992 DOS BBS door game, retaining original Turbo Pascal source and ANSI art. Implements game-state flow, combat, progression, saving and terminal presentation without emulating a CPU.

Reconstructs the Pascal compiler included in the Dubna monitor from a recovered object module. Includes disassembly, annotated recovery material, Pascal auxiliaries and a direct C++ translation that emits big-endian BESM-6 object modules.

Reconstructs Kurchatov Institute Monitor-80, derived from Dubna, by disassembly and correlation with surviving Dubna sources. Contains substantial assembly and recovered Fortran overlays plus binary comparison and volume construction tooling.

Recovers Pascal-Autocode version 9 (17 May 1988), descended from the first BESM-6 Pascal compiler begun in 1975. The implementation emits Cyrillic-mnemonic autocode for the BESM-6 assembler and includes editor and formatting tools.

Reconstructs TIRAZH, a line-printer document formatting system with rudimentary markup, two-column output, justification and hyphenation. Includes recovered Pascal implementation and decompilation/reassembly scripts.

Recovers the KADRY personnel database system as multiple Pascal programs, including main database commands, questionnaire input, service/help, field formats and report generation. README identifies original binary zones on disk image 2148.

Richard Cornwell's Smalltalk-80 clone based on the Blue Book, with a simplified/custom VM, C bootstrap compiler, native Smalltalk compiler, object memory, image snapshots and a partly finished graphical interface.

Preserves IBM 709 diagnostics covering CPU, indexing, floating point, memory, tape, cards, drums, printer, display and special controls. Includes dated assembly listings, scan images, loader/diagnostic assembler sources and card/tape generation tools.

Cornwell's 1990s X Toolkit widget set developed alongside XMS mail, addressing Athena widget limitations through cascaded menus, selection controls, cached 3D drawing and an extensible widget library.

Leonid Broukhis and Serge Vakulenko's Unix for BK-0010/BK-0011M, derived from revived LSX and Mini-Unix V6 sources. Modernizes ancient C, fixes cross-compilers and relocates the kernel into the BK memory map.

Demos Commander (deco) preserves a two-panel Unix shell file manager with file selection, copying, renaming, viewing, hex viewing and editing. Includes full C implementation, help translations and modern CMake build support.
Modernizes Ken Thompson's SNO compiler/interpreter from the Unix 4 tape. Retains legacy C sources alongside a C++17 implementation and tests, documenting deviations from standard Snobol III.

Matthew Madison's BLISS-M compiler source with parser, macro facility and LLVM backend for the DEC-associated systems language. Repository carries an LLVM 11 update and extensive frontend/backend implementation.

Preserves Steve Hosgood and Terry Barnaby's early-1980s cut-down Unix-like OMU kernel, originally for a homemade 6809 computer and ported to 68000 with multitasking, hard-disk support and UID/GID handling.
Hosts a cleaned-up version of Dave Dunfield's historic Micro-C C-subset compiler, optimizer, preprocessor, libraries and target code generators, aimed at bootstrapping on a modern host.
Original native arcade game in which Mr Aldo catches ceiling rain; source implements waves, character animation, hazards, score, music and fast display primitives.
Chloé Avrillon’s native AY-3-8912 theme adaptation and playback demonstration. Despite repository search description mentioning a game, README and implementation establish a music demo.

T. Zoerner’s own three early VIC-20 games recovered by retyping paper hex dumps, disassembling with dxa, reconstructing labels/comments and repairing code. Keep as one coherent author-restoration collection.
Robert Hurst reconstructed his hand-coded 1984 maze game from recovered cassette data and a VICMON disassembly, aiming for exact reassembly of the original.
Author ops’s 1985 VIC-20 game revisited in 2018, with BASIC game administration and interrupt-driven assembly movement/music. Distinct VIC-20 implementation of the arcade theme.
Annotated disassembly of David Snider’s Serpentine, VIC-20 port by Creative Software, documenting its bitmap-style character rendering and snake/egg/frog systems.

Eleven VIC-20 cartridge games reconstructed with da65 and relabelled for ca65, including relocatable absolute references and split-bank treatment of 16KB titles. Keep as one repository-level disassembly collection.
Dave Curran’s 2026 6502 rewrite of Doug Smoak’s July 1983 Compute! BASIC type-in game. Original BASIC listing and magazine scans accompany the implementation.
Native VIC-20 FiZZ platform-puzzle implementation in Turbo Rascal, with modular object physics, control, lasers/floater/fontaine components and JSON level data.
Marky-D-32’s restored/adapted 6809 two-player droid shooter from the Dragon32 Micropaedia listings in Personal Computer News 27–29 (September 1983), adjusted to CoCo ROM and workspace addresses.
CoCo adaptation of Pat McCabe and Colin Turner’s Dragon User May 1986 knight-move board puzzle, restoring its 6809 assembly and remapping ROM services.
CoCo2 source port of Brian Cadge’s Dragon User June 1984 one/two-player driving game, with documented ROM-call conversion and named recovered game variables.

Howard Price/Tobermory’s 2012 SAM Coupé recreation of Astral/Logotron XOR. Author explicitly says it was started from scratch and nothing was reverse-engineered; predecessor behavior/maps do not imply recovered CPU input.

Malcolm Tyrrell’s original 2011–2012 four-kilobyte real-time puzzle game for unexpanded VIC-20. One-button red/green mood switching controls whether the moving player responds to floor symbols, keys and switches.
A substantial browser-native Amiga-style tracker with independent WebAudio playback, MOD/XM parsing/writing and sample/pattern editors, rather than a hosted original binary.
Native Classic Toolbox PowerPC Mac OS 9 and Win32 gateway/proxy application that supplies modern TLS, mail splicing, Wayback forwarding and tunnels to vintage clients.
Native RSS/Atom reader for PowerPC Mac OS 9 and Windows 95-XP, sharing a portable C engine and using separate native Carbon and Win32 interfaces.
New small-footprint TCP/IP and MacIP stack linked into native Macintosh applications, plus a MacTCP-compatible driver, for a 512Ke with System 6 over LocalTalk.
A native C11 Macintosh II media player with DAAP streaming, AIFF/PCM pipeline, classic Toolbox UI and Apple Event scripting, inspired by the iTunes interface rather than recovered iTunes source.
Classic Mac remote-control/development tool consisting of a tiny native System 7 MacTCP agent and Rust CLI/client/MCP server, with screen, input, file, Apple Event and resource-fork operations.
Substantial derivative of Marcio Teixeira MiniVNC adding native PowerPC CFM builds, Retro68 integration, background operation and true-color wire-format fixes, while retaining classic 68k builds.
A Lazarus/Free Pascal desktop and console utility implementing filesystem-level extraction and mutation for Acorn, Commodore, Amiga, DOS and other retro disk images.
Preserved and maintained ARM relocatable module source controlling VIDC-enhancer oscillator clocks on original Acorn Archimedes RISC OS 2/3 hardware.
Restored 1997-2000 Turbo Pascal-era PC utility that reads and writes physical Archimedes floppy sectors into emulator-compatible disk images, including later F-format improvements.
Independent Java/PlayN implementation of the 1989 Amiga Prospector in the Mazes of XOR, compiled to an HTML5 browser game, with maze rules, renderer, editor and replay handling.
A substantial TypeScript/browser port of the released Macintosh Continuum source, translating game physics, shots, collision and rendering into modules rather than executing the original game binary.
Bare-metal ARM7TDMI port of reconstructed Archimedes Lander, using a Python source transpiler plus custom GBA display/input/RISC OS SWI replacement assembly.
Direct Windows port of John Calhoun released Glider PRO C source, retaining gameplay/house resources while replacing platform UI/audio/rendering and adding resource extraction tools.

Native SM83 assembly game by Bot Randomness. Actual source initializes LCD/VRAM/OAM, scrolls the star field, moves multiple asteroids, reads controls and implements spaceship movement. This is an authored homebrew prototype, not recovered commercial source.

Riley Lannon’s NES assembly project, inspired/guided by the NESdev Galaxy Patrol example. Main source implements a scrolling asteroid/fuel game, game states, player movement and collision handling; an included sound engine remains partial. This is a distinct educational authored version, not a commercial disassembly.

Jesse Williams / tragicmuffin’s Falling, a complete authored NES game in NESASM assembly. Source contains title/play/pause/game-over states, difficulty progression, player/obstacle/pickup logic, graphics and music/sound routines.

Authored NES Snake game with a modular NESASM implementation. Game code covers persistent direction, movement ticks, pause/game-over states, snake growth and rendering, with CHR, palettes and nametables committed alongside it.

Reusable C++ Game Boy emulator targeting Nintendo 3DS. Pinned implementation contains SM83 operand/opcode execution, PPU scanline rendering, cartridge memory banking, APU, timer, joypad, ROM browsing and a platform/core separation. It loads general Game Boy ROMs rather than wrapping one game.

Robert Louie’s reusable TypeScript Game Boy emulator with independent CPU operation families, GPU/APU/timer/memory/cartridge subsystems and browser UI/examples. Gameboy.runFrame coordinates arbitrary cartridge execution and frame rendering rather than embedding one game.

Authored SGDK/C Tetris game for Sega Genesis. Source separates scene management, main menu, music, piece creation/movement/rotation/collision and board rendering, providing substantive gameplay rather than a ROM collection.

Lucas Falcão and Flavio Freitas’s SGDK class-project source for a medieval two-player projectile-parrying game. Actual code contains arena, knight/wizard sprites, directional controls, attack handler and display/physics routines. Distinct from the tracked 1986 Apple II game sharing the title.

Native SGDK/C work-in-progress isometric racing/adventure source by realbrucest. Main loop initializes scenario, car/camera and scrolling; car.c implements rotation-derived velocity, sprite direction frames and motion, alongside scenario, pickup, weapon, enemy, HUD and screen modules.

Authored C/SGDK demake of Paper.io 1 for Genesis, with tile-map territory/path data, human/computer players, movement, claim/fill calculations, score and rendering implemented in src/main.c. Source-level demake rather than game-specific CPU emulation.

Sixteen Bits’s JamToday Almería 2019 native Genesis game. SGDK C source implements stage/state transitions, players/enemies, lives, attacks, input, sprite updates and sounds; committed resources and pipeline make it a concrete source project.

Native Sega Mega Drive Snake implementation in C/SGDK. game.c implements directional steering, level speed, edge/wrap checks, food/bonus placement and self-collision; linked-list body, menu, game-over and win modules accompany graphics/audio resources.
Original modular DOS C89 VGA and Sound Blaster engine, with nine scene demonstrations; useful native retro engine source rather than an emulator wrapper.
Small but complete annotated PC-98 bootable assembly demonstration: prints text and beeps without DOS; includes a reproducible floppy-image recipe.
Author-released historical roughly 11K-line DOS C++ software 3D engine with handwritten inline assembly, clipping, generic rasterization, mipmapping, lighting and terrain demos.

Reusable Windows 9x VxD traps OPL/AdLib and MPU-401 I/O from DOS sessions and streams captured writes to user-mode software audio rendering. Own driver/glue implementation with several bundled synthesis backends.
Preservation repository for the historical JUDAS 2.10d DOS sound library: module/sample playback, software mixers and direct Sound Blaster, GUS, AC97 and HDA hardware support.
Substantial reusable headless Ghidra workflow with an original LE/LX loader, Watcom calling convention specifications, library signatures, PE/DirectX typing and analysis/export/MCP tools.
Original 1991 QuickBASIC text-adventure compiler/interpreter re-released by its author, including a small HOUND demonstration and original source/project files. Distinct historical author network.

Complete source/assets of Max and Morgan McGuire's original Windows artillery game, housed in the xenon directory of Morgan's multi-project archive; inspired by Scorched Earth, not the unrelated Bitmap Brothers Xenon shooter.

Original Python extract/rebuild toolkit for Colonization for Windows (1995) NE resources, custom asset containers, palettes and map previews; reimplements data-format and tile composition behavior without running the game CPU.

Author-published original DOS Game-Maker commercial product sources, runtime, editors and bundled sample games. Includes substantial native engine/gameplay implementation and original Borland build graph.
Turnkey native DOS game/demo development environment integrating DJGPP, CMake/Ninja, VS Code and DOSBox-X with a substantive custom remote GDB serial debugging stub.

Preserved Stacken/KTH Emacs-style screen editor, with Pascal editing modules, MACRO-10 terminal/disk support and native link scripts. This is the historical AMIS editor, unrelated to DOS AMIS resident-service specifications.

SAILDART-recovered TOPS-10 ARPANET NCP, IMP driver, FTP and mail subsystem sources. README credits Robert Sundberg for NCP and Edward Taft for FTP/MAIL; actual IMPSER implementation and native FTP link command are preserved.

Historical cfront 3.0.3 C++-to-C implementation with compiler, runtime and libraries, re-ported from the Plan 9 fourth-edition source distribution. Includes actual parser/simplifier/code printer and staged bootstrap scripts.

Gardens Point Modula-2 compiler frontend with a CIL emitter, preserving the historical compiler lineage while enabling unmanaged Modula-2 applications on .NET. Source includes semantic traversal, parser, CIL writer and C# runtime modules.

Disassembly-recovered CP/M-86 BIOS/BDOS/CCP with frozen, annotated and experimental source variants, plus reconstructed command sources. Includes local patch mapping and native IBM PC XT/V20 MBC output recipes.

Restored Werner Cirsovius CP/M source library, including BASELIB and reconstructed Digital Research ZSID debugger. Current maintainer adds Z180 disassembly support and build integration to recovered source originally distributed as a readable website.

Charles Hedrick and colleagues’ extended-addressing Lisp preserved from Linköping tape images. Extracted source includes actual Lisp compiler, runtime/assembler modules and native TOPS-20 control scripts.

Original BBN Logo assembly source plus MIT modifications and NRC turtle/music adaptations. Actual interpreter source includes storage tables, procedure compilation, turtle terminal support and configuration switches.

DECUS PDP-10 XPL/XCOM 4 source and a modern nexcom.xpl cross-compiler port using an XPL-to-C translator. Preserves actual parser tables, scanner and PDP-10 code emitter rather than only compiler documentation.

Applied Data historical reusable emulator suite written by Bob Supnik, Len Fehskens and Mike McCarthy. Preserved MACRO-10 source contains VM break handling, command editor and machine loaders, alongside minicomputer-specific components.

Stanford University Drawing/Design System source corpus from SAILDART and ITS, containing circuit drawing, wirelisting, layout and routing programs. Inspected DRAW display implementation and WL assembly inclusion manifest provide concrete implementation evidence.

DEC KL10 diagnostic-console program running on the PDP-11 frontend, preserved in MIT and SAIL variants with loader/device modules and console instructions. Reviewed kldcp.20 is PALX-format source assembling actual console modules.

Preserves the John Hall Mine Storm source and adapts the Avocet ASM09 input to the Kingswood as09 assembler; main_loop.asm implements initialization, minefield sequencing and scoring rather than merely wrapping a binary.

A native Vectrex adaptation of the Atari 2600 title Custer’s Revenge. spud.asm contains cartridge setup, input, score, collision, music and game-state implementation, with local vector/data/include files.

Native Vectrex Hexpawn implementation by Dan Siewers, inspired by Robert C. Leedom’s KIM Hexpawn. Source/main.asm implements cartridge startup, a 3×3 pawn board, move state and learned-response storage; a separate Binary/Vexpawn.bin is supplied.

A native C++ Pong implementation by Antonio Maiorano, with paddle movement, collision, sound, scoring, BIOS wrappers and joystick support in src/. The inspected src/main.cpp has a complete frame loop, rather than an empty game template.
Reconstructs the BBC Micro QUEST1 payload in maintained BeebAsm source, with game code, room/entity data, graphics and relocation layout rather than binary includes.
Named 6502 game-engine assembly and decoded rooms/messages/pictures for the 1987 Mystery House release; also preserves 313 lines of original LISA source recovered from stale binary memory.
High-level Rust port of the Amiga Ultima VI executable, with address-mapped combat/game functions, disk intake, rendering and native/wasm frontends; users provide their own game files.
Rewrites disassembled Amiga Populous simulation rules in Swift, including walkers, settlements, fights, conquest progression and powers; reads graphics/sound/text from an owner-provided ADF.
Re-encodes Monkey Island 2 graphics/resources for Amiga OCS constraints, including a real SMAP zigzag encoder and resource rebuild pipeline, using owner-supplied PC/Amiga game material.
Translates the ZX Spectrum Next Jumping Jim game routine by routine into native C64 code; the main source explicitly selects the 6510 CPU and implements game state, input and rendering.
C++/SDL2 engine for the Commodore 64 games Wizard and Ultimate Wizard; source defines monster behaviours, sprites and game state, with original-data and updated-graphics modes.
ACME reconstruction and initial reverse-engineering pass for the C64 game, including 6510 engine/loader, 1541 drive code, combat overlays and four D64 layouts.
Substantial Z80 carrom game with board state, physical shot simulation, scoring, four robot styles and 1-bit sound; source contains actual startup/game tables and IM2 setup.
A source-backed 6502 Snake implementation designed for the Apple II’s 255 usable boot-sector bytes; includes monitor graphics, keyboard control, disk packaging and optional DOS-loadable output.
C map/room parser and interactive editor for the 1990 game, including compressed room structures, tiles, objects, switches and file patching rather than just format notes.

Boriel BASIC native prototype with terrain collision, scrolling rider, keyboard-repeat handling, double-buffered banked screens and stationary enemy sprites; actual loop calls input/rendering rather than being an empty template.
Preserves Nick Hill’s original 1999 Turbo Pascal game with twenty levels, collision/damage/scoring and Borland CRT/Graph code; inspired by an Amstrad CPC game of the same name.
Restores the original DOS Doom 2D C/assembly game and resources, with substantial GAME/GAME.C implementation and historical build scripts.
Bare-metal Naomi system libraries, toolchain setup, video/PowerVR, input, filesystem, threading and debugging code, with real libnaomi/video.c implementation and on-target examples/tests.
Native Naomi puzzle game implementing coloured-light sources, block matching, score/penalty rules and game-over state in C.
Released cdi4dc/mdf4dc disc-image tooling, with actual converter implementation in cdi4dc/src/main.c and associated CD image structures.
Substantial native Dreamcast shell/application suite with boot/runtime initialization in src/main.c, KallistiOS integration and hardware-oriented applications.
Source-based PlayStation SDK continuation, including concrete GPU implementation under libs/libpsx/src/gpu.c and runtime/toolchain packaging.
C PlayStation hardware library with GPU command/runtime source, implemented in src/gpu.c rather than a binary-only SDK bundle.
Jo-Engine C platformer for Saturn with hero collisions, enemies, attacks and map/game state; concrete hero.c implementation exceeds an empty engine starter.
Native SMS engine for Commander Keen 1 with game logic/rendering and original-game asset conversion; actual C main/game source rather than an x86 CPU-emulation wrapper.
SGDK C action-RPG engine/physics prototype with concrete scene implementation, movement and early game systems.
Native Genesis Tetris implementation with board/game state and logic in src/Board.c, rather than a ROM wrapper.
Substantial C tool for reading/recovering and creating ITS DUMP archives, with real archive handling in itstar.c.
Continuation of a 1985 Unix SUPDUP client, with TCP/Chaosnet protocol handling and terminal support in substantial C; includes experimental server work.
University of Hamburg Pascal compiler/runtime source preserved from tape, including readable Pascal and MACRO material under oldpascal/.
TOPS-20 programmable command-language compiler/EXEC extension source, including substantive BLISS-36 execpc and historical build-control files.
Readable IMP/MACRO runtime and library source with command/control build procedures under dec10/imp/. Compiler executables are also present, but do not establish complete compiler source recovery.
1981 MACRO-10 disassembler for PDP-11/MACY11 boot-loader outputs, with substantial readable unpal.m10 implementation.
Substantial historical FORTRAN and MACRO-10 library source, with actual routines in flib.for and maclib.m10 and a maclib.doc API reference.
Stanford-era TENEX backup recovery utility in C, with 36-bit decoding and Unix tape handling in read10xbsys.c and detailed operation notes.
Xerox MAXC/PDP-10-compatible system corpus, including actual monitor assembly, microcode and BCPL/PAL/Alto interface source rather than only tape images.
Historical HAL/S HALMAT IR reconstruction with a C99 interpreter/debugger in emu/halmat_engine.c and OCaml analysis components.

Original Windows 3.x Risk adaptation by Eduardo Joaquín and Miguel Gesteiro, preserved in Borland Pascal source with actual board/graphics/game code. The original RISK.PAS header dates that source to summer 1994.
Reimplements Macintosh Programmer’s Workshop shell syntax and builtins in C++, with real conditional/loop/execution/parser code and an mpw-make entry point.
Source-backed classic Mac/modern-host synchronization tooling with actual red-black file-tree operations, conversion modules and resource-fork/type/creator metadata handling.
Preserves the first-edition book’s ColorIt, NewHiyer and WindMenu Pascal/resource source. ColorIt contains real menu, window, TextEdit and QuickDraw logic rather than an empty hello-world stub.
Preserves the Programmer’s Guide to MPW Creation application, with substantial Pascal event/menu/window/TextEdit/printing logic and resource/build files.
Reviewed the game-specific static 68000-to-Swift translator, generated-code boundary and Amiga hardware runtime before considering a catalogue promotion.
Author-maintained Ruby/SDL continuation of a 1994 Turbo Pascal maze game. Atari ST is an inspiration reference, not the target.
ASP.NET Core/SignalR remake with a client raycaster and server-authoritative multiplayer. No binary equivalence claimed.
C128 adaptation of the author's deconstructed C64 version, with disk save/load. README discloses Claude and Copilot assistance.
Author-retyped 1989 magazine BASIC game with MSX compatibility. MIT re-release; not independently executed.
Original MSX BASIC homebrew with editable ASCII source and packaged ROM version. Source publication, not a commercial-game decompilation.
DOS COM disassembly with TASM-style source, includes and an IDA database. Generic labels and resource dependencies remain.
DOS assembly reconstruction with timer routines, many generic labels and explicit unresolved hard-coded-offset constraints. Modified startup means no byte-exact claim.
Named functions/globals, structure specifications and Ghidra scripts for DOS, Win95 and Saturn builds. This is an analysis corpus, not a completed source port.
Preserved 1995 Portfolio operating-system source snapshot. Repository attributes the public release to EagleSoft; public availability does not establish an open-source licence.
Collection of BIOS sources/listings for Soviet computers and DEC Rainbow. Architecture varies by component; buildability is not claimed for the collection.
Native ShareFS protocol implementation for modern hosts serving RISC OS clients. README documents x64/arm64 builds; GPL-3.0-only. Scoped Copilot instructions are present.
Matching-oriented decompilation with original-era compiler investigation. Not a playable port; compiler-version uncertainty remains. Successor to pds-tools, distinct from asset tooling.
Partial shiftable reconstruction with SH4 function tests and matching build targets; combines recovered functions with original code and requires user game data.
Dreamcast/KallistiOS port based on k4zmu2a's SpaceCadetPinball decompilation, with documented text-panel rendering issues.
Dreamcast adaptation of n64decomp/mk64 with hardware audio and PowerVR backend. Author reports physical-hardware testing; independent execution not performed.
RGBDS disassembly with documented US ROM and patch identities, assembly instructions and CI. Matching is author-documented, not independently verified here.
RGBDS disassembly with models, graphics compression and a stripped build. Unreferenced content, script pointers and English/prototype differences remain unfinished.
RGBDS reconstruction with named interrupts, banked assembly, build comparison and remaining baserom INCBIN regions.
Banked Game Boy disassembly generated using mgbdis, with target digest and assembly scaffold. Semantic annotation completeness is not established.
Banked disassembly with RAM/VRAM maps, structure definitions, compression and audio notes; explicit conventions favour meaningful names and why-comments.
Disassembly of the SELF TEST WCS diagnostic ROM using the author's SNES ROM Framework; requires original ROM for asset extraction.
N-SPC/Kankichi-kun sound-driver reconstruction with named VCMD macros and patch tables, drawing on SDK and Yoshi's Island analysis. Audio CPU, not Super FX game logic.
Work-in-progress Asar reconstruction of v1.0; original ROM required and revisions 1/2 explicitly unsupported. SHA1 comparison target supplied.
ca65/spcasm source with US retail, localisation prototype and Japanese configurations. C decompilation is future work, not present completion.
Inactive partial reconstruction of the GOG release. Several small modules complete by author report while major engine/game modules remain incomplete; not byte-accurate.
Barnyard and Toshi 2.0 engine decompilation with Windows build instructions, engine library, SDK and developer tools.
Readable Java reconstruction with extracted-resource tooling and Jademula Windows layer. Explicitly targets behaviour rather than identical bytecode.
Japanese-version reconstruction with C sources, assembly portions, linker scripts and graphics/audio build pipeline. Supplied ROM identity does not establish completion.
SourceGen banked-ROM analysis focused on SmartPort extraction for Mega IIe, with symbol files and linked HTML listings. Use original author repository, not the fadden copy.
Native CPCTelera game source with input, collision, turn/map and music systems. Main code credits Antonio Corpas Cuenca and LGPLv3-or-later.
Commented NASM reconstruction of a 3552-byte directory utility with DOS/BIOS simulation fixtures. Kaypro provenance is described as believed, not certain.
HDD/HDI/NHD/SLH emulator image-header readers/writers and FAT partition boot-sector inspector; standalone format scripts rather than a full filesystem implementation.
WAV/PCM conversion and packing for PC8/PPC/P86/PPS plus PC-98 playback examples. Distinguishes soundboard formats and sample constraints.
Root contains only .gitignore and LICENSE. Revisit when actual source or an author release appears.
README identifies mwenge/matrix and links its source/releases; no distinct contribution established in this pass.
README explicitly moves the project to already tracked a2stuff/prodos-drivers.
README credits Bald Engineer and links the original repository; track the author source added in this batch.
README explicitly marks this as the legacy predecessor of already tracked blythos/atolm. Asset extraction progress must not be read as a completed playable decompilation.
Pokitto remake of the C64 puzzle game; main.cpp and level/graphics headers are present. Bundled library binaries mean this is not a self-contained library-source release.
Reusable assembly definitions for C64 KERNAL, BASIC, SID, VIC, CIA and 1541 DOS/VIA interfaces; a development include library, not a game disassembly.
Collection of small CPC BASIC games including Moonlander, Emergency and Hanoi. Source listings are present alongside a disk image; kept as one coherent collection.

Control-flow-traced MSX cartridge disassembly with named game logic and regional listings. Author reports exact 16KB rebuilds but warns region/build attribution remains unsettled. Separate implementation from the tracked ricbit/antarctic listing.
Traced cassette reconstruction with loaders, relocated game blocks and annotated embedded Loriciels monitor. Author supplies tape rebuild and coherence checks; original tape is user-supplied.
Annotated MSX cassette disassembly covering Spectrum-derived loader and relocated game blocks. ZX lineage is documented without classifying this as a separate Spectrum restoration.
Early behavioural reconstruction of Miika Virpioja's Wings 1.40, not the unrelated Amiga Wings. Ship/terrain source and differential-test harness are present; whole-game completion is not claimed.
ROM and installer disassembly inputs, labels and build recipe for the Apple II Sider/Xebec SASI interface. Listing generation depends on the author's separate disassembler.
Dreamcast port derived from sonicdcer/sf64, with PowerVR backend and AICA audio code. README targets real hardware, requires the user's N64 ROM and does not promise Dreamcast-emulator support.

Disc-driven executable reconstruction with symbol/asset maps and C equivalents. Checked source still has generic FUN labels; byte-identical baseline and equivalent C progress are distinct. README's no-game-code wording coexists with checked-in small C functions.

Early independently authored Macintosh-compatible ROM project. README explicitly limits M1 to a diagnostic reset image; a bootable Macintosh replacement and proposed Amiga/ST hosts are not established.
Annotated prototype SFX-100/Nintendo PlayStation BIOS with WLA-DX build and configurable original/fixed behaviour, translations and diagnostic fixes.
Bank-organized vanilla Arcana listing plus DiztinGUIsh project, event scripts and audio sources. README identifies remaining unknown data; semantic completion is not inferred from source presence.
Asar-based SNES disassembly integrated with the author's ROM framework, game-specific RAM/ROM maps and asset extraction scripts. Separate from tracked Amiga and Apple IIgs ports.
Substantive laserdisc-game research on sprite pages, palette, phrases and memory layouts, with image-bank reconstruction assembly. Not a complete game-code restoration.
Function maps, circuit-format documentation and Ghidra import scripts for three arcade 68000 programs and Saturn SH-2 port. No decompiled C or complete source rebuild is distributed.
Portable Z80 assembly OS with kernel, drivers, filesystem, target configurations and SDK examples; native source development rather than binary reconstruction.
Unix-like CP/M shell written with MESCC Small-C, including pipelines, aliases and built-in or external commands. Not a replacement Unix kernel.
Maintained UnoDOS disk kernel source used by Chloe 280SE firmware, with divMMC ROM/system components and RASM build directions.
Kermit-80 port for RSX180/280 with MAC assembly source and transfer/terminal commands. Author reports P112 Z180 and Z280RC tests; those were not rerun here.
Defeat-animation candidates and controlled far-call group experiments reviewed without expanding exactness credit.
Dark Chronicle/Dark Cloud 2 PAL decompilation and native port, with separate PS2 and host build/run paths requiring the user's disc image.
Documented Claude-assisted analysis of Gauntlet II sound bytecode, with disassembly, score/MIDI extraction and YM2151 rendering tools. Scope is the audio subsystem, not the main game.
Original Atari 2600 duck-dodging game with DASM source and Stella build/run recipe. Search returned it for Atari ST, but primary README identifies 2600.
Keyboard and analog-control modifications derived from Lorenz Wiest's reversed Star Raiders source; actual modified assembly is present.
Asset editor for Landstalker ROMs and the author's companion disassembly: maps, sprites, text and other data, with documented per-format limitations.
Early disassembly with build scripts and bytecode tables. Author explicitly warns it is not shiftable and not yet suitable for major projects.
Native C128 80-column VDC memory game; inspected Kick Assembler source uses C128 KERNAL VDC calls and explicit card state.
Network Pong with ACME C64 clients and Python host server. Author explicitly reports instability on real WiC64 hardware and success only in emulators.
Collection porting the author's Amiga games using Atari graphics/audio/OS compatibility layers. Requirements vary by game from ST through Falcon CT60; not all games target baseline ST.
README explicitly describes a cut-down DOS emulator for unmodified F1GP, not decompilation. Hold for game-specific-emulation audit rather than promote as restored source.
Phaser browser game; CPC mentions describe music/font credits, not a CPC target or historical-game restoration.
GitHub contents API reports the repository is empty. Name alone does not establish available source.

Early scaffold with extraction and splitting artifacts. Inspected src/main.c contains an empty game_loop and illustrative initialization; need stronger recovered implementation evidence before promoting broad matching claims.
README title and asset URLs point to ToBee while gameplay calls itself Raimbo. Resolve project identity/lineage before adding.
README makes extensive complete-matching claims; recursive tree evidence was not returned in usable form. Source scope and repeated-body accounting need a focused check before promotion.
OCS/ECS assembly engine with Tiled conversion pipeline, BOBs, ProTracker playback and rewind code. Author targets A500/A600/A2000 with Chip plus Fast RAM; baseline performance claims were not tested.
Direct-hardware A500 engine source; inspected Engine.c contains custom-chip access, bitmap/sprite state and input setup, with PTPlayer assembly.
Small Amiga Intuition board/graphics prototype with object movement and collision code. Main runs a fixed 200-frame demonstration; not presented as a finished game.

3DO executable reconstruction using original executable/debug symbols, intentionally enhanced with timing, scene controls and audio changes. Author explicitly says this is not preservation-level matching.
SDL/CMake engine and editor for a Lost Vikings fan project. README identifies missing supplementary files and old build dependencies; a complete playable release is not established.
Annotated X-Terminator 2.1 cartridge firmware with device RAM structures, scanner state, code format and optional English font. Game accessory firmware, not a game.

Emulicious-derived Columns sound-engine listing with voice/channel structures, PSG registers and envelope/vibrato annotations. Remaining unknown flags are explicit; distinct from full SMS Columns disassembly.
Commented Mark Cooksey engine/data disassembly with WLA-DX integration. Author reports matching audio data, not a playable full game; separate voice sample routine is not covered.
Early WLA-DX disassembly for US/EU Sonic Blast; ROM-splitting and build scripts exist. Japanese G Sonic support remains prospective.
CDL-guided ca65 disassembly tooling implemented in Lua and Notepad++ scripts. README pins tested editor/plugin versions and warns newer versions may fail.
Trax-derived Zelda II listing packaged with ca65/ld65 build scripts and CHR extraction; original disassembly attribution is retained.
Regional NES/Famicom disassembly with Japanese and English asset splitting and NES2 output. Separate from SNES Mother 2; user-supplied ROMs required.
ca65 reassemblable listing guided by Mesen CDL. README explicitly documents ambiguous code/data and limited semantic annotation; exact reconstruction is not equivalent to full understanding.
ca65 source for original NTSC and revision A, with asset extraction and make-test comparison; distinct from tracked game-specific recompilation.
Author-released Jaguar puzzle-game source with game/core libraries and resources. Most levels and webcode generation are deliberately omitted.

Modernized historical Club Drive source supplemented by retail-ROM recovery of missing files. README discloses leaked-source lineage and LLM assistance; source presence does not establish redistribution rights.
Historical Small C, assembler, tools, window library and VAL linker sources, with original notices and build relationships. One coherent compiler-toolchain collection.
Source-based improvement of the author's BBC Manic Miner disassembly, with rendering, timing, collisions, music and Master compatibility changes.
BBC Jet Set Willy disassembly-derived enhancements, including relocated consolidated source, graphics/music corrections and documented crash fixes.
C# reconstruction/visualization of Exile's world-generation algorithms and original map data, derived from Tom Seddon's analysis. Explicitly not a full game.
Unfinished 1993 BBC Micro game by Rich Talbot-Watkins and Matt Godbolt, preserved as original disk and decoded/combined source. Inspected AllSource includes BASIC-hosted assembly.
W.R. Hutsell's VGA strategy game source modernized from QuickBASIC/PDS to QB64. README treats Mac/Linux support as theoretical; only documented Windows target retained.
1995 DOS source with modern compatibility layer and Zig build recipes. README distinguishes compilation success from incomplete SDL/audio and potentially crashing stub runtime.
Author's text-based DOS RPG source including WILD.BAS and story/data files. Development requests and unfinished features remain explicit.
Portable C Atari 2600/7800 disassembler with tracing, hardware labels, configuration overrides and optional cycle comments. Bank-switching/file-size limits remain documented.
Annotated 6809 analysis, graphics decoding and Python tooling for Ken Kalish's game, alongside a Pytch adaptation. Author documents unresolved illegal-opcode behaviour and other uncertainties.

Ciaran Anscomb's observation-based rewrite for Dragon/CoCo, with asm6809 build and released source archives. Code is MIT; derived BBC graphics/music/level assets are explicitly excluded from that grant.
Modern Go/Ebitengine library inspired by fantasy consoles. README explicitly targets modern hardware; an Amiga search hit is not an Amiga engine.
Recursive tree contains only README, licence and gitignore. No game source implementation is present despite the project description.
README explicitly pivots to whole-program ARM60 static recompilation with a Portfolio/3DO runtime. Hold for game-specific recompilation audit rather than label recovered high-level source.
Two BASIC listings have machine-code USR entry points but no README, provenance or corresponding machine-code source. Source completeness/lineage needs clarification.

6502 gameplay port from the Atari ST original, with mapped routines and headless comparison tooling. Author reports full game except title music; shape data still extracted from original media. Source inspected, no independent runtime or equivalence verification.
Incomplete C++23/SDL3 reconstruction focused on the Muralla town sequence. GRP decoder implementation and source tree inspected; not a complete game.

One minigame only. Rust simulation cites recovered DOS addresses but explicitly substitutes xorshift RNG and approximates timing at 35 Hz. AI-assisted REA workflow; do not call it exact gameplay reproduction.
C# port from original Turbo Pascal 1.31 source, with Pascal-referenced combat code and oracle tests. Author says core simulation complete with some UI stubs. Not a binary decompilation.
START.EXE resident full-state model and composed Unicorn/DOSBox-X validation reviewed without whole-game inference.
NES revisions 0/1 and GameCube variant disassembly, not the arcade source. Named entity/controller RAM inspected. Documentation incomplete; graphics must be extracted separately.

Work-in-progress disassembly of the unlicensed Famicom adaptation, distinct from SNES SMW. Named object velocity behavior exists; substantial code remains undocumented and ROM asset extraction is required.

NES Game Genie firmware with reset/controller/NMI routines and build/comparison scripts. bank.asm contains source; wrapper incbins reference generated bank data. Some registers and routines remain unidentified.
Banked assembly plus a BizHawk research/TAS script. Author calls byte coverage complete but commentary crude; semantic completeness and independent assembly not established.
C# source/asset IDE for Star Fox SNES, with ASM parsing, graphics and level tooling. Requires separately supplied original source/assets; tool is not itself a recovered game.
RGBDS disassembly with named screen state machine, engine, audio and data. README specifies a target ROM hash; no independent assembly performed.
Disassembly with named sprite assets, script tooling and RGBDS build instructions; author checksum is a build target rather than independently verified evidence.
Named card constants, audio and game source; build targets include Japanese original and Japanese/English Early Days Collection variants. Matching claims attributed to README.
Early semantic analysis of Japanese Harvest Moon GB. README reports only 99 of 12635 labels meaningfully named (0.78%); banked assembly exists but should not be presented as fully understood source.
Partial modding/randomizer-oriented disassembly, with named trigger tables and original ROM dependency. Trigger argument meanings remain partly unknown.

Three-CPU arcade research with raw and annotated listings, HUD bytecode semantics, graphics decoder and MAME tracing scripts. Listing format includes addresses/opcodes and is not proven reassemblable. Repository explicitly discloses Claude use.
Disassembly, source patch fragments and population balancing notes. Observed population-table semantics and debug patches; no full-source completeness claim.
M50734/740-family firmware analysis, resident font extraction and ROM maps. Annotated reset/port logic inspected; author coverage/understanding claims not independently validated.
Original author's arcade game source, with game manager, sprite/collision and graphics code. Historical PRC-tools build; non-commercial release conditions, not unrestricted open-source licensing.
Original author's card game source under stated MIT terms, with bidding/play AI and CodeWarrior Palm OS project. Modern build not verified.

Annotated tape reconstruction with split relocated game source, address-anchored notes and build/tests. Upstream claims byte-exact reassembly; original tape not distributed and claims not independently run.
Recovered 63-line tokenized MSX BASIC game plus Z80 helpers/loaders. Commented BASIC and retokenization verification distinguish it from an all-assembly game. Upstream completeness claims attributed.
Annotated Konami RC-705 8K cartridge source, anchored notes and verification tools. Upstream reports byte-exact build and full coverage; ROM required separately.
Konami RC-718 annotated 16K cartridge listing with named data ranges, entry points and script decompression tooling. Author matching/coverage figures not independently reproduced.
Konami RC-721 annotated listing including interior-instruction target equates, named ranges and decompression tools. Original ROM required; upstream coverage claims attributed.
ASM68K reworking of moxniso's SNASM68k disassembly, with named vectors/registers and documented lineage. Author matching claim excludes 14KB hardware padding.
Work-in-progress bank/data/music source with named interrupt vectors and configurable USA build. Documentation and semantic completeness not asserted.

Preservation archive of Segher's CIC analysis and SuperCIC key/lock implementations. Source identifies PIC16F630/676 targets and upstream authors. This is an attributed archive, not newly authored research or a 65C816 program.

Mark Reed editor sources covering commands, keyboard, display, disks, menus and printing. Main source identifies version 1.2 while README describes additions in 1.1; do not treat documentation version as current program version.

Restored CP/M for the Quorum Spectrum clone, including BIOS, BDOS, CCP and bootloader. Author reports identical disk image and emulator boot; retained as upstream claims without independent build.

Modern compiler rebuilding historical CP/M utilities to Z80 assembly and relocatable objects. Inspected compiler integrates frontend, AST/peephole passes and calling-convention checks. Output-size comparisons and full-language claims are upstream, not independently verified.

Driver-format research and MIDI extraction tool with sequence/channel documentation. Several commands unknown and converter tempo is approximate; not a complete driver reconstruction.

Small linker with GEMDOS header/relocation output written in Lisp. README lists relocation/alignment checks and general formats as unfinished; not a mature universal linker.

ROM-driven tracer/generator and evidence modules; game-derived code is generated locally, not committed. Facts separate USA and EU layouts; progress does not imply full semantics or native port.
