Fresh-search slice. Exact repository query `Atari ST homebrew source` returned no repositories. Exact code query `Atari ST homebrew` was noisy but a curated link trail led to the promoted Atari Dev Studio repository, whose primary README establishes Atari 2600/7800 rather than ST scope.

Game-agnostic extraction of instruments from SWIV, Turrican II and Superfrog projects. ADF/HUNK readers, checksum-aware unpackers, conservative 68000 walking, MCP and capture comparison are implemented. Recompiler is explicitly a prototype with a restricted blitter/custom-chip model; unmodelled accesses are logged, not proof of a complete native game port.
Reads and writes DSK/EDSK through the Linux floppy-controller interface. Standard and some unusual geometries are documented; faithful recreation of every protection scheme remains future work.
Historical Z80 syntax checks, vasm symbol extraction and additional graphics/sound helpers. The regex checker explicitly is incomplete, not a full assembler frontend.

Archived educational static-analysis collection of DOS-era specimens. The author describes removing destructive disk-overwrite code, so these are modified analytical listings, not byte-exact original binaries. No specimen was assembled or executed.

Converts planar four-bit cursor images to/from PNG, with splitting/consolidation that preserves unknown leading header data. Travel Junction is the primary target; Pia Carrot MOUSE.DAT is additionally documented.
Queries and changes Human68k DOS console, IOCS display and GraphicMask settings. Source explicitly selects .cpu 68000.
Error-diffusion conversion respects Oric 240×200 graphics attributes and emits TAP with an optional BASIC loader plus BMP preview. Runs as GrafX2 script or command-line Lua.

Inspects/extracts CMD groups, modifies groups and converts flat/H86 input. The 8080 model name is a CP/M-86 loading model, not proof of an 8080 target CPU. exe2cmd is specifically constrained to a Personal CP/M-86 BDOS small-model image, not a general DOS application converter.
A callable 6809 single-instruction decoder with pointer-based string output, not an interactive host disassembly suite.
BRR encoder/decoder and SPC sample extraction, with resampling, loop handling and optional Gaussian filtering. PS1 audio support appears only as a future plan.

Native sound-sequence tests exercise tone, envelope, sweep, waveform, noise and terminal routing. Implemented channel routines provide timed register sequences; this is a test input suite, not an emulator implementation or independently validated fidelity result.
Source expands the sparse README: mapping/DPLC tools, artwork splitting/recoloring, FM voice handling and SMPS-to-assembly conversion are present.
Recovered host-side ADPCM encoding/decoding and codebook/table-design sources. The visible tree does not represent every SDK developer tool, nor a Nintendo 64 game decompilation.
Work-in-progress matching C reconstruction with game-state implementation and asset recovery. Upstream explicitly warns that hardcoded addresses limit shiftability and large-scale mods.
Combines component P/S/M/V/C ROM files into NeoSD .neo containers with metadata. Exotic images including Bad Apple and possibly SS5 Perfect are documented exceptions.
Translation patch materials include script/font extraction, assembly modifications and disc reconstruction. Honorifics flag also selects original versus translated images.

Converts multiple chip/music formats into SAP-R and low-overhead POKEY playback. It explicitly does not make POKEY an exact SID/AY emulator; timer-driven effects, digidrums and rapid envelopes have limits.
Maintained continuation of Torsten Jager fat95 3.18 for FAT12/16/32, with MBR/GPT integration. A filesystem handler is distinct from the required low-level device driver.
Historical font editor port now edits PSF-style VGA-console fonts through curses. Source and README preserve Atari ST ancestry, but current code is not advertised as an Atari executable.
Native screen editor with machine-specific terminal/input adaptations. Text is kept in available TPA; functionality can be configured out to conserve space.
Original PAL source made readable/buildable with xa65. Mixed BASIC/assembly and relocatable output are separate flavours, not simultaneous features.

Annotated engine relocated to RAM, with optional Sargon 2.1 CP/M opening-book replacement. Source explains the original missing book-table byte and changed RESTORE behaviour; this is not an unchanged cartridge reconstruction.
Redirects existing AppleShare FST traffic through TCP/IP rather than replacing the FST. AFP 2.0/optional 2.2 compatibility is explicit; AFP 3.x-only servers are unsupported.

Preserves scans, OCR article and typed BASIC compiler listings from 1985. Maintainer explicitly reports failure even on a small BORDER example and suspects transcription or original-listing errors; working tape version remains missing.
Views/extracts Theme Park floppy/CD sprites, palettes, animation and sound resources. Music playback is explicitly experimental.

Small source-only header inspector prints magic, table pointers, entry address and name. Direct indexing/name scanning lacks a clear malformed-input bounds guard, so it is not a robust universal dump validator.
WAV decoding/encoding, raw-program conversion and BASIC listing with documented cassette format and debug-wave diagnostics.
General multi-system emulator rather than a game-specific emulation port. Source has Z80, 6502, VDP and sound components; guest machines share hardware but have individual media and BIOS constraints.
Inspects/edits RTI instruments and builds RMT banks through a real tracker-driver/emulated-6502/POKEY chain. Source describes working copies and explicit bank saves rather than overwriting originals.
C# library models PRG memory, bookmarks, characters and assembler/disassembler operations, with a related sprite editor. It is not a complete C64 emulator.
libfuse/ADFlib filesystem for OFS/FFS volumes. Defaults to read-write; read-only requires -o ro. Single-thread operation is enforced because concurrent writes can corrupt images.
Wraps m68k-linux-gnu-gcc-8 assembly output and custom gas68k assembler to produce TOS PRG files. It cannot link multiple object files; source inclusion is the documented workaround.

Translates CHIP-8 opcodes to Z80 ROM plus runtime, with ACIA text rendering of the 64×32 display. Translation direction is CHIP-8→Z80, not Z80→host; shipped game inputs do not prove full compatibility.

Interpreted Lisp implementation includes evaluation, reading, printing and mark/sweep GC. README marks tail calls/GC done but notes no string type and inadequate error handling; compilation examples are incomplete.

Manual address/data permutation and bounded heuristic Auto-Fix for scrambled EPROMs. Auto-Fix is explicitly Z80-only despite additional decoder modules; known wiring patterns are tried before general search. Confidence threshold is described as uncalibrated, not proof of universal recovery.
Library/CLI for CoCo DECB virtual disks, file extraction/insertion and formatting. It says JVC format but explicitly neither creates nor recognises a JVC header.
Fork of the tracked moralrecordings Applesoft BASIC detokenizer. Inspected implementation does not establish a separate project identity.
Compared with BackupTheBerlios/dsktools: one added README commit only, no code changes. Promote original source archive once.
False platform match: ARM JIT for BBC micro:bit, not the 6502 BBC Micro. module.json names microbit dependencies.

Generic screenshot translation pipeline rather than PC-98 binary/format restoration. Backend uses local Qwen inference and hardcoded local paths; README references absent requirements files. AI inference is not evidence of AI-authored implementation. Retain only as a lead until a distinct preservation/development role is established.
Historical tracker source archive with two differently aged source trees. Author cannot confidently identify the final version; src-q/ad.c explicitly is not the version used in AProSys.

Streams SEQ/PRG files through variable-length text replacement. The README contains the actual BASIC listing, despite the tree otherwise presenting PRG files. BASIC links can be repaired; fixed-offset machine code is not safe after length changes.

Qt waveform/block interface supports processing selections, noise/frequency controls, filtering, channel changes and TAP output. Source is substantive despite no README. WAV parser expects specific PCM/chunk layouts, not arbitrary audio formats.
TZX/TAP/CSW to PZX, PZX to WAV, and editable textual pulse/block representation. Documentation specifies TZX 1.20 and CSW 1.01/2.00; do not infer support for future revisions.
Builds a DFS SSD image from files with load/execute addresses and optional generated !BOOT. Fixed 80-track, 10-sector, 256-byte geometry is not universal Acorn disk-format support.

Archive/disk inspection, extraction and conversion with format-identification and nested-container handling. CLI and Windows GUI have different host support; format recognition is not universal read/write support.

Converts standard 35-track, 16-sector, 256-byte DSK input to WOZ2. Source-level defect: extension loop overwrites has_p and has_dot from the same character, making their conjunction false; documented ProDOS-order detection is not established as working.
Reads classic pre-OS-X resource-fork types, names and data. AppleDouble handling in inspected implementation assumes a fixed layout; do not infer full modern filesystem/container support.

Historical DOS-to-C decompiler substantially reworked with a Qt frontend and MZ/PSP loading. Memory models, arrays and recovery remain constrained; historical binaries do not establish that current source builds.

Recovers BASIC from BRUN30 QuickBASIC 3 executables, including COMMON chains and floating-evaluation-order preservation. BCOM30 /O is unsupported; multi-module binaries only recover the first module. Some constant-index arrays become scalars, changing layout.

Two-disk translation rebuild handles PRECO on Disk A and FAT12 on Disk B, with input hash checks, script/image changes and IPS output. ERC VFD is a container, not an HDM rename; emulator in-memory saves require explicit flushing.

OS-9/DECB disk tools and historical ROM/compiler sources. Microware C material explicitly needs work; optional DiskShed GUI has a separate build. It is not uniformly complete simply because several components work.
Historical debugger continuation with symbol loading, terminal adaptation and a conditional HD64180/Z180 build. Version 4.2 fixes symbol files ending exactly at a record boundary.

Assembler covers several 6800/6801/6809/6301/6309/68HC11-family modes and binary, Intel HEX, S-record and FLEX relocatable outputs. RELASMB compatibility was reverse engineered and is not an exhaustive compatibility guarantee.

Combines SNES ROM mapping, labels and emulator trace/CDL information including 65816 register-width context. Importer respects the selected mapping rather than retaining inconsistent detected offsets.

RGBDS assembly reconstruction of the USA 1 MiB MBC5 CGB-only game. Named routines and asset boundaries are present; author byte-exact and coverage totals are not independent verification. Unreferenced bytes retain unknown purpose.

Loads bitmap/TGA and width-height-prefixed 16-bit texture data, converts Saturn colors/textures, writes PNG/TGA and handles selected transparency. Sparse README is supplemented by implementation evidence.

Native SH-4 port using recovered OOT game code, PowerVR display-list translation and AICA audio. Display-list interpretation is not MIPS CPU emulation. Only gc-eu-mq-dbg input is documented, not every retail ROM.

Work-in-progress reconstruction targets the July 12 NTSC-J prototype, not all retail variants. Source includes main game and IOP-module interfaces. Hardcoded overlay addresses and unrecovered details remain.
Historical homebrew Tetris source with 68000 host code and GPU game/rendering components, continued with newer tooling. Not a commercial game decompilation.
Reusable extraction/repacking, graphics, text, compression and patch helpers. WonderSwan implementation splits 64 KiB banks and recalculates checksums; other platforms have individual constraints.
Converts indexed BMP to WonderSwan Color chunky tiles, optionally deduplicating mirrored map tiles; -4col emits monochrome planar data. Output modes must not be conflated.
Early recovered functions and overlay configuration for USA Rev 0 YLZE01. Original ROM supplies unrecovered material; presence of a build system does not mean the game is fully reconstructed.
Native DS/DSi adaptation of the reverse-engineered Space Cadet engine. Full Tilt CADET data is reported nonworking, and DS downscaling/light issues differ from DSi.
Hex-Rays MIPS microcode extension for selected Allegrex operations including bitrev, mfic, min/max and wsbw. mtic and instructions in delay slots remain unsupported.
ROM rework of historical GSFORTH includes subroutine-threaded Forth and block storage with readable 6502 assembly. Modern changes mean it is not an unchanged 1983 binary.
Port derived from Acornsoft Forth disassembly, retaining a 6502 host stub while running Forth on the Z80 second processor. Interactive but incomplete, with unit tests documented.
Reads WAV samples into tape streams, flags suspect bits/checksums and renders tokenized BASIC. Editing and TAP/WAV export are TODOs, despite the broader repository description.

Rosanne-native capture draws glyphs on white/black backgrounds, reads pixels and metrics, then creates BDF and pixel-outline TTF. It does not extract original scalable-font outlines. Captured fonts/OS files are not shipped.
Pocket Linker parallel-port cartridge backup/write/verify source. Current master is explicitly untested by the maintainer because suitable parallel-port hardware is unavailable.

Generates batch files, assembly and file lists to combine prepared images/audio into MACS animation. It orchestrates existing image/ADPCM/assembler/linker tools rather than implementing every converter itself.

Collection of BASIC listing converters, not a single full interpreter. Microsoft dialect testing varies; Sorcerer/Nascom/OSI variants are explicitly untested and ZBasic token maps incomplete. Top-level README describes ancestry rather than full current scope.
Unified Acorn disk/archive/BASIC toolkit with DFS/ADFS/AFS components and metadata-preserving ZIP handling. Parser resolves SparkFS, INF and filename metadata; per-filesystem operations differ.

Modern Lua/LOVE2D visual editor imitates retro aesthetics, but inspected sources do not establish native retro output or a reversing/preservation role. Do not infer native platform support from styling.

Saturn research and Jo Engine tutorial/example collection, not a separately buildable implementation in the inspected tree. Retain as a research source rather than promote a duplicate engine/tool project.
Archived package explicitly moved into rob-smallshire/oaknut. Promote the coherent canonical monorepo once; preserve old import namespace and migration relationship.

Related native ROM sources include serial/user-port filing systems and restored sideways-RAM management. Board-specific features are conditionally omitted; HostFS serial polling has timing limitations.

Source examples and reusable graphics routines with Node/VSCode tasks that assemble, replace files in a disk image and launch AppleWin. This is a development workflow, not a new assembler or game reconstruction.

CMD/BASIC/raw disassembly, annotation/JSON IR, assembler and deterministic emulator feed observed coverage back into analysis. Recursive descent leaves unreached bytes unknown and diagnoses overlaps. Web and MCP interfaces share core libraries.
Converts among D64, G64, P64, FDI, NIB and KryoFlux streams, with track/pulse diagnostics. Sector representations cannot preserve physical information absent from their format.
Core track/sector writer with CBM DOS directory, extra-track and separator modules; supports per-file placement/interleave. Unknown options can be silently ignored because modules interpret them.

macOS converter implements platform-specific image layouts and native exports rather than merely retro visual filters. Inspected CPC source exposes mode-specific packing and palette processing; other mode and disk claims are upstream documentation, not exhaustive validation.
Annotated reconstruction of the BBC sideways ROM for a 68000 cross assembler. Python explicitly loads the ROM as 65C02: 68000 is the generated instruction set, not the CPU executing this ROM.
Port of UNLZEXE supporting LZEXE 0.90/0.91 MZ/ZM images, reconstructed relocation tables and bounds-checked input. Not a universal DOS unpacker or C decompiler.
Extracts/edits Shift-JIS text and patches halfwidth display for vanilla VG2 and the Perfect Collection revision. Offsets differ between versions and must be re-extracted.

Sparse source-only translation workspace. Inspected Lodoss 1 reinserter enforces field byte lengths, pads text, applies fixed-offset edits and writes new game/scenario HDM images. Description mentions both games, but inspected implementation does not establish complete support for Lodoss 2.
Native IOCS-based CRT/LCD test patterns enumerate 15/24/31 kHz modes and color/VRAM layouts. It is a display diagnostic, not a source reconstruction or universal monitor compatibility test.

Generated annotated listing with address-bound notes, explicit indirect entry hints, graphics decoders and openMSX VRAM comparisons. Full 32 KiB explanation/matching and 21 tests are upstream measurements, not independent verification.

Historical Euphoric-associated format tools include BASIC tokenization, assemblers, plotter rendering and disk conversion. This root adds smaller Sedoric-image configuration support. Empty primary README does not mean absent implementation.
Loads tape blocks on the original machine and writes numbered disk files; includes multipart and slow-tape modes. This is distinct from modern WAV decoding.
Disk-based macro assembler supports Z80/Z180/Z280 instruction sets, conditional assembly and REL output suitable for L80/LINK. Source includes explicit relocatable-record generation.
Author-maintained CP/M-like BIOS/BDOS/CCP and native utilities including assembler, BASIC and Forth. Nearly compatible disk directory is not 8080 binary compatibility; programs load at $0200.

Mechanical assembly translator maps instructions and selected BDOS/reboot calls. No macros, incomplete ! line separation and 255-character line limit; manual repair can be necessary. It is not CPU emulation.
Banked disassembly of the unlicensed 9 Fighter NES title, not Capcom arcade Street Fighter III. Build scripts assemble named banks and append graphics/header data.

Collection of game-specific graphics/text/tile decompressors and some compressors. Inspected Ardy Lightfoot source uses a fixed ROM name, fixed offset and small buffers; not an automatic generic SNES format detector.
Native external-clock link receiver prints ASCII/hex bytes via serial and VBlank interrupts. Source warns of a high-volume data bug in its 255-byte queue; not a lossless general serial analyser.
Modified Macro-Assembler AS used by Mega Drive Sonic disassemblies. Includes genuine code generators, not game source itself; historical host portability statements are not current verified builds.

US MK-81019 analysis publishes function maps, provisional names, Ghidra scripts and cross-overlay transfer tools, but no recovered C or game binaries. Zero placeholders is not semantic completeness; thousands of names remain provisional.
Early archive/model inspection and editing for Okami data_pc, including scene viewer and standalone utilities. PlayStation search provenance must not become a claim of PS2 media compatibility.

Matching reconstruction and asset extraction from an owned big-endian ROM, explicitly not a PC port. Code still contains unknown names and partial structure views; a matching build is not semantic completion.
Work-in-progress game reconstruction with named combat routines and data annotations. Human-editable asset conversion and further recovery remain unfinished.

Packs/extracts .neo and MAME/Darksoft layouts, edits header metadata, handles C interleaving and optional P-bank half swap. Auto-detection is a reset-vector plausibility heuristic, not proof for every hack or unusual image.
Converts palette, CHR and raw nametable data into PC Engine assembly, with an example display program. RLE nametables are unsupported and palette mapping is manually adjustable.

Reconstructs missing pieces around original FFLSRC.ZIP and modernizes build tooling. Retail versus modified/no-trailer outputs are separate; retail identity includes trailer bytes and regenerated security prefix.

Image conversion covers CEL/IMAG/LRFORM, palettes and selected NFS containers. No dithering, incomplete CEL option combinations and directional format limits remain. ANIM output and NFS wwww writing are TODOs despite broad introductory wording.

EU YKGP ARM9/overlay reconstruction reports all 306 modules matching, while distinguishing C, library assembly and two CLZ exceptions. Matching modules are not a playable rebuilt ROM; naming/structure consolidation remains ongoing and reported counters have different denominators.

Extracts ARM7/ARM9/overlay memory sections and generates XML analysis projects with optional symbols/I/O labels. Optional BSS filling creates modeled placeholder bytes, not recovered original initialized data.

Narrow scripts extract the Snail Maze path from a particular 8 KiB v1.3 BIOS and inject an export-cartridge header. Hardcoded layout/checksum assumptions are not a general arbitrary-ROM repair service.
Historical Gemini 2 source snapshot recovered from an old Atari TT, including native TOS/GEM support code. Preservation of a snapshot does not establish a clean modern build or completeness.

Browser parser handles PICT resource/file framing, PackBits and selected drawing records. Inspected implementation contains unfinished/debugging notes; do not infer complete QuickDraw opcode fidelity from picture extraction.
Provides resource-fork and Finder-info access across native named forks, extended attributes and Windows AFP streams. Despite the name, it is not an Apple Filing Protocol network server.
Portable 6502-family assembler with BBC BASIC-like directives, loops and expressions; writes assembled files directly into DFS SSD/DSD images and can create boot entries.

Reusable Mode 7 routines and small standalone examples, plus translated examples from Discovering BBC Micro Machine Code. This is an educational code library, not a fork or alternative implementation of the BeebAsm assembler.

Inspected root is chiefly Workbench icon/theme assets and bundled utilities, with small icon-generation command workflows. No distinct reversing/restoration implementation established; do not misclassify packaged binaries as available utility source.
An early read/echo loop and string helpers are present, but lexer and parser return immediately. Retain the project lead without advertising a functioning Lisp interpreter.

Detailed format notes with unknown fields, but no parser implementation, named game/version verification or validation corpus established. Retain as a format-research source rather than a working general PSP model toolkit.
Editing mode integrates m68k-lsp, an opt-in cycle counter and experimental uae-dap. Cycle-count overlays are manually refreshed; broader retro-platform support is a plan, not a verified feature.

Small native MiniGL interface-hooking experiment logs selected context calls and restores hooks after a timed interval. Sparse repository description must not be interpreted as a full source-level debugger.
Native ACE-based homebrew with gameplay, collision, entities, UI and packed converted assets; also offers an SDL host build. Source is C11, with 68000 code and AGA features off.

Proof-of-concept Rust/Swift/Zig native alert programs for TOS and classic Mac. Inline trap glue and packaging are implemented, but runtime/standard-library facilities are deliberately absent. Complete hello-world demonstrations are not production-ready full toolchains.
Avalonia adaptation shares tracker/DAW code, emulated playback and a native SID exporter. Retro sound bank is still incomplete; MP3/FLAC export remains Windows-only while WAV is cross-platform.
Reconstructs three SwinSID firmware variants including the Lazy Jones fix and an unreleased variant with reported glitches. This is AVR SID-replacement firmware, not C64-executed 6510 game code.

Integrated emulator, assembly/BASIC development and code discovery. V2 targets VS2019 rather than inheriting V1 VS2017 compatibility; Next support and some BASIC-debugging capabilities remain incomplete.
Table/bitfield instruction decoder emits addresses, instruction bytes and mnemonics including indexed forms. It is a listing tool, not a complete interactive code/data recovery framework.

Single substantive script inspects AMSDOS headers and combines inputs into banked RIFF/AMS! CPR output. Missing README does not mean no implementation, but plural repository name is not evidence of a larger suite.

Converts music into replay formats and compares executable sizes including buffers, boilerplate and generated code. General execution-duration collection is future work; only limited FAP timing is automatic.

Alternate Pico/A2VGA firmware emulates the Apple II Mouse Interface Card protocol for USB HID mice instead of VGA output. Source documents 6502/6805 PIA handshaking; current implementation runs on Pico, not either original CPU.

ca65 include supplies documented Monitor/Applesoft entry points, soft switches and zero-page names, with optional namespaces. It is a reference/header library, not reconstructed firmware executable code.
Compiles/decompiles MUGEN FNT containers into graphics and text metadata, with explicit format/error handling. Decompile here means font-container extraction, not machine-code recovery.
Translation workflow includes text/pointer reinsertion, halfwidth-font patches and image tools. The reported 369/369 strings are translation coverage, not full game-code reconstruction.

MCP bridge controls openMSX execution, media, memory/VDP, input and snapshots with shared stdio/HTTP capabilities and documentation retrieval. It orchestrates an existing emulator rather than reimplementing MSX hardware.
Reads/writes physical media through Catweasel MK1/MK3/MK4 and converts DMK/JV1/JV3. FM/MFM/RX02 formats extend beyond TRS-80; independent image converters do not require controller hardware.
Writes images from Ultimate media to physical 1571/1581-class drives using C128 fast serial. Empty sectors are skipped and device/image mismatches are not checked.
ATASM source utilities configure and exercise the Atari 1050 Disk Duplicator upgrade, including SIO commands and firmware vectors. Not the drive firmware itself or a generic Atari disk imager.

Game-specific N88 BASIC decryption/encryption and extraction/insertion. Source annotates original Z80 operations; bank/address arguments and embedded keys are format-specific, not general cryptographic recovery.

Replacement objcopy-style helper assembles banked cartridge images from SDCC linker/map output. Bank naming, segment maps and finite image buffers are explicit assumptions, not an independent complete C compiler.
Converts ZX81 P and ZX80 O images into TZX generalized-data blocks. TZX output does not make the input a ZX Spectrum program.
Native callable module compiles packed 16-color sprite data into drawing instructions, using color zero as transparency and compact LEAX skip sequences. It trades greater code size for speed.
Early Go-oriented NES compiler emits ca65 assembly and includes emulator and Game Genie tools. Source-level host debugging and native NES output are distinct workflows.

Pre-decompresses graphics and patches chip-arming sites to build 96 Mbit SFA2/Zero2 ROMs without S-DD1. Preserves side-effecting dummy stores and uses pinned hardware models; this is modified game output, not byte-identical retail ROM reconstruction.
Publishes named function maps, review records, RNC2 unpacking and screen conversion tools, but no reconstructed C or game executable. Naming all 391 functions does not prove every semantic claim.

Creates hardware texture layouts including palettes, VQ compression, mipmaps and previews. Mipmaps must be square; stride mode excludes compression/twiddling/mipmaps and cannot be used for bump/paletted data.
MPB/MDB, MLT, OSB and FOB inspection/editing with per-format support. MSB sequences are extractable but not writable; FPB DSP programs remain insufficiently understood.

In-progress original-platform reconstruction with separate executable/overlay matching. Explicitly not a PC port or port-ready codebase; naming, typed data, documentation and shiftability remain separate work after code matching.

Literal instruction-to-C translation uses function symbols, overlays and relocation metadata; delay slots and indirect calls require runtime support. Generated C is not manually recovered high-level game logic.
Coherent GoldenEye suite contains setup/stan conversion, Gebug64 tooling, C audio utilities and a browser map viewer. It is not a completed full game decompilation.
Extends Super System Card 3.0 EX_GETFNT with 8x12/8x16 ASCII modes, preserving old SJIS modes. Games must explicitly detect/use the extension; this does not translate every game automatically.
Macro assembler includes native Jaguar GPU/DSP instruction encoding and Lynx support. Include search uses BLL_ROOT versus BJL_ROOT for different targets.
Enhanced continuation of original 3DO Doom sources with renderer and build/disc workflow changes. It is not a fresh disassembly or a promised byte-identical retail build.
Open implementation of startup code, BIOS/OS wrappers and color extensions. Generated wrapper source issues real interrupt-based calls; it is not a replacement WonderSwan game emulator.
Parses PAC instructions, parameters and code structures for Patapon analysis. Despite the name, it does not emit high-level source, assemble PAC or emit IR; interface work remains incomplete.

Substantive loaders/decoder/annotation tools accompany Claude commands: Mac resource and ROM formats, TOS PRG relocations, vectors, table recovery and vasm output. Skill packaging alone neither proves nor disproves implemented functionality.

PHP website source for a book/magazine catalogue, not an Oric programming library or native software reconstruction. Useful research source, but do not promote the catalogue backend as a retro runtime library.

Inspected tree contains only a short README announcing a WIP. No recovered source, build or analysis artifact is present at this revision; retain as a lead rather than claim a source-bearing decompilation.
Jaguar is a FreeEMS automotive PCB; assembly means hardware construction. It is unrelated to Atari Jaguar software or an assembler.
MSX means EPANET multi-species water-quality modelling, not the MSX home computer. Python implementation and README establish this false platform match.

Already tracked as flicky-mega-drive-source-reconstruction under oranguthang/flicky_src. Old API URL returns Moved Permanently to repository ID 788148376, which matches RetrolariumLab/flicky_src. Preserve renamed-owner lineage; do not create a second reconstruction entry.

Interactive historical essay backed by an implemented tokenizer, interpreter and browser environment. Recreates a small BASIC programming experience rather than the complete C64 ROM or cycle-accurate machine.

Integrated SDCC, binary utilities, image creation and C firmware wrappers. Reviewed CRTC helper explicitly excludes 32 KiB overscan and screens above 256 lines; broad toolchain support does not remove per-routine limits.
Creates CDT/TZX images from host files, including block and headerless methods. This continuation adds macOS build compatibility and output changes.

C implementation derived from BBC Micro Lisp with function compilation, persistence and X11 turtle graphics. This is a modern-host descendant, not a BBC-native compiler. README warns that strings are not garbage collected.

Guest daemon and host protocol expose remote Apple Events, files, screenshots and native verbs over TCP or serial. Optional MCP is a frontend rather than a requirement for the bridge. ToolServer returns output, while MPW Shell fallback replies empty.

Implemented ASCII renumbering helper, but source contradicts universal preservation claims: it splits on colons before masking strings, and its ON branch emits literal ON ... instead of the original selector. GOTO rewriting also precedes ON-list rewriting. Not safe as an arbitrary-dialect source transformation.
ROM reconstruction has xa assembly, substantial byte tables and da65 code/data/label configuration. A byte-preserving representation is not equivalent to fully interpreted assembler internals.
ImGui/SDL editor includes screenshot extraction, configurable assembler output, masked sprites, animation and tiled views. Explicit beta with possible missing functionality.
Haskell tool implements iNES/ZIP loading, memory maps, instruction parsing, slices and pseudo-code presentation with a terminal UI. Not a general completed NES-to-C game decompiler.
Coherent collection converts tiles, Echo music/instruments, PCM, VGM and compressed data, and generates/fixes ROM headers. MIDI-to-Echo conversion is explicitly preliminary.
Implements SSP160x instruction assembly and SVP ROM manipulation alongside research hardware designs. Scope is Virtua Racing cartridge coprocessor, not Mega Drive 68000 instruction assembly.

Compares recorded audio signatures and plots differences to help inspect hardware, emulators and modifications. Signal-generation setup and host analysis are separate stages; this is not a source-code decompiler.

Annotated cartridge listing names tape, keyboard, screen, audio and buffer variables with access references and build files. Search matched Master Cartridge but this is Atari educational software, not Sega Master System.

Game routines reconstructed in C retain a 64 KiB address-indexed memory array and GBA rendering adaptations. Explicit serial and interrupt stubs remain; this is not a completed original-Game-Boy matching build or a general CPU interpreter.
Editors and format knowledge for six AKI wrestling games, including costumes, archives and models. Incomplete tooling and documentation, not a full game reconstruction.
Console library, PC browser/relay, master server and examples enable homebrew networking through flashcart USB. Requires a tethered computer; does not add standalone onboard network hardware.

Function maps, naming reviews and rail/movement/enemy studies cover Saturn and two Windows executables. No decompiled C or runnable game is published; provisional names remain and movement notes explicitly identify misnamed enemy code.
Extracts fixed-layout Latin, Japanese and Sega-specific glyph sets with documented code-point mapping and font IDs. Not a full boot ROM reconstruction or a font repacker.

Upstream reports executable, two overlays and 446 packages matching. Preserve listed handwritten/inline assembly, register pins, assembler/linker-layout patches and unresolved semantic naming/types. A matching build is not a clean portable C-only port.

WIP engine reconstruction for NTSC-U SCUS_971.98 with separate engine, scripting and data progress. Build accepts extracted assembly/data alongside recovered C++; matching does not mean full semantic recovery.
Kernel modules and hardware API documentation aim at open vanilla firmware. README explicitly says far from complete, despite the repository description using complete as a project goal.
Resolves module NIDs from XML databases, creates import/export structures and maps hardware registers. Enriches Ghidra analysis rather than performing complete automatic decompilation.

README headline says ROM rebuilt from C, but detailed progress explicitly separates byte-matched code including assembly from readable-C decompilation. Three-region SHA1 claims are not 100% C recovery.

Compares function/data sections in object files with symbol demangling, rebuild/watch integration and reports. Object matching and metadata-complete flags are not an independently verified complete-game or semantic equivalence measure.
Implemented jdis decodes Tom GPU or Jerry DSP binaries with offsets/base-address options. Assemblers, optimizers and hazard generators are possible future uses of its core, not shipped tools.

SDX2 and ADP4 encoding/decoding with Portfolio stereo layout. FFmpeg container handling does not establish identical ADP4 decoding; README documents differing decoder interpretation and raw-input requirements.
Converts MOD music and four-colour tile graphics, plus ROM checksum writing. Rust rewrite is explicitly unfinished; checksum generation performs no real ROM validation and overwrites input.
Studies driver 2.11a and parses music banks into structured sequence listings, with FASM regeneration macros. Address-prefixed diagnostic listings explicitly cannot be recompiled.

GPL cartridge control-flow traversal patches a hardcoded relocation range. CALL payload knowledge must be edited for each game; assumes calls return and clear condition bits, which author says is not always true. Not a safe universal relocator.

Tk/Pillow editor emits low-resolution monochrome BASIC and TIM output. Generated BASIC packs strings and removes its construction statements on first run; this is intentional output behaviour, not ordinary static image data.

Extracts/rebuilds resources, edits text/fonts/graphics and decompiles script bytecode for SCUMM v5-v8 and HE with per-feature limits. Font and video encoding support is not uniform across every version.

Reimplementation derived from disassembled original AGI with C logic execution and SDL2 platform code. Reads PC v2/v3 game data; listed Amiga mouse commands and early sprite quirks are outstanding ideas, not implemented compatibility.

Text-only engine identifies tables by patterns in Spectrum SNA snapshots. Supports a bounded set of later Adventure International games; no graphics, some missing commands and imperfect Kayleth table extraction.

X68 project decodes opcodes/effective addresses and prints mnemonic listings through TRAP15 console services. Name says decompiler, but inspected implementation is a disassembler, not high-level C recovery.

Relevant emulator disassembly archive with three 35 MB listings, not SNES game code. README and tree verified, but source retrieval returned empty content for an oversized file. Preserve a follow-up for bounded listing inspection; this is an access/inspection limit, not evidence that the implementation is absent.
CPM is the CMake package manager here, not the CP/M operating system. Three-file wrapper retrieves general x86 udis86 and has no demonstrated specific retro-platform analysis contribution.
Source-backed tests cover socket lifecycle, I/O, DNS, descriptor transfer and benchmarks. Loopback and host-assisted network tiers differ; skipped privileged operations are not passes.

Implements partition layouts, FFS/OFS/PFS3/FAT32 file operations, floppies, LHA and artwork decoding. Filesystem mounting includes allocator bitmap repair bookkeeping; inspection should not be presumed side-effect-free without checking device/write/flush mode.

GadTools partition/format utility with device-liveness classification and fail-safe treatment when boot device is unknown. RDB handling derives from amitools; existing host tests compare layout output, not every live disk operation.
Source examples progress from TOS programs and console input to A-Line graphics. Demonstration collection, not reconstructed commercial games or a full SDK.
Editor has phrase/chain/song management, keyboard interaction and player components. Low hand travel is a design goal; fast playback and low RAM use are explicitly not current goals.
Java BASIC runtime and cross-compiler with 6502 assembler/emulator and script-language backends. BASIC is parsed into host objects rather than residing as original tokenized code in emulated RAM.

Assembles and decompiles Fuxoft music language, including loops/calls and per-voice state. Decompilation is explicitly not universally round-trippable; some historical tracks are invalid yet happened to play.

Web/desktop quantization, dithering and exports for classic CPC and Plus, including per-line palettes and tilesets. Mode pen-budget code constrains reserved/transparency pens; 4096 available colours does not mean4096 simultaneous pens.
Native tests exercise lower or upper16KiB under several display modes, looping until error or BREAK. Targets mode-dependent RAM symptoms, not proof of all possible hardware faults.
Single extensionless source file embeds assembler in BBC BASIC and installs OSWORD E0 transfer handling. Includes Tube claiming, parameter layout and presence/unload operations.
USB CDC firmware and hardware design implement block reads/writes for ROM/EEPROM devices. Apple II is the ROM context; firmware executes on ATmega32U4, not6502.
Source implements CFG/SSA/C-generation experiments with a udis86 wrapper. Author explicitly calls it broken/incomplete toy work, not a working arbitrary-DOS porting pipeline.
Continuation of released Compass source with editor, monitor and debugger, assembled via Nestor80. Source-supported improvements are distinct from original authorship.
Scans standard MFM_DISK sector ID/data marks and rewrites incorrect CRCs. Assumes standard byte-aligned layout; not general flux recovery or deliberate copy-protection preservation.
Converts POKEY dumps into transcription-oriented MIDI, not SAP files directly. Slides become retriggered notes; noise/high-pass effects are unhandled, so this is not a faithful sound renderer.
Integrated8KiB monitor/assembler source with BASIC-facing facilities and cartridge/PRG packaging. Real implementation despite absent root README.
Native Small-C compiler with cross-target runtimes. Explicit restricted subset: no structs/unions/floats/typedef/casts, single-level pointers and one-dimensional arrays. Not a full ANSI C compiler.
Library handles resampling/filtering and BRR samples for SNES audio. Separate GUI is linked but not included as a claimed library feature.
Palette browsing/editing supports whole ROMs and split data, with binary/assembly-related UI. Data tool, not game decompilation.
Implements palette/tile/ROM data editing, but README warns of source-data corruption and unfinished compression writing, text editing and attribute rendering. Not a safe complete editor.
Estimates usage from map/NOI/IHX/CDB files or ROMs, with overlaps, manual areas and bank templates. SMS/Game Gear rules are GBDK-specific, not arbitrary-ROM structure recovery.
Translation source includes script, art, font codecs and patch-building tools. Modifies original ROM rather than reconstructing the entire original game.
V2 converts MIDI, textual MUS and binary COM/ASEQ/M64 music language with commands/loops and control flow. It no longer loads whole ROMs; legacyV1.5 serves that workflow.
Edits object placement, carrier motion, gravity and level metadata, with collision display and OBJ export. USA1.0/1.1 supported; European support is future intent.
Converts wave audio to DCA/ADPCM or PCM with mono/stereo and length/rate controls. Defaults can downsample and mix to mono to fit a single AICA channel.
AICA/Yamaha ADPCM to WAV utility with configurable header skip and sample rate. Designed around Magic the Gathering assets; explicitly excludes stereo even where extensions match.
Builds C overlays at configured RAM locations, supports runtime patching via emulator integration and disc/xdelta assembly. It assists mods, not automatic full-game C recovery.

Windows GUI and Python bakers convert user-supplied disc data for a separate PSP engine. Audio path treats PS2 VAG and PC PCM differently and excludes speech/radio/mission banks from the selected bake; not a full playable port itself.
Builds/unpacks DS ROMs from components with ARM7/ARM9, overlay, banner and alignment handling. Packaging is not decompilation of game logic.
Wraps DS binaries/addresses into an ELF template for Ghidra/IDA. DSi modcrypt must already be removed; converter is not a decrypter or recovered source project.
Edits GCM/RARC/BTI/J3D/JPC and compression formats, plus DOL offset inspection. Can create RARC but not new GCM/JPC; BMG scope is currently Wind Waker only.
Source parses MusyX samples, macros and instrument/ADSR structures. Empty root README and template ReadMe.txt do not mean source absent; feature scope is taken conservatively from implementation.
Displays keyboard/mouse/two-joystick input through IOCS for real X68000 or X68000Z mapping checks. Does not establish electrical compatibility of every adapter.
Direct-threaded Forth with cross-assembler/compiler sources and fast-RAM primitives. Library is not fully vetted; author warns some ITC-derived assumptions can crash DTC code.
Formats, lists, copies and removes files in161280-byte35-track linear disk images. No fsck/repair capability yet; not arbitrary CoCo/OS-9 filesystem coverage.
Host tools list/copy/remove/format/check CP/M images, with optional libdsk and filesystem definitions. This is genuinely CP/M support, unlike same-acronym CMake wrappers.

Metadata-guided ROM disassembly/reassembly, fingerprint label transfer, comparisons, DMD decoding and checksum tools target WPC/WPC-S/WPC95. Heuristic tables and matches remain hypotheses; roundtrip is a build check, not semantic completeness.
Implements instruction, SSA, block and code-generation modules with explicit origin/entry/MMIO inputs. Not a complete automatic game-port generator or proof of recoverable indirect control flow.

Already tracked as retrokit-le-lx-ghidra-toolkit under nemo22/retrokit. Old API redirects to repository1418067423, identical to the selected new owner. Preserve renamed-owner identity instead of creating another project.
PC Engines is the APU network-appliance vendor here, not NEC PC Engine. Script downloads/flashes modern appliance firmware and reboots; not retro console tooling.

Implementation is a bulk downloader/launcher setup for prepatched game libraries and emulators, not a translation patch authoring tool or source reconstruction. No independent reverse-engineering or format implementation established in inspected scripts.

Description proposes a WonderSwan C compiler, but inspected README/Makefile/compiler driver document inherited BCC/ELKS/PC8086 targets. Retain lead until WonderSwan-specific ABI/runtime/ROM output is evidenced; do not label a complete target toolchain from the repository name.
Scripts bridge Linux/WSL builds to host Windows WinAPE, loading disk images and NOI symbols on changes. Not a new CPC emulator or game engine.
New game code recovers original BASIC rules and formulas while replacing wording/art. Seeded Python RNG and formula tests do not prove identical original random sequences.
Partial initialization recovery with STRONG.DAT extraction/reassembly tooling and Borland overlay normalization. Palette/RLE and most game-code recovery remain unfinished.

C17/SDL3 engine recovers game rules and raw record widths; widescreen expands visibility checks and modern options intentionally change presentation. OPL/speaker emulation is an audio component, not a generic guest CPU game wrapper.
Banked assembly and memory/script maps from DiztinGUIsh. Code converted to assembly is not fully understood: README marks large semantic gaps and explicitly excludes audio disassembly.
Partial disassembly and edited assets support multiple translations. English completion does not imply all language variants complete; current source defaults select Latin Spanish and enable debug.
Source port includes enemy/gameplay logic and banked assets, but README records stage/boss routines removed to make a build succeed. Not a confirmed complete playable game.

Sequencer-level PSG core with variant data and clocked write behaviour. Upstream compares attenuation streams with pinned Nuked-PSG, but this is not blanket electrical or analog audio equivalence for every chip.
Print-routine analysis, extraction tools and SQLite script workflow support game1 translation. Repository title includes1&2, but game2 notes are future work.
Translation texts, character encoding notes and C text-formatting tool accompany the patch. Hardware/full-playthrough success is reported upstream, not independently verified here.
Graphics extraction/reinsertion uses ASCII-art representations to preserve palettes, with separate shop text patches and test saves. Translation largely concerns visual text, not only strings.
First pass covers functions but names, raw pointers and RAM semantics still need improvement. Matching output is the restoration gate, not a claim of complete understanding.
Partial USA disassembly includes typed compression-state names and documented mixed raw/RLE/reference encoding. Base ROM still required; generated matching output is not all source recovery.
Banked assembly, graphics tables and hardware/memory definitions exist despite minimal README. Many address-derived names remain; no completion percentage inferred.
16-in-1 menu source covers headers, interrupts, graphics and bank/menu handling. Scope is cartridge menu, not the games contained on a multicart.
Translation pipeline includes font/script resources, ROM preparation and insertion tools. A patched game is not an original byte-identical reconstruction.
Small focused patch replaces the single Japanese options screen with custom drawing code and compressed art. Rest of UI already English; do not inflate into whole-game text recovery.
Configurable splitter integrates spimdisasm/Rabbitizer and emits rebuild inputs. Symbols, section boundaries and analysis options require evidence; it is not automatic high-level C recovery.
Matching original-target reconstruction with region-specific code/data progress and recovered scheduler/audio structures. Not a PC port; original asset extraction remains required.
Source tree mixes recovered game code, included assembly stubs and original-library source. Library volume alone must not count as recovered game logic.
Source explicitly remains non-shiftable and contains many GLOBAL_ASM stubs beside C functions. Byte-matching target is not readiness for arbitrary modifications.
Guide includes a substantive script generating Ghidra function-ID databases from user SDK libraries. Goes beyond a link list, but is not a game decompilation or shipped SDK database.

CORE.GT4 engine matching is separate from Adhoc game scripts. README distinguishes matched functions, linked C/code bytes, tiny reconstructed-data fraction and a lexical clean-source metric; full build retains original assembly for gaps.
PAL2.00 reconstruction links recovered functions at original addresses and fills gaps from local disassembly. Readability refinement and future PC reimplementation remain separate work.

Stripped boot executable and overlays have recovered functions and layout metadata. Inspected near-match C is explicitly excluded from matching build and replaced by assembly; readable research code is not automatically linked code.

USA ADGE reconstruction reports auto-matched raw output and donor-reused functions separately. Inspected .c donor files contain asm bodies, so C extension and matched-count metrics do not establish idiomatic C recovery.
WIP uses donor symbols and animation C matching. README percentages count named symbols, not compiled-C completion; most code remains generated assembly.
Historical game source, editor tools and some artwork are archived together. The3DOCompany is publisher, not the3DO console target; original copyright notices remain.
CVBasic/assembly port preserves the source game loop while adapting audio, banking and input. Custom emulator supplies estimated timing, not independent hardware cycle proof.
Original-style line-numbered dungeon/inn/training BASIC and level files, including1979copyright/revision header. No README does not mean absent source.
Single-unit repair documents boot/NAND/FTL findings and includes bounded read-only digest tools. Working cold boot does not establish every NAND cell healthy or all historical data recovered.
Two-pass assembler supports labels/directives and emits address/code JSON for a separate emulator. The .6809 extension is text JSON, not a standard executable or raw ROM.

Inspected tree has empty game and engine files, a small script interpreter and a tiny assembly handler. No working Amiga game/engine implementation established; retain as a lead rather than promote the advertised game.

Repository title promises all Mega Drive games but README narrows to incomplete Game Genie work; tree contains README and GameGenie.bin only. No inspectable source or disassembly established at this revision.
Already tracked as solomons-key-nes-reconstruction under oranguthang. Old API redirects to repository ID1352704779, identical to the selected root; preserve owner-rename lineage.
Already tracked as castle-excellent-nes-source-reconstruction under oranguthang. Old API redirects to repository ID1352704427, identical to the selected root; do not duplicate for owner rename.

Retain for architecture audit, not promotion in this pass: playable component is explicitly EarthBound-only SNES emulation, while native Nim reimplementation is future work. There is genuine region-level assembly reconstruction, which must be separated from game-specific emulation before inclusion under the existing scope rule.

Architecture-audit backlog: game-specific ARM static recompilation plus DS hardware runtime, not recovered high-level game source. Current claim reaches opening credits/START only; no finished native port. Keep separate from ordinary matching decompilation and do not promote before scope review.

PC-98 disk-image and executable analysis toolkit with Rust image modules and Python Capstone 16-bit x86 decoder. README decompilation and porting goals are not proof of a complete automatic port pipeline. V30 extension coverage is not independently validated.
Character-table and shifted-symbol decoding research. Source implements bytes-to-text but text-to-bytes is a pass stub; this is not a completed translation patch.
Translation repository with a C script extractor, fixed ROM table offsets and Japanese symbol mappings. Do not infer a complete playable translation from the repository name.
Matching game C and separate SDK-based host client. Inspected C defines recovered game/media structures; original PsyQ libraries are linked separately, not counted as newly decompiled game logic.

Matching and reconstruction tracks coexist. Inspected aiinit.c is INCLUDE_ASM wrappers, not recovered C bodies; README percentages are dated author reports, not a current semantic completeness measure.
In-progress US-release decompilation with build/extract scripts. Inspected player.c retains INCLUDE_ASM bodies. README explicitly says code is not yet shiftable.

US ROM reconstruction; inspected entry C creates native libultra threads. Setup generates assembly for nonmatched functions, so buildability does not establish complete C recovery.

Browser-local IPS/BPS patch engine and WonderSwan translation catalogue. Inspected parser handles patch headers, buffer growth and bounds. CERTIFIED and PRACTICAL are project-defined verification labels, not independent tracker certification.

Assembler-buildable cartridge and QUEST/PENNIES reconstruction plus bounded Python behavioral examples. GPL is interpreted game code; do not mislabel this as native TMS9900 instruction reconstruction. Source sample provides mapped variables and structured GPL representation.
Julius1.8.0 port maintained as patches and RISC OS packaging. Inspected patch implements desktop logging, filename treatment, platform sources and frame yielding.

Reads native font descriptor/content files, exports JSON and converts to TTF/OTF/UFO. Inspected big-endian FontStreamer decodes bitmap rows and pointers. Host-side font work, not an Amiga execution CPU requirement.
Native bootblock and launcher source by Ross preserved by earok. Closes CLI/Workbench and reclaims Chip RAM for floppy-launched programs. Inspected assembly uses Exec/DOS/Intuition services.
Preserved GadToolsBoxv3 source for native GUI/resource creation and C code generation. Inspected C generator includes native Amiga APIs and emits windows, gadgets and locale assets.

Standard/extended DSK inspection, MGT/SAM handling, BASIC/screen viewers and copy-protection identification. Inspected Pascal packed records implement disk and track structures; media CPU is not a host CPU constraint.

Historical CPC cross-development container and examples. Dockerfile installs build tools and cpclib. README explicitly recommends rust.cpclib instead; retain as a historical bundle, not the current recommended workflow.

GAC sample adventure reimplemented in C on a BBC Master and refactored on A5000. Inspected extensionless C/gCode contains gameplay/counter/inventory interface. Do not infer6502 execution from BBC branding when Norcroft C environment is unspecified.
Terry Kyriacopoulos DOS3.3 image utilities maintained by Cats Eye, with explicit ANSI-C Unix/MS-DOS portability changes. Historical fork attribution preserved; one tool suite record.

Python CF-image partition inspection/extraction/assembly for MicroDrive/Turbo. Inspected source embeds6502 boot bytes; that is image content, not Python host CPU. Distinguishes HFS detection from assumed ProDOS on other partitions.
Go resource-fork parser with big-endian resource-map decoding and typed resource extraction. Not a native68k application merely because inputs are Macintosh files.

Standalone standard-C++ resource abstractions and Mac/Palm format classes. Explicitly work in progress; sample map implementation initializes fields and must not be treated as proof all resource operations are finished.
Native Z80 diagnostics for display modes, sprites, keyboard, joystick and PSG. Inspected source selects ROM/COM/CAS/BASIC output formats and BIOS calls.

Native CPU-frequency and mixed read/write memory benchmarks with opcode-based CPU detection. Inspected SDCC naked Z280 probe; Z280 detection marked experimental. Timing is VDP-interrupt-based and approximate, not a universal CPU-clock oracle.
PNG-to-Screen2 sprites, tiles and SCR converters used for Night Knight. Supports16x16 sprite decomposition and256tile limit; output C/assembly is data, not a CPU-bound program.
Native IPv4 UDP SNTP client for ESP/X libnetwork sockets and Human68k RTC setting. C implementation avoids floating point and64-bit assumptions; README documents legacy socket-API quirks.
Native DaynaPORT network-adapter driver tooling for BlueSCSIV2 on X68000; inspected SCSI C implementation. Separate from BlueSCSI firmware and hardware.
Partial sound-bank disassembly and compression/tile research. Dynamic-programming RLE encoder and in-budget reskin scripts are implemented; not a full game-source reconstruction.
On-machine assembler/editor/linker with instruction timing analysis. Inspected opcode cycle tables support the documented Z80 assembler rather than merely example binaries.
Ruby macro-assembler DSL with labels, relocation/debug metadata, TAP output and Spectrum BASIC helpers. Ruby host requirements separate from generated Z80 code.
Annotated historical assembler/editor/monitor reconstruction with installer and relocation/configuration tables. Inspected source documents interleaved code/data and relocation design.
GitHub identifies this as a fork of blondie7575/ChoplifterReverse; inspected README retains Quinn Dunki attribution and the same ProDOS-loader scope. No distinct project scope established.

BAKED EMULATION architecture audit: generated C retains6809 registers, condition codes, memory access and cycle accounting atop board-chip models, with a separate interpreter twin. BAKED EMULATION: generated C retains68000 registers, condition flags, memory-mapped STE hardware and dynamic resume dispatch. No interpreter is not equivalent to recovered high-level native game logic. Hold for architecture/scope audit.

Platform/provenance conflict: README calls this cancelled3DO UMK3 source, but inspected SYSTEM.H defines SONY_PSX and background C describes Mortal KombatIII Sony paths. Source archive exists; do not promote a3DO port without resolving identity and lineage.

Empty root README and inspected Rails model/controller provide repository CRUD scaffolding. A working Macintosh resource parser or useful recovery workflow was not established; retain a lead rather than advertise an implemented format tool.

Amiga-derived C port with semantic ball/physics structures and platform shims. Shared C builds SDL hosts and native AGA; hardware emulation shims alone do not establish BAKED EMULATION. No whole-project architecture certification from one sample.
lwIP-based native stack with AmiTCP-compatible bsdsocket API, SANA-II integration and client/server tools. Inspected front end uses per-opener library state and core-task messages.

Author-preserved1993 Ghost-virus removal tool and replacement Degas-picture bootsector. Source documents XBRA self-detection and BIOS disk-change hooks. Catalogued as historical software, not executed or recommended for current security.
Source collection of independent PMMU, memory-protection, SCSI/XHDI and resource utilities. Inspected NF_SCSI provides native SCSI driver interfaces for Hatari/ARAnyM.
Typed6502/6510 assembler/disassembler and CPU emulator with pluggable64KiB bus. CPU implementation credits Jacob Paul O2 ancestry; general-purpose CPU tooling is not game-specific baked execution.

DFS/ADFS/UEF format readers/writers and conversion utilities. Inspected py2/ADFSlib.py contains little-endian parsing and historical Python2 syntax. A guessed py3path was absent; actualtree path used.
Acorn Replay multimedia demuxer and SDL-player research. Inspected parser checks ARMovie header and extracts dimensions/compression fields. Several optional fields remain TODO; no root README exists.
Converts cassette UEF data to cartridge/sideways ROM images with generated6502 loader code, persistent ROM pointer, tape-call interception and bank handling.
Turbo Basic1.0/1.1 template/dispatch decoder, typedIR and BASIC emitter. Original compiler used as an oracle, not a runtime dependency. Parked July29 with incomplete wild-corpus coverage.
English translation patch sources with free-space allocation, text/graphics handling and a separately described Chapter4 protection fix.

Fan translation source with extraction/injection, event analysis and BZH decompression. Inspected bitstream decoder implements literal/backreference paths. SparseREADME does not establish finished translation or gameplay coverage.

ePC-8801MA Common Source Project port replacing Windows-specific integration with SDL3. Inspected debugger console keeps symbolic device/memory interfaces. Whole-platform emulator, not BAKED EMULATION game port.

Shift-JIS extraction/injection and script research for X68000 Ray-Gun. Inspected injector backs up and rewrites datafiles. Machine translation/dictionary assistance is disclosed for text; not evidence of AI-authored code.

SDK macros, headers, examples and relocation tooling. Builds at two origins to derive relocatable ORIX binaries; inspected header assembly uses SDK module metadata.

Open-source nativeGBC city-building game with RGBDS source, save variants and hardware documentation. Not an original commercial-game reconstruction.

Analog-board KiCad schematic reverse engineering with a stalled verification task; no software/firmware or direct software-development tool established in this tree. Outside current software tracker scope.

Modern SATURN rhythm-chart/cosmetics editor, not Sega Saturn hardware or software reconstruction. README and Avalonia project identify a name-match false positive, with no legacy-platform link established.

Borland overlay analysis and recovered save formats support a semantic C++ economy remake. Inspected food rules retain original segment references and explicit unresolved arithmetic/banking checks, rather than pretending every rule is finished.
Source-preserving pointer/script translation pipeline, with explicit rendering-layout controls and fail-closed unknown modes. Currently one Alshark profile, not a general PC-88/PC-98 translator.

Electron workspace integrates Z80 decoding, memory/graphics analysis, watchpoints and automation. Inspected decoder bounds repeated prefixes and resolves indexed displacements. AI analysis capability is not evidence of AI authorship.
Annotated banked source and symbolic cutscene/nametable routines, with mostly Russian comments. Separate translation-focused repository, not merely a ROM upload.
Converts YM register recordings into SN76489 VGM with envelope, attenuation and noise adaptation. Target chip clocks/LFSR are configurable; not a CPU transcoder.
Vagrant provisioning for MiNT GCC, EmuTOS and Hatari, with sample C utilities. Supporting development environment, not recovered compiler source.
Browser disk browser plus boot-sector signatures, heuristics and bounded 68000 analysis. Source distinguishes executable checksum, legitimate protectors and infection indicators.

ACSI/serial interface experiments and native ST test programs. Inspected ACSIPACK assembly accesses DMA and GPIP; an ESP32 sample and ST C file are empty, so directory count is not implementation completeness.
E+ new-map/Filecore structures, fragment allocation, BigDir parsing and boot-loader preservation utilities. Current primary use is RISC OS Pi media, not every historical ADFS variant.
RISC OS 3 ROM checksum/size repair, striping and 5th-column extraction/building. Inspected checksum code implements four interleaved CRC accumulators.
ADFS, ArcFS, Spark, ZIP, ISO and sprite conversion preserving RISC OS metadata. Inspected ArcFS reader documents record layout and compression methods.
Line-at-a-time multi-backend assembler and CLI. Inspected 68000 backend handles BASIC token collisions and effective-address parsing. Host integration is distinct from output CPU support.
Small C resource-fork library with AppleSingle/AppleDouble discovery, big-endian headers and map-header verification. Evidence supports these primitives, not comprehensive resource-type decoding.
Parses resource forks using TMPL definitions, adding fork-local custom definitions without globally replacing built-ins. Source implements asynchronous template loading.
LZSA2 plus BCJ compression for on-demand DOS code overlays. Inspected loader allocates paragraphs, decompresses into a far segment and reverses branch transformation.
LZEXE 0.90/0.91/0.91e unpacker reconstructs MZ headers and relocation tables. Source returns a copied input for uncompressed data, so zero-copy wording must not be read as actual output behavior.
Game Boy loader and architecture plugin. Source validates logo/header and maps the first two ROM banks; do not infer full bank-switch analysis from loader support.
Annotated banked assembly with explicit uncertainty in unused reset-vector code and hardware routines.

Matching reconstruction and text tools with semantic state-machine dispatch alongside original-address symbols. Author reports 1130 matching code regions; this does not certify all assets, readability or whole-game runtime.
Reviewed the room-script actor-operation, turn-key, hit-result and intro-sweep symbol recovery; the deploy check succeeded.
wxWidgets/ion-engine content editor with tiles, stamps and map workflows. Experimental SNES tile support does not establish finished SNES exporters.
Translation code/art/script and VWF build pipeline using Kosinski compression and 68k assembly.
CHR conversion and map modification with tile deduplication under flips. Inspected optimizer distinguishes flat/blank tiles and calculates flipped CRCs.
VDP1 drawing and memory-performance probes using Yaul. Actual memory benchmark performs width-specific writes and counts operations; no root README does not mean no implementation.
Function-name map, physics/archive/model studies and RNC tools, not distributed decompiled C. Source explicitly distinguishes symbol naming from a rebuilt executable.
Preserved VB6 image-creation application with maintainer fixes. Inspected event code validates paths and dispatches DiscJuggler/Nero operations, unlike a binary-only download.
IP executable loader and PC-I/O bridge with added Maple passthrough. Inspected target command handlers implement network transfer and execution handoff.
Typed field/model/camera code with PsyQ compiler-version annotations and retained address symbols. Matching project, not a finished native PC port.
Electron/CLI installation manager with published plans and optional AI repository interpretation. It orchestrates external ports; it does not itself decompile all listed games.
Electron/Angular audio preparation for mono 8-bit ProTracker/8SVX output. Current changelog describes JavaScript conversion replacing older SoX dependency.
Sonic Arranger format decoding, replay/conversion and newer tracker UI. Paula channel state models period-latched samples; isolated audio synthesis is not a BAKED EMULATION game-port classification.
Native/Python network transfer and development-deployment clients for M4. Inspected C helper calculates AMSDOS header checksum.
RIFF/AMS CPR maker and bank dumper. Source enforces 16 KiB per bank and at most 32 banks, with explicit raw-output and padding options.
On-machine Spectranet module exposes GDB packets after NMI entry. Inspected server implements checksummed packets and TCP port 1667.
Adaptation of CamelForth/80 with Sega PSG/VDP words and keyboard support. Inspected extensions emit hardware port writes.

Inspected batch orchestration, but actual image conversion depends on bundled executables and proprietary menu ZIPs without corresponding implementation source here. Retain as an audit lead rather than promote a wrapper as recovered tooling.
Amiga SWOS 96/97 analysis combines annotated assembly, generated C and IDA/Ghidra export and repair scripts. Generated decompiler C is not a finished native C port.

Continuation of XenonTranslation/tools includes script extraction/compression and Shift-JIS translation insertion. Author reports story translated and inserted, with main load menu and omake still excluded.

Single-file browser tool implements SCR conversion, BASIC tokenization, TAP/TZX generation, WAV synthesis/decoding and a limited Z80 assembler. Unsupported instruction forms explicitly fail; not a full assembler or hardware-fidelity claim.
Preserved early-1990s native +3/+D/DISCiPLE disk and tape conversion assembly, adapted to z88dk z80asm directives. Actual directory/selection and DOS-call implementation is present.
Native C64 utility transfers D71/D81 images from a 1541 Ultimate 2 to physical drives. Source uses KERNAL channels and block-write commands; C128 burst-mode version is only planned.
Converts compatible C64 disk programs to EasyFlash cartridges using KERNAL load hooks and cartridge banking. Only LOAD-based programs are supported, not arbitrary custom loaders.
Raylib viewer maps C64 disk sectors and BAM usage, with checksum diagnostics for the author’s custom backup logs. Directory analysis and health indicators remain unfinished.

65816 tracing disassembler handles raw/OMF segments, tracks M/X operand widths, names IIgs tool calls with fingerprints and iterates from user-supplied entrypoints. Companion 2mg extracts ProDOS images.
Swift image converter emits Merlin-compatible 4bpp graphics, palette setup and draw code for IIgs memory. RGB channels are reduced to four bits.

Native grep-like utility integrates regex and argument parsing with GS/OS file types, wildcards and recursive search. Implements a bounded regex/option subset rather than complete GNU grep compatibility.

Collection of lightly modified 2CDT/iDSK sources; unique capabilities beyond the tracked tool lineage and mastering workflow not established. Retain for lineage review, not another independent implementation.
Primary repository for the TypeScript CP-1600 emulator, disassembler and MCP debugging server.
Primary repository for CP/M-65, a native CP/M port and development environment for 6502-family retro systems.

Original main, loader and two boot sources have byte-comparison build gates; a separate enhanced path replaces disk routines and boot chain to build an AmigaDOS-format disk. Extracted graphics/music and tools are included. Keep original-byte matching distinct from the deliberately modified enhanced build.

Assembly reconstruction of the original Atari ST engine with transcribed tables, Alcyon C startup/music and relocation reconstruction. Concrete assembly and build scripts are present; not merely a decompilation goal.

Substantive Caprice32 4.1.0 adaptation with joystick-driven virtual keyboard, four-controller/ToTo support, autorun, snapshots and Pi-specific display handling. Includes emulator core and source build files rather than only a packaged binary.
Original 2021 CPC game by Angelos Mavros. The substantial readable BASIC listing contains title flow, character drawing, dialogue and game interaction, accompanied by tape/audio distribution files.
Pico-hosted SC-3000 emulator implements RAM, TMS9918 video, PSG, cartridge/tape handling and keyboard/gamepad input. CMake lists actual machine, Z80, VGA, filesystem and USB implementation units.
Reusable Z80 routines detect keyboard/PPI availability and merge cursor/key rows with joystick inputs; companion startup, interrupt and VDP/PSG templates support native game development.

Defer claimed complete Menace port: README and COMPLETED claims conflict with unfinished original logic; actual game.cpp uses generic timed random enemies and placeholder rendering, while disassembly helper slices guessed disk offsets. Concrete tools exist, but faithful reconstruction and reliable extraction claims are not established. Do not promote completion rhetoric as game restoration.

Readable C reconstruction derived from the separately tracked matching Atari ST assembly. README describes 33 modules, 423 identified functions and differential checking against Musashi. Included at the user's explicit request; preserve core/reconstruction scope rather than call this repository a playable port.

Defer software inclusion: this root provides PCB/enclosure design, documentation and compiled STM32 update/bootloader binaries, but no corresponding firmware source tree. Do not describe hardware manufacturing files plus binaries as a source-backed software implementation.

Repository-level port coordination, pinned upstream recipes and actual AGA/HAM8 support code for m68k AROS/AmigaOS. Do not split every planned port into a claimed delivered game. Root status distinguishes compiled, first-light, testing and release gates.
Native blitter sprite clipping/skew/masking routines with a C demo and PHP generators for palette, sprites and world data. Concrete implementation, not a title-specific completed Power Drift port.

Host-side SNDH diagnostics parses metadata and subtunes, checks termination/bounds and converts Atari text to Unicode; source includes ICE support. Current CLI reads and prints files, not an automatic music repair or playback claim.
Converts indexed 320x200 PNG pictures to Atari ST planar PI1, writes sixteen palette words and zeroed colour-cycle data, and checks a 32066-byte output length.
Converts Atari ST CyberPaint SEQ animations into animated GIF, with COPY/XOR frame composition and compressed/uncompressed word streams. Inspected frame conversion implementation.

MSA track decompression/compression and FAT12 inspection, listing, extraction and insertion with CLI and wxWidgets GUI sources; companion module scanning script. Actual codec and filesystem logic inspected.
Collection of Python/Tk and browser helpers for TOS relocation inspection, graphics/sample conversion and generated tables. Keep scope at root rather than separate records for each small script.

Native display-lag measurement aid synchronizes a screen counter with floppy/user LED transitions for high-frame-rate camera comparison. GFA BASIC listing contains the timing and palette/PSG accesses.
Original BASIC demake of Baba Is You with rule-word parsing, movement, undo and a small level editor. Five tutorial-level maps and concrete game logic are present.
Studio Ghibli-inspired acorn-catching game with one/two-player modes, sprite multiplexing and IRQ-driven music. Native implementation and assets are included.
Assembly side-scroller made for Arok party 2026 with scrolling, sword combat, effects and game assets. Inspected raster interrupt setup and gameplay source.

Halloween-themed C64 game with obstacle entities, sprites, collision logic and joystick/paddle input. Main TRSE source and included obstacle module are substantial, not only images or a binary release.
SID-oriented JSON patch editor, preview/export pipeline and native C64 audition support. Assembly exporter emits seven-byte effect records and separate sweep/vibrato tables for game integration.

Defer canonical-host migration check: GitHub README explicitly says the project moved to Codeberg, where graphics.dat support was added. The GitHub Python dungeon parser and example are concrete, but the destination was inaccessible in this review; retain the canonical source lead rather than silently track an obsolete mirror as current.
Native CPC utility measures floppy rotation speed, searches sector IDs and assists head alignment. Source includes direct FDC routines, firmware numeric operations and a Z80 interrupt timer.

Python pixel-art/editor implementation with CPC firmware/hardware palette mappings and mode-dependent pixel packing for modes 0, 1 and 2. Reviewed image conversion code in addition to the short README.
Command-line batch tape conversion frontend supporting WAV, CDT DRB/CSW and CSW1.1/2.0 outputs, with directory filtering and optional recursion. Actual dispatch to CTape readers/writers inspected.
Windows WPF sprite manipulation tool with CPC mode0/1/2 palette handling and explicit firmware/hardware/RGB colour conversion. Actual palette class and UI project inspected.
Browser-based CPC snapshot-header inspection for Z80 registers, CRTC, gate array, bank mapping and palette, with companion ImHex structures for versions and extension chunks.
Linux workflows assemble DAAD adventure distributions for multiple retro systems and HTML. Inspected CPC script builds DDB/interpreter data, prepares images and inserts outputs into a disk image.
C++ Sega emulator implementation with Z80 and 68000 cores, machine memory maps, VDP/audio components and SDL2 event/render loop. Source selects SG-1000/SMS/GG and Genesis paths.

Python cartridge-image library separates copier-stub detection, Sega header anchors/region/size, checksum, file identity and manifest comparison. Inspected actual header/checksum and dump code, not only coverage statistics.

Excluded at inspected revision: generic React/Vite starter documentation and a single Star Draw heading, with no demonstrated retro-development function. A suggestive repository name is not an implementation.

Native Samurai Shodown-inspired V9990 demonstration with graphics setup, palettes and animation source. The upstream description explicitly says unplayable proof of concept.
Pixel-scrolling platform game with parallax, player/enemy logic, maps and multi-colour sprite presentation. Reviewed actual jump/fall/run game logic.
Falling-block match-three puzzle game with horizontal/vertical/diagonal matches, combos, levels and keyboard/joystick input. Main C source wires title and game loops into MSX BIOS support.
Sixteen-round arcade game with direction/charge input, enemies and exits. Z80 enemy-pattern parsing and spawn control implementation inspected.

BASIC action game moves floors to rescue pigs while avoiding wolves; substantial state, sprite and input routines are included.

PI1 display and PNG conversion with reference-palette reuse and optional contiguous16×16 tile output. Actual palette quantization/linearization implementation inspected.

backlog.description: Continue auditing `jotd666` repositories not yet promoted, especially candidates with missing or template/copied READMEs; require project-specific evidence before adding them.
backlog.notes: Inventoried all 61 public JOTD repositories. Promoted Xevious and Galaxian after project-specific README verification, plus eight distinct Amiga tools, ROM, relocation and slave collections. Copied READMEs were checked against source: Rolling Thunder, Dig Dug, Mr. Do! and Bosconian have distinct Amiga assembly and are catalogued as work in progress, without build or playability claims. Gods Deluxe and Supercars 3 have project-specific remake documentation and were also promoted. The copied Berzerk listing credits Scott Tunstall; catalogued his canonical arcade disassembly and marked JOTD's copy as a duplicate. Tiger Heli and Super Pac-Man still contain mostly copied Amiga templates and need more subject-specific proof; Jungle King has an arcade-only listing, Marble Madness 2 an incomplete loader, and JRPacman500 an ambiguous asset script. Verify current Makefile, startup and selected C implementations; README declares 68000 and ColdFire/ABI variants but no independent build was run. Primary README snapshot: https://github.com/freemint/libcmini/blob/77eb5e1e0129c5dad932e08e50d893cf792a5347/README.md. Reviewed current Makefile, sources/crt0.S and sources/puts.c; promoted libcmini with verified 68000/ColdFire output scope and upstream LGPL provenance. No independent build or runtime test.

backlog.description: Audit the remaining title directories in tony-cruise/colecovision-games-source as separate ColecoVision/Adam projects.
backlog.notes: Root README lists 24 titled directories. Artillery Duel and Montezuma's Revenge were reviewed and promoted separately. For each remaining directory, inspect its own README and assembly header/build directives, preserve title-specific provenance, verify source/target CPU decisions, byte-match claims and explicit AI attribution, and avoid an umbrella record. Reviewed and promoted B.C.'s Quest for Tires, Boulder Dash, BurgerTime, Carnival, Centipede, Choplifter, Defender and Donkey Kong on 2026-10-14. Fourteen title directories remain. Reviewed and promoted Donkey Kong Jr., Frenzy, Gateway to Apshai, H.E.R.O., Mouse Trap, Mr. Do!, Nova Blast, Q*bert’s Qubes, Slither and Smurf Rescue on 2026-10-16. Four directories remain: Space Panic, Squish-em Featuring Sam, Star Wars Arcade and The Heist. Reviewed the final four directories on 2026-10-25 and promoted Space Panic, Squish-em Featuring Sam, Star Wars Arcade and The Heist. All 24 titled directories now have separate title-level reviews.
